The 5 burrito used to be a deal-breaker but since Taquito have jacked their prices up to 7 the place has lost it's appeal. The burrito ingredients are on the poor side, not a smart move when their are better and cheaper alternatives just up the road

Ashamed to say I only checked this place out back in April but have been back numerous times since. Great addition to the Tollcross area, tucked just next to the Cameo Cinema. Amazing flavours, great prices and the guacamole is so fresh and tasty. You've got to give it a try.

Popped into here as wanted something quick and to try something new. The girl behind the counter was lovely and much like the idea of Chipolte - you pick what you would like and then add in the toppings! I opted for a small vegetarian burrito (with rice and beans) and my partner got the beef burrito. The large is enormous, so happy I got the small. The toppings you can add include - jalapenos, cheese, pico de gallo, sour cream, lettuce, guacomle for .50 extra and some hot sauces. I opted for medium and it was spice enough!  We also both asked for everything and were truly wondering if the lovely girl helping us could fold the burrito - as it was rammed full. Amazingly, she managed to wrap it and put it on the grill for a few minutes, they offer a small burrito and a soda for 5, so our meal was 10 for the two of us. It was hard to eat only because it was so massive - it was tasty and fresh - my only gripe being - the toppings weren't evenly spread through so at some stages I have salsa, and at others sour cream. But it tasted nice and was a good deal with good service! Just to note - they only have a table with 6 seats at it for community style eating if you opt to stay in, so best to takeaway as there might not be space. I wish I could give it 3.5 stars, it wasn't exactly the Mexican spices I would expect, but the service was nice and fast and the food fresh and tasty.

Great burrito place for a nice lunch break; this place is more for takeout as there is not much sitting space but the burritos a big, tasty and cheap! Perfect combination; it can get very crowded around lunch hour but never crazy enough that it would have changed my mind; lunch deal involves a small (not that small) burrito and a drink for 5 which i think is a great deal;

Let me clear something up straight away... Taquito is more of a Taco Bell rather than being Edinburgh's answer to Chipotle or Moe's. Now that that's out of the way...   I stopped in here for a quick bite at a cheap price... and that's exactly what I got. For just under 4 I had a decent chicken burrito and a canned fizzy drink. The burrito was good (for Scotland standards). While the chicken and rice were great, it could use some improvement on having more fresh ingredients. For example, I'm pretty sure the jalapenos (chills) were the kind from a jar, which is odd because I think fresh ones are actually cheaper than buying them in the jar. Also, I didn't notice much if any cilantro (coriander), which is one of the things that usually sticks out to me when I have fresh Mexican or southwest food. At any rate, I would by no means be planning to compare it with a burrito you might pick up in Mexico or the USA.   The service had much to be desired, but I must remind you that the window says "Mexican Street Food." Taquito reminds me a lot of a taco truck that might be parked on the side of the street, and with that in mind the service is quite similar. They take your order, eventually ask for your money (which could be a few minutes later), and not really much to say other than that. it's actually a bit confusing when it comes to figuring out where to queue to order and also to wait for your order, so if it's a bit awkward you're not the only one.   There really isn't much seating. It's not the place for planning to sit down and enjoy a meal with friends. The seating suggests exactly what I believe is intended... either you're eating quick and then on your way, or your getting it takeaway. I was on my own and just wanted a quick lunch, so Taquito was perfect.   You may be wondering with my review why I've given it 4 stars. The reason for this is that you can be out the door for less 3.50-4.00 and when I compare that to what I could get elsewhere for the same price, it really can't be beat. Until Chipotle breaks out of London (and cuts their price in half), I'm happy to go to Taquito.

Ordered take-out round #2 from Yak & Yeti. Basically, this place is the best. Some important things to add...  1. They give a 10% discount on the menu if you pick up take-out 2. They give a free bottle of Coke and papadums with take out orders over a certain amount (15 quid I think?) 3. They do free delivery within a 2 mile radius 4. The best: upon request they will do fully VEGAN food options  Add to this their cheerful demeanor and helpful staff and this place is by far they best Indian/Nepalese option in Edinburgh

I still don't really know what the difference is between specifically Nepalese food and regular Indian food...  That's why I'm giving this place 4 stars and not 5. The food itself was extremely tasty (I had the Bengal King Prawns which were marinated in all sorts of spices and then cooked in the tandoori oven, they were gorgeous). But I went there feeling all excited about trying a new 'cuisine' that I'd never had before, and left feeling that there are a lot of Indian restaurants much closer to where I live that serve the vast majrity of the same dishes - almost as if they're just using it as a gimmick.  Aside from that, there really isn't anything you can fault this place on. Despite my whingeing I still picked up a takeaway menu on my way out. Although the food might be very similar to a lot of other restaurants in the area, their prices are definitely the best.

Nepalese food, because of the nature of the country it comes from, is wildly varied - and in some places odd and confusing.  However, this works excellently in favour of the Yak & Yeti restaurant - because for the most part it will be like nothing you have ever eaten before - perfect for when the thought of the same old italian/french/chinese food just doesnt do it for you any more.  A unique cross over of what tastes like thai food and indian food, the Yak & Yeti has an excellent menu, with a range of dishes so interesting I ended up speaking at some length to our friendly waiter (who was knowledgable and patient with me) about what each dish tasted like. When my 'Pokheli Methi Murgh' arrived it was beautifully cooked and delicious (if unpronouncable).  My over all experience of Yak & Yeti was that it was a fresh, new restaurant that succeds in providing something different and tasty for a meal.

I really couldn't fault Yak & Yeti as the food is delicious, the service is friendly and quick and the general ambiance of the place makes you feel relaxed and at home.  I've been here a few times with some friends in my second year of uni and every time we've left stuffed with Nepalese food and content with the whole experience.  The menu has a wide range of meat, poultry and vegetarian dishes, all of wich are authentic to Nepal and have their own unique blend of spices.  The last time I was in I went for the lamb gurkhali khasi which is a traditional dish of the region and tasted amazing.  With boiled rice, a naan bread and drink the whole meal came to tenner which we all throught was great value for money. I'll hopefully come here again soon as its service, food and atmosphere are all faultless.

I had never tasted Nepalese food before I dined at Yak and Yeti and I was not disappointed. I had no idea what Nepalese food was before I went and I'm still not too sure now as a lot of the dishes on the menu were Indian such as Chicken Korma and Vindaloo. I had a fish curry which was gorgeous, it was cooked in lots of spices and was full of flavour. Yak and Yeti's menu offer a wide range of dishes and there is an impressive veggie selection as well.   The food is extremely well priced with starters costing around 3 and main meals around 6, and best of all, they offer a 15% student discount. The decor inside the restaurant is very authentic and modern and the staff were incredibly inviting and charming. Yak and Yeti also serve delicious cocktails and they do takeaways.
Fabulous Nepalese food here! Try the nann! Came back here to try different things, and it is always quite. very cute waitress.

What a surprisingly tasteful and affordable delight of a restaurant. I am thoroughly impressed with the set meals for one person. I ordered a 'thali' plate, and it was so full of so much food, for about 5! Unbelievable. I will definitely go back to this place, it is worth checking out for sure, and it's easy on your wallet. It doesn't taste like you are paying a low price for the food either. The tastes were robust, high quality, and non greasy. They offer these Nepalese dumplings that they can steam for you instead of fry. Highly recommend that dish. I also like their soups, and their friendliness. This is one of my favorite restaurants in Edinburgh.
It's been burnt out at present due to a kitchen fire. No sign of it re-opening at present. Pretty tragic.

We ate here as part of our stay at the Bruntsfield Hotel (you can read my review here: yelp.co.uk/biz/best-west... ) The food here was the absolute height of decadence; to start, I had the shellfish bisque whilst Kris had the chicken liver pate (a favourite starter of his). My bisque was rich and suitably fishy; it wasn't too salty either which is sometimes a danger with a shellfish soup. Perfect! Kris thoroughly loved his pate as well, stating it was one of the best he'd tried. For mains, Kris opted for the Alba Chicken (haggis-stuffed chicken) in a whisky sauce with mustard mash and I chose a pheasant, duck and venison red wine casserole. Kris' chicken was absolutely divine, cooked to perfection and the mustard mash was a delicious touch. My casserole was utterly gorgeous but I will warn you all, it is incredibly rich and it almost killed me; I was so full afterwards I could barely make it back to our hotel room! Sadly I can't remember what I had for pudding; I do remember that I could barely eat it because I was so full from my casserole (my own fault)! I thoroughly enjoyed the meal, despite my own over-indulgence and found the staff to be brilliantly helpful and polite. Whether you happen to be nearby or are staying at the hotel, definitely go to Bisque!

It has been a couple of years since the last time I ate at Bisque (namely because the food was awful) and I'm under the impression that they have since had a bit of a re-vamp in the kitchen.  I would be tempted to give it another go, but there are just so many other good places to eat in the Bruntsfield area.  So, this review is really just about the drinks and ambiance.  Bisque is A-OK.  It's totally fine.  The staff are actually quite nice with a cheeky edge which is great, the drinks are completely fine if maybe a bit on the expensive side, and the ambiance... well it's reasonably beige but it's completely fine.  I hear that this used to be an old man's pub.  I really like old man's pubs.  Sure trendy places are good too, but I think ambiance tends to suffer when a place is neither quaint nor trendy... it just becomes... well as I said, beige.    Bisque is a completely acceptable place to go for a drink Friday after work, but it's not somewhere I would seek out for the fun of it.

Whether you're after a drink, lunch, dinner, cakes, cocktails or teas and coffee you can find them all in Bisque. This is a recent discovery for me and it's definitely becoming one of my favourite watering holes in Edinburgh.   Bisque offers chilled out surroundings, comfy seats and an outdoor seating area too so excellent for those summer nights.   I haven't eaten here... yet, but I've had a shufti at fellow diners plates and the food looks top notch and it's very reasonably priced too.   Overall, an excellent bar/brasserie to while away an afternoon or evening.  Oh and it's worth noting that Bisque offers free Wifi. Hurrah!

Hotel bars/bistros are well within the unknown band of watering holes and hangouts for students, at least they are to me anyway.   Discarding this preconception I found the garden terrace and top notch bar available at the Bisque great for an afternoons chill. The Bistro is apparently mighty fine too with the likes of confit duck and other modern dining fancies.  The garden terrace is worth the visit alone, not bad price wise either.

A cool, lively and chic place to eat and drink in the bruntsfield area of Edinburgh. The interior is very stylish with a contemporary feel. There is a wonderful outside garden terrace to sit and enjoy a drink a meal or a coffee and sandwich. They serve all day food and drink and are open till late. The lunchtime menu offers salad buffets during the week and roast lunches on a weekend. They also have a very nice wine selection and there is also free internet access.
The food is not great here and is overpriced, wouldn't recommend it.

Bisque's best feature is the huge outdoor terrace on which you can enjoy your meal or drinks. The prices are very reasonable and food is served allday. The bar becomes more lively in the evening and is open until late.

What an adorable gem of a place this is. After some futile hunting around for a restaurant, we spotted this place down a wee side street off the Kings Theatre. Got to admit, we didn't go in with high expectations, but goes to show how poor my judgement is!  We shared some vegetable spring rolls to start, then SR had a Pad Prik Kink (with chicken) and I opted for Pla Rad Prik Monkfish, and shared some steamed rice and fried noodles. I will note that the noodles didn't work with the monkfish - steamed rice much better. THe SR loved his chicken, but had major food envy for my prettily arranged asparagus and monkfish. the fish, in a light batter, had a fantastic sauce - intensely sweet, intensely sour, intensely spicy. It was an intoxicating combination, tempered with the blandness of steamed rice.   Prices were reasonable, the staff pleasant enough, it was BYOB but we didn't care and we were delighted, absolutely. A hidden gem, indeed.
Ok, ok, I went back to Absolute Thai and got their Tom Kha soup. It was excellent. Bumping up from 3 stars to 4!

This is a lovely little restaurant off the beaten track. Staff are friendly & the food is delicious - great fresh & spicy flavours! BYOB is a bonus too so you can enjoy with your favourite wine or beer. We can't wait to go back next time.

It's a pity that this restaurant is hidden off the beaten track, because the food here is very tasty and the service is very good.  I have only been to three Thai restaurants but this is by far the best one I have been to and the food has been consistently good on the four times I have been there. I have found a firm favourite dish in the red curry, which always tastes delicious. The restaurant provides good value for money with the servings you get and also offers BYOB, which is an added bonus on the wallet. The decor of the restaurant is pretty simple but this shouldn't take anything away from the fact that this is a hidden gem in Edinburgh.

Was rather disappointed on my last visit here. I ordered Katmandhu Lamb but think i got Katmandhu Mutton as it was tough as old boots. The sauce itself was mediocre. Nan bread cooked to perfection though.  Lamb should be tender and succulent not chewy like rawhide. Sorry. Tried for a 2nd time and this time i got lamb palok. Lamb was tender and succuelnt. Well done. Much better

I SEEM TO BE spending a great deal of time in Indian restaurants of late and it's fair to say that I've been on a good run.  Today was date night, which involved a trip to the cinema to see the new Jason Bourne movie, but we needed to satisfy our hunger beforehand. Morningside Spice seemed like the best option given its close proximity to the Dominion Theatre.  My brother and soon-to-be sister-in-law, Jemma, moved to this part of town a few months ago and have dined at Morningside Spice a couple of times. Given we have enjoyed several meals together at their (and our) previous local, Rivage, I trusted their judgement; I just hoped my Indian odyssey would continue positively.  The dining room was compact but spacious, with tables donning white linen table clothes and staff smartly attired. It was hard to interpret the cross-section of diners at first, which can often be the case during the Edinburgh Festival. On closer inspection (I am a nosey little s*it when I'm out eating), there were a few accents, definite students, and some families on this busy Thursday service.  There were plenty of staff on hand to cope, however, and they were very polite and well-trained on first impression.Worth noting that the restaurant is fully licensened and we enjoyed a famliar friend in the form of a bottle of Baron D'Arignac Cabernet Sauvignon at a reasonable 13.95.  I began with the sheek kebab priced at 4.95, which happens to be a favourite of mine at Rivage. Unfortunately, I found this starter a little underwhelming.  While the lamb mince was tender and moist, it lacked the depth of flavour and seasoning that I had expected. It didn't have the crusty exterior or the barbeque flavour that you get from a tandoor, which meant it was slightly odd in texture.  It also needed a sauce to add a bit of zing as it was pretty one-dimensional beside just a standard salad.  Sarah opened with lamb tikka (4.95), which consisted of skewered meat that fared better on the spice side and benefited from a smoky barbeque note to it. I found certain pieces a little chewy for my liking, which is why I often avoid lamb at Indians until my trust has been gained that it will be executed properly. Again, I felt a sauce of some description would have helped lubricate the plate, especially with some of the meat being rather on the dry side.  I was right in the mood for my favoured garlic chilli chicken, but felt it would be considerate of me to give it a miss in case I was reeking of garlic at the cinema, thereby preventing some unbeknown punter inhaling my vampire-repelling breath.  I had the Kathmandu chicken (8.75) instead and it was a real treat.  I found the heat to my liking, and was thankful that I could taste the garlic, ginger and particularly the fine tinge of cinnamon.  The texture and taste of lentils alongside a generous amount of tender chicken went some way to rectifying the initial impression from my previous course.  Over the table Sarah ordered Karahi chicken (8.75) and it certainly looked appealing to the eye. She found the tomatoes and fresh herbs helped created a lightness to the dish, with pleasantly spiced, soft chicken benefiting from being cooked in the tandoor oven.  Like my main it was quickly polished off with a side of standard pilau rice (3.25).  Our usual garlic naan was near enough as good as they come at 3.25.  There were a few wobbles on this occasion but the main courses were very tasty and I certainly wouldn't hesitate to order them again.  They essentially turned around what could have been an otherwise very disappointing evening.  Service standards were set high, too, and the surroundings acceptable. The Indian odyssey continues...

Morningside Spice is a great Indian restaurant and takeaway in the Morningside area of Edinburgh - in an ideal location for students to pop into for their lunch or dinner.   They offer a wide selection of authentic Indian cuisine which is cooked with fresh spices and is always full of flavour. I ordered the Chili Garlic Chicken which was completely delicious but really spicy and it felt like my mouth was on fire by the end of the meal. The rice is excellently cooked and the naan breaks are massive - yum! Morningside Spice also had wide selection of vegetarian meals and I had the vegetable pakoras to start which were amazing. The waiters in the restaurant were warm and welcoming and incredibly efficient in their service.   They also offer a takeaway service which was really popular was I was dining in the restaurant and having tasted their food I can see why. The only downside which I could see was that the people who were ordering takeaways were waiting a long time for their food, but it was a busy Friday night so it is probably to be expected.  I will definitely be back at Morningside Spice for another curry soon, I loved it.

Morningside Spice is a great Indian restaurant with a good, well organised menu, and great food and service.  I went there for the first time about three weeks ago and the decor inside was pretty stunning with a fresh, contemporary feel.  The menu has a whole range of kebabs of varying sorts as well as the usual rogan josh, balti and tikka dishes.  I opted for the beef karahi which I hadn't ever tried before and it tasted great.  I love cardamom seeds and this dish had plenty of them with a good balance of heat and real flavour.  The portions are a perfect size, even for big eaters, and the naans are some of the biggest and best I think I have ever eaten.   The service is quick and friendly and they also do free deliveries on takeaways under 10 which I would certainly recommend.  I can't really fault this place as it's moderately priced with great food and a chilled out atmosphere.

This is my favourite Indian restaurant in Edinburgh. The food is amazing and so is the service! A real gem!   A bit off the beaten track for those of us not living in the area but worth the trip everytime!

This is the best Indian Restaurant for an evening meal I have been to in Edinburgh. The restaurant is spotless and the waiters are very smart. The general atmosphere is great with traditional Indian music in the background. The value for money is good, it is not particularly cheap but it is a brilliant place to splash out if you like Indian food. The service is excellent with waiting times for food being around 30 minutes when I was there last.   The menu is excellent, there is a extensive range of curries and starters. I would have to say the Chicken Madras is amazing! The mango lassi drinks are also second to none. This restaurant is probably best enjoyed in couples or groups of people rather than families. The only thing lacking is a good range of desserts but there are very few Indian Restaurants that I feel provide a good range of desserts. Many do not even feel able to cope with dessert after their main meals as the portions are very generous.   All in all the experience of dining in Morningside Spoce is excellent and there is nothing to complain about!! . They even provide you with excellent mints with the bill.

I used the takeaway service of this restaurant and I wasnt disappointed. They had a massive selections of mains to choose from (and very kindly recommended a side dish with most of them!) As a vegetarian, I was pleased to see an interesting veggie section on the menu and can wholly recommend the sabzi kofta passanda- veggie balls covered in egg (sounds weird but was goood!) The naan was perfect and the side dish of sag panir was delicious!  The only down side was the time it took to deliver. Granted, we ordered on a Saturday night, but it was way over an hour before the food arrived and we only live 10 mins away! But it was worth the wait, as the food was amazing! Cant wait to try out the restaurant now!

The Morningside Spice is a fantastic Indian restaurant on Morningside Road. It has recently undergone a refurbishment and now the interior looks classy and modern; I went for a meal there this evening and there were fresh tulips on the tables, it was a nice touch. The staff are wonderful; whenever I visit I am greeted like an old friend, it's one of the reasons I keep going back. Tonight I ordered the lamb tikka, it is a relatively simple dish but a lot depends on the quality of the lamb; needless to say, the quality of the meat was excellent and I enjoyed my dinner immensely. I finished off with the pistachio kulfi which the waiter informed me was homemade, it was delicious and my mum declared it 'magnificent'. I can't wait for my next visit.
We had a take away from here and the food wasn't bad. Felt a little awkward standing among the diners waiting to get our food though.

36 for two burgers and drinks.  My partner's veggie mac&cheese burger was good; and it was quite big!  That's in comparison to my tasteless, small Joe Pesci burger.  ... Should have read the other reviews on here before we sat down. Defo no fries or sides, even for that at price. Won't be back.

I was looking for some decent priced lunch on the royal mile and this place didn't disappoint. It had a mouthwatering selection of burgers, sides and craft beers. They even had a suggested beer pairing on the menu which was great. Lovely staff and quick service. They even offer a free phone charging service while you eat. I thought that was a great idea.
The meat looked good but it was overcooked and dry. Rather strange because it came pretty fast so I am not sure they cook it on order (for sure they don't girl it on charcoal...)

Average would sum up my experience here. The burger was ok, but there was a certain lack of flavour about the meat and I'm not sure all of the components came together (I had the Dirty South) that well. The fries were just warm enough.   The beer list was extensive, but damn expensive! Also a huge proportion were sold out.   Service was friendly enough, but we had to ask for further drinks orders to be taken, and while it's never nice to be pestered, you do like to be asked periodically.   Here's a caveat - this was a visit in August and there were 25 of us and while those two things combined may contribute to a reduced experience, it shouldn't really effect a place situated on the Royal Mile - it's not like they didn't know it would be busy.   Edinburgh has some brilliant burger options (Burger, Red Squirrel to name two) and I'll not be rushing back here to give it another go. Sorry!

I really hoped this burger joint would measure up but sadly I was disappointed and have had better burgers served as a pub lunch. The milkshakes are definitely 'milk' shakes and I couldn't tell if it contained ice cream, if you want a thick shake this is not the place to get it! Limited choice of flavours 4 on the menu and no peanut butter and a super steep price of 4.50 for the size. When ordering we were told they had ONE piece of chicken left due to a busy Saturday and a late Sunday delivery so burgers were made either with a beef or veg patty option (don't expect to be asked how rare you want the beef). I ordered "the dirty south" burger with the vege patty but on delivery of the burger it contained no pork as per the menu, so that had to go back.  The battered onion rings and gherkins were thick and voluminous, being slightly greasy and would be better suited to a thinner, crispier coating. Lots of apologies from staff and no discount for the trouble. 20 for lunch was a bit steep, all things considered.

So we wandered in because we were starved and the best places were entirely booked for the night. We are from the US, so we expect that there will be some differences in how local foods taste.  Overall, we had some excellent food on our trip to Scotland. This wasn't one of those meals. The reason I'm reviewing is because I think this place has the potential to be a really good pub.  I actually liked everything but the burger. I had a burger with bacon, egg and a fried hash brown potato.  The bacon and hash browns were really tasty.  The fries were fine. The bun was good. The really big problem was the meat. It was heavily dosed with black pepper. So much pepper that you couldn't taste anything else. It just overpowered the whole burger, and made it almost inedible. I was starved so I ate most of it anyway, at least until I wasn't so hungry. Once I wasn't so hungry, I couldn't eat anymore because the taste was so bad.  It's a shame because it had the makings of a really good burger, but ruined by bad seasoning.

Burgers were pretty good. One note burgers in Scotland are always well done so if you are used to juicey skip the burgers. If you like them well done this is the place for you. Service was good. Fries extra near 5 pounds and are portion for one Burgers cost about 13.95 pounds each

When they say just burgers and beers, it literally means just burgers and beers and nothing extra special.   Ordered the blue cheese burger. Well, I think I it's a very normal burger nothing exciting and just passed as a burger.  There are other places in Edinburgh which has better burger which gives extra with the same price. I think having its establishment on royal mile does not justifies the tourist price.  However, I have to say the sweet potato fries is a winner and best I have ever tried in Edinburgh. I was going to try the deep fried pickles but seems like they have taken it out of the menu.  They have a good list of beer though.  Overall, just normal burger for those who wants to fill up their stomach.

Given its location and beer prices this has 'tourist trap' written all over it but the Marcellus Wallace burger I had last Thursday was very good. Whether it (or indeed any others in the city) is worth paying double figures for is another question though.  Service was good to begin with (never before to I recall a wait person coming to advise us they're going off shift and pointing out their replacement) but my half of our party ended up being forgotten about & so only recieved our food when the other half were paying up and moving on. with such a high high ratio of staff to customers it wasn't clear how this could have occured but it wasn't a show stopper.  Has Edinburgh reached 'peak burger' yet? Possibly but this is not one of the city's many burger establishments that I'd rush to return to if that type of meal is deemed the order of the day.

The burger trend marches on apace in Edinburgh. Rather glad I decided to check out Just Burgers and Beer.  We ventured in hungry on a Saturday afternoon - made the wise move of skipping breakfast that morning. Hankering for my usual eggs, my eyes boggled at a burger on the menu called The Brinner - bacon, hash brown and a fried egg on a burger. I loved the addition of sauteed onions, which added just a smidge of sweetness. In spite of the song and dance of all the additional toppings the taste of the burger itself still came through well (unless some places I won't name - yet!).  One of my dining companions opted for the Mac Attack which had a whole burger made of macaroni cheese, nestled on top of the beef burger - wowza!  Everything was tasty and enjoyed, even the lovely crisp fries (even if they were served in a wee bucket - eh?) and I've been back a couple of times since. The build your own burger feature is quite good too, and I'm trying to hone in on my perfect burger - watch this space...

I started this draft after waiting an hour and twenty minutes for my burger (and twenty minutes for my drink beforehand). I've no idea how m burger could take so long to prepare even though we'd rocked up with a group of 14 (the place is set over two floors and was not crowded). I eventually ate my okay burger and not-quite crispy enough chips and got the hell out of there.  Amongst our group, there were several instances of orders being taken incorrectly, the wait staff having to walk around each upstairs table trying to work out who'd previously ordered what, leading to a really amateurish showing from the staff there.  As a backpacker, I liked that they had Wifi and Powerpoints so you could charge your phone (even advertising that fact on the menus), and it's not like the food was terrible, but there is no way I'll find myself turning to Burgers and Beers Grillhouse. They really need to get someone in there to train their staff.

I had never been to Burgers & Beers before today. I very much doubt i'll be back.  That sentence makes me quite sad, as it's a decent space (love all the wood details), the beer list (though expensive) lists some tried and True favourites and the sweet potato fries were tasty enough as a "tide over" snack. But today, the service left me with too much of a bad taste in my mouth to make me lean this direction again.  I come from a service industry background. This makes me both incredibly critical and incredibly sympathetic. I'll let someone get away with murder when they are obviously in the weeds, but I also have no patience when there doesn't seem to be a reason for poor service. Consider this my critical side.  We got seated quickly and the place was half full when we arrived... not busy but we weren't the only folks in the room. The gal serving us seemed to have about five tables to wait on in total. So we were seating... and then we waited.... and waited.... and waited. I'm a firm believer that the first drink should hit the table within 7 minutes of sitting down. We weren't approached for a drink order until at least the ten minute mark.  Once we ordered our two beers and sweet potato fries (an order that got an audible tisk from our server... I get it, it wasn't a full meal but the place was not busy and regardless, don't tisk someone AT THE TABLE!) we waited... and we waited... and we waited. The table next to us that was seated after received their drinks... and we waited. After another good 10-15 minutes, our beers came to the table. They were in bottles. I had assumed because of the delay that they might have been changing the kegs, but nope... bottles. It took 15 minutes to open bottles.   ???  The fries came pretty quickly thereafter, though the table next to us received their meals first once again. Like I said, they were tasty, but at that point, they had lost me already.  The sad part was, we would have happily taken down a second beer while we sat there chatting. Instead, we spend a strange hour looking over our shoulder, waiting for things to arrive. I would have even given this place a half nod if our server actually acknowledged the fact it took the better part of a half hour to get TWO bottles of beer to the table... but nope.   It was enough of a headache for me to look elsewhere next time i'm in the area.

I haven't been for burgers yet but went for a couple of beers with the yelp crew after a great zombie event! It was a nice place to go for a beer even if it was a tad pricey. The staff were friendly and let us all dressed as zombies chill in the front of the bar.   Not something I would go out of my way for but I wouldn't complain there. I will check out the burgers and update this in the future!

BURGER QUEST CONTINUES, and I want to score these guys higher, I really do. There are plenty of reasons to justify why Burgers and Beers Grillhouse might get a high 4, or even 5 stars...  Their ideas are great. The menu boasts some excellent combos, from the Mac Attack with its mac 'n' cheese fritter and Virginia sweet cured bacon, to the Brinner with its fried egg and hash brown; even the option of a focaccia or white glazed bun instead of the now-standard brioche adds a touch of individuality.  The staff are on their game. Friendly, knowledgeable, up for some banter and - most importantly - informal.   The quality is high. I chose the Marcellus Wallace: an 8oz beef patty, Virginia sweet cured bacon, peanut butter, lettuce, tomato, Monterey jack cheese, onion & buffalo hot sauce, and served on a seeded brioche bun. It rocked. Could've had more peanut butter (but what couldn't, right?) and the bun was a little big for the patty, but the flavours were great. The peanut butter and the buffalo sauce really taking charge throughout. The fries and sweet potato fries were crispy and nice, pretty standard, but no less enjoyable.  The place has space. The decor is certainly on trend with a lot of the burger joints permeating the country - bricks and chains and cages, all in a historical building setting (it's on the Royal Mile!) had shades of the Boozy Cow about it, or even Meat Mission in London. Plenty of tables inside and out and even a bar area, with a decent range of beverages, both alcoholic and not, for those who are willing to wait.  So why doesn't Burgers and Beers Grillhouse score a 4 or 5 from me? Well, sit back, friend, I'll tell you.  It would take some kind of fool not to notice the recent resurgence of the burger joint in Edinburgh. And long may it continue. We have loads. A craze started by the likes of Holyrood 9A, Lebowski's and Bar Kohl (may she rest in peace!) but more recently embraced by newer businesses, such as Burger, BMB, the Boozy Cow, who claim to SPECIALISE in burgers.  The problem with these latter examples is that, unlike the gastro pubs that preceded them, when you look at their delightful list of sandwiches, the price you see next to the burger is for the burger. Just the burger. That's it. No longer are fries and a slaw included in the cost on the menu, no, now you need to order those supplements as a side and pay the associated costs thereof.  Anyone who has read my reviews of Burger and BMB will know I have an issue with this. Fries should be included in the price of the burger. End of. It's a British institution and long may it reign! Anyone who has read my reviews of Burger and BMB will ALSO know that I score Burger higher on the grounds that, for the same quality of sandwich, they are decidedly cheaper.  And this is where Burgers and Beers Grillhouse fails.  A monthly special at Burger, the sandwich alone will set you back about 7.99. Without chips. At BMB, the weekly special costs about 2 more, sitting at a penny shy of a tenner. Without chips.  At B&B Grillhouse they don't have specials (some would argue they are ALL special), but in the realms of burger creation, I would deem my Marcellus Wallace to be just that: a bespoke-designed burger, the standard of which competes quite capably alongside that which is produced by Burger, BMB, the Boozy Cow et al...   The Marcellus Wallace cost me 12.99.  Without chips.  This, my friends, is not on.  When three burgers and two fries to share costs a grand total of 60 - with no alcohol - this is not on. This is a prime example of paying for location. And I live in Edinburgh, and I see the Royal Mile every day. So why am I paying for their post code?  For these prices I wouldn't even be back if it was the best burger I'd ever had (alas that honour still resides in Berlin). And I didn't even mention the beer prices - 5 for a pint of Heineken. Heineken!? Who makes this stuff up!?  Be warned, friends. Save a fiver and get just as good from elsewhere.... it's not like we're short of options!!
Nice place but a bit expensive..  The burgers are served without any sides. 12 only for the burger is really expensive.

Stopped in here for dinner last night having heard good things about Meat Hook operating out of the bar's kitchen.  It's not immediately clear but you have to order the food at the bar. That hurdle overcome the burger my brother had & my Beerwurst with housemade "German" potato salad were both good and filling. The mustard & ketchup were also housemade & served in good sized pots along with one of HP sauce. Not sure if they make their own buns too but both were of a Brioche nature.   The bar itself has obviously not changed in any way just because it's got noted cooks making burgers onsite so it's still one to go to for good ales at sensible prices & to watch the sport on either BT or Sky. And probably the terrestrial channels too.

I was in Empress yesterday evening for a few drinks with colleagues and a bite to eat. Have to say I was impressed. Empress has a relaxed and friendly atmosphere, the bar staff were nice, chatty and very helpful with more detail about the menu options. A good selection of tasty bar food, and thankfully the beer selection seems to have improved since the last time I was here. It is no longer the preserve of random micro brewery beers which I'd never heard of, there are now some  mainstream beers to choose from. A big improvement!

Honestly, The Empress burger was the best I have had in a very long time. Cooked perfectly, no need for ketchup or any other extra sauces. Pretty good thin fries (chips). My mom had fish and chips (thick cut fries), also very good with some excellent tartar sauce (which they mixed themselves).  If I ever make it to Edinburgh again, The Empress will be on my list to revisit.

Reading the previous reviews I thought this was going to be dodgy as anything. I was ready to down my pint and leave sharpish. It turns out it was a decent surprise.   There was no angry patrons growling in my direction. Everybody was having a pint and watching the fitba. There ain't nothing fancy about it though. There ain't much to say. It's a bit of an old mans boozers. It serves a few decent beers from Harveistoun and Williams brothers. The staff were friendly.   Fine for a quick pint, but nothing special.

Lager & drink prices are cheap & service is good. Interesting atmosphere as well. Also has big TV screens for sports events which is good if combined with affordable booze. Free WiFi is available too.

This is a good, traditional pub which, as the decor informs you, has been around for a long time.  It feels friendly inside with a clean, impressive, wooden bar and plenty of top quality spirits behind it.  Malt whiskey is its speciality and it has a great, but also expensive, selection.  Pints are reasonably priced at about 3 each and they sell good quality, real ales and beers alongside the standard Tennents and Strongbow.   Mathers also has plamsa TV screens which are always showing the latest football, rugby or boxing matches.  Naturally, this attracts a good bunch of 'lads', but on any given nights there's a good range of people, including locals and students.

Like the others have pointed out, this is a man's pub, and I felt like a delicate flower in here, when I came on a night when I really should have known better, one of the World Cup games. Duh.  Safe to say I only stayed for one because I sort of feared for my life, but the pub was busy, bustling and packed with punters swigging pints and having a merry old time of it. I didn't fit in with my large glass of Rose at that point.  Great atmosphere, I might try a quieter time on my next visit and stick to the Pints.

Emma had it spot on, Bar Bruiser.   I've never felt less manly in my whole life. Everyone in here used to be a boxer/kick-boxer and have a 3 course meal of nails and barbed wire for dinner. They don't really make any noise or have anything to say until someone scores a goal, which then becomes the hot topic of conversation all week.   Staff are very nice though and the place is comfy.

Old traditional bar which has been around for a long time.   It tends to attract a slightly older crowd, who are much more interested in having good conversation than posing in an expensive George Street bar.   There's a coal fire in the winter, which is just the thing for thawing you out when you come in from the cold.
Pretty much what it says on the tin, an old geezers spit n sawdust pub. I like it!

Mathers is a bit of a spit and sawdust kind of establishment at the top of Broughton Street, the kind of place where you could probably actually get away with gobbing on the floor if you so desired. Its clientele look like the kind of guys who are qualified to use pneumatic drills, this is most definitely a bloke's pub and tends to be full of proper blokes on any given evening. I wouldn't come here on my own for a quiet drink, but the boyfriend and I have been in together on a few occasions to take advantage of their extensive and reasonably priced range of single malts. They show most major sporting events on their TVs, although I'd advise you get there early to grab a drink and somewhere to stand - it can get pretty mobbed.

Five star service on a fairly bustling Tuesday afternoon, myself and my girlfriend called in for some lunch. The waitress was also the assistant manager, I think her name was Laura and not only was she in good spirits but also friendly and helpful.   Whenever the burgers came out I was a little unimpressed at first, however, 3/4 of the way though I was beginning to struggle! Went for the Harlem, proper pressed steak burger, slices of chorizo and a red pepper aioli - was very tasty.   Overall I would definitely visit again, great value from a Groupon deal and was an enjoyable afternoon out.

Stopped in here one night not long before Xmas so, with most of the place reserved for a seasonal party, maybe not a time to experience it at its best.  No issues with the service & the milkshakes were large but how can you manage to get buns that are far too big for the burger they contain? Given the number of burger places in the city nowadays that needs some working on.

Taking over from the Riperian Rooms on East London Street, TriBeCa have opened their second Edinburgh location (Bruntsfield) which follows three Glasgow locations.  Decent size space with downstairs serving New York diner style food from 8am-10pm (Eve menu 5-10pm) 7 days a week. I tried brunch - "the Varick breakfast", which is French toast, eggs as you want them, crispy bacon, sausage etc. The food is decent, served quickly with good portions. The service was efficient and friendly. I haven't been to the other locations but can see why this is a popular place. Free wi-fi.

This is one of my favourite restaurants I've been too in awhile , so much so that we ate here twice in a row . The waffles and chicken dish is the weirdest but most wonderful combination! The waitresses are soo helpful and you don't have to chase them down to help . Great food , great service and a lovely atmosphere . I will be back here :)

Brochan is such a lovely addition to the Marchmont neighborhood. The owner Elaine has created a cafe with a lovely, light vibe and amazing food. The oatmeal is delicious and comes with awesome toppings (once I had some vegan brownie topping fresh out of the oven which was amazing). The cakes, cookies and coffee are also lovely. Brochan is a great place to meet up with friends or study--I'm moving and I'm going to miss it!

As far as burritos go, this was a good 'un.  The regular was generous on the portion size with ample filling. I went for coconut squash and It was well-seasoned; really full of flavour. So were the beans and the salsa. - It was a delicious burrito, and fairly inexpensive considering just how much it filled me up. I was in that awkward place when your after-work plans don't involve food but home is just a little too far to go home for something to eat. In the end, I was very glad of this, because I found a new burrito joint I can rely on.  I love that the veggie and vegan options here are that little bit more interesting. Coconut squash was delicious but the chipotle shredded tofu also sounded great.  The only negative I can think is that they aren't open late. But, that's no biggie. - I'm more than satisfied with dinner from Taco Mazama this time round!

Warning to snobs: this is NOT authentic Mexican.   Now that's out the way, they make decent tacos that most people seemed to eat just to refuel before going back for more shopping on Prince's St.   I had three tacos with the charbroiled chicken. The chicken was charbroiled but it wasn't seasoned nor did it have any distinct flavor. This is where many inauthentic eateries miss the mark, marinate your chicken. How else will my taste buds force me to remember your chain, absent of s distinct flavor?   They also use grocery store flour tortillas, authentic restaurants use homemade corn tortillas.   The winner here is the guacamole, which was surprisingly good. I took some of it home as well. They stock jarritos, too. All in all, not a bad place for a quick bite but don't expect much by way of taste.

Taco Mazama is perfectly suitable for a burrito on the fly. I was looking for a quick fix whilst waiting for an engagement, and so as my bus stopped in front of the Taco Mazama location on Hanover street I trotted up to the doors and then inside--only to be told they were closed! Fine, no problem. Imagine my bewilderment moments later when I see another Taco Mazama, this one on Princes Street below street level with just a sign advertising its presence, except obviously open past 5pm. I wandered in, ready to take my burrito chances once more.  Put simply, Taco Mazama is fine. My burrito was 4.99 and pleasant enough, if a wee bit on the smaller side compared to the gargantuan fares you can get from Illegal Jack's and Los Cardos. I was intrigued by the other veggie options such as squash, but ended up going with my old standard, veggie haggis. When I asked for it the girl behind the counter without a word disappeared  seemingly into the floor only to appear about 5 minutes later from out of nowhere with veg haggis in hand. Burrito magic?!  I think what Taco Mazama didn't really provide for me was atmosphere. The tables (maybe three total) and chairs are all very cheap and no-nonsense. The burrito was about the same (and no black beans?? wahhh!), although it did fill the belly well enough. The furnishings and atmosphere left a lot to be desired, but like I said, if you're looking for a quick bite in a hurry you don't really need candlesticks and ambiance. At the end of the day I suppose if I was in a hurry I would consider going back to Taco Mazama, but when the alternatives (admittedly on the other ends of town) are so much nicer I don't know that I'd bother unless pressed for time.
Our favourite Indian in Edinburgh by far. The north indian garlic chicken is super

This shop is ugly, it has dated (one from 2011) magazines sitting on a coffee table and had I not been on a mission to try different Indians I would likely have walked past. However on a mission, I was and one part of the shop front actually stands up - "For curry lovers".  I have tried my usual selection of dishes (biryani, madras, chilli garlic) and have to say the food was of good standard, rich spice flavours came through as they should and the meat has always been tender and flavoursome. Part of that flavour though comes from the fact that they use chicken thigh and breast, this does mean you may get the odd tough bit, but overall it is worth it.  While the portions of curry and rice are roughly standard for an Indian takeaway (probably enough to feed you for two nights, if you compared the portion to a ready-meal) you get a big portion of pakora, served in a polystyrene box. The pakora, curry and rice was around 10 so not expensive either, given the quantity of food.  All in all I would recommend Saiyem's if you stay in the area.

I wasn't expecting too much from Saiyems when I first went there- the bright yellow exterior shouted - tacky- to me, but my friend who lives locally to the area insisted that their curries are great, and he was right. We ordered on a Wednesday night just before a Champions League game and so it was quite busy with other people having the same idea of watching the match over a curry. We waited inside the restaurant and it is a lot more quaint and respectable than the exterior, although that isn't hard.  I ordered a chicken bhuna with 2 papadums and a garlic naan bread, the prices here are pretty decent and for the quality and portions of food, it offers good value. The naan bread was one of the freshest I have had and not at all greasy, whilst the chicken bhuna was flavoursome and the chicken very fresh and tender.

Brilliant little Indian take away just on Gorgie Road been around a while. Good choices, good service, brill meals and value for money. What else is there to say really. Does exactly what it says on the tin

My pay day treat each month, everything we have tried is excellent.   Plus points - The portions are huge, so careful on the amount you order.  - Huge range of veggie treats for the missus - the seafood is super fresh  - delivery is really quick  - if you go in person the shop is clean and modern  Things to try that we love:  Spicy Hot Squid, Large  Spicy Hot Crispy Tofu with Fresh Chilli & Onion, Large  Spicy Hot Crispy Aubergine, Large  Vegetable Singaporean Rice Noodle

Excellent Chinese takeaway in Newington. I have been to Hot Kungfu with friends many times, and I've never been disappointed.  The food is always prepared fresh and quite quickly. Prices are good and include rice, which I always thought was the norm but often is not the case in Edinburgh. Drink prices are also good value, so I can get an entire meal for 6-7. You can't really beat that.  Food tastes good, staff are friendly, and there is an efficient delivery service too, if you're not able to collect. Highly recommended.

Popped in here to order a little bit of takeaway on a rainy Friday night. Contrary to the other reviews I have seen online, I actually found the service to be quite friendly. Though when I asked what the difference really is between the large dish and the small dish, I was just told the large dish is bigger than the small dish. The food itself was not bad, it didn't exactly blow me away. I went for the small chicken chow mien (no veg because I am weird like that), which is actually is quite big, so who knows what the large is like! The chicken was a little on the dry side but the noodles were pretty good.

Attempted to pop in for a drink, but the bartender refused to accept my wife's U.S. issued ID even tho she was clearly of age and stated that they would only accept a passport, which was at the hotel (who goes out on a Friday night with their passport?). First time we had this issue in Edinburgh and promptly went to another pub down the street, which didn't have any issues accepting her ID.

Whiki is a bar on the Royal Mile in Edinburgh.    The first time I went the bar tender recommended a really good beer, so A+ for the drinks. I also had the food here, which I think was a little ordinary but still decent for the price.   So recommended for a drink or a drink with food. Perhaps not ideal if you're just after food.

My last breakfast in Edinburgh before hopping on the plane back to Dublin. Was extremely happy I came in! The people were nice, and the food was outstanding. I had the full breakfast and for the price I thought it was loaded with food. All of it was very good too, not bland or a cheap tourist imitation. I really liked this place and was disappointed I hadn't gone in earlier.  Also, I can imagine that it's a pretty cool place in the evenings. They have live music every night and a ton of Scotch Whisky to try if you're into that sort of thing. Very cool place.

Whiski is the kind of bar that will win the tourists over, while the locals will tend to head somewhere off the beaten track.  Serving up a mixture of pub grub and traditional Scots dishes (like cullen skink), Whiski blends contemporary decor with a traditional feel.  As the previous reviewers have said, it is quite a synthesized representation of the Scots pub, and it feels as though its existence is based on what tourists it can lure in. Nevertheless, I can imagine it would be quite charming to people travelling through Edinburgh, so it gets four stars from me since I can see its appeal to international guests. And when all is said and done, there's a good selection of booze behind the bar and well cooked food, so it's pleasant and popular with passer's by!

We were looking for a nice place for some late night food and perhaps, some entertainment and we read good reviews of this place. We found the food pretty good and the dessert was excellent! They have some kind of performance every night of the week and ours was Traditionally folk songs. The performers gave such a rousing performance that some of the guests joined them in the clapping and singing! Very good experience indeed.

This place... everything is good.    1. Cullen Skink SO good... I don't know how to put it.  We wanted six bowls of this.  2. Rump Steak perfectly cooked, great whiskey sauce.  3. Haggis Tower so good, fresh, delicious.  4. Sticky Toffee Pudding yes this is good too!!! WITH ice cream!!  Service is good too.  But the food... the best.

What a fab pub with lots of atmosphere, fab food and all the whiski u could want.  In the evenings from 9.30 onwards they have music so this place has it all.  The decor is traditional with stag heads, photo's and Scottish memorabilia but with a bit of kitch like fairy lights.  Tables of 10 and more can make a booking otherwise just turn up have a drink or two and wait for a table to become available.   I had the haggis tower with a whiskey sauce tatties and neeps, gorgeous and very filling.  The house made chorizo and pork sausages,mash and onion gravy, banging.  The whiskey cheese cake and cranachan should not be missed.  Without shadow of a doubt I would recommend this place, miss this miss out. Xoxo

Great beer and whiski selection! Didn't have any food just came in for a few pints and some music. Bar staff were awesome! Super friendly in a real way. A good spot in the middle of the tourist world where locals come as well!
Delicious first-time haggis experience, and really good steak pie. My daughter devoured her burger as well, and my son finished all his soup. Family-friendly and fun whisky flights.

My first venture in here, I wasn't sure what to think.  It felt difficult to get attention for service.  But then it warmed up.  The staff turned out to be very friendly and helpful.  The whisky list is monstrous and the food is pretty good.  I ended up coming back a few times during my visit and standing around the bar and listening to music was a most enjoyable way to kill a few hours (and brain cells).    When someone says "Whiski", there's Whiski Bar and Restaurant and then their sister establishment, Whiski rooms.  While related, don't confuse the two.

This spot was recommended by 3 different people on Yelp and on the streets of EDI so I made it a must try. The recommendations definitely came thru on this place, it is awesome.  I had the steak and ale pie which is a modern deconstructed version. The flavors are so rich and creamy and the best thing about getting it their way is the pie crust is super flaky.   The mussels are great too. They come thru with a huge amount of mussels. Probably 30 or more?  The bangers and mash were some of the best bangers. The meat in the middle is so juicy and spiced with mustard seeds and other tasty flavors which simply made my day.  If you're a large group try calling ahead and booking the back room during the week. On the weekend though its first come first serve which makes it near impossible if you're more than 4 people trying to walk up at dinner time.  Cheers

Oh man, that whiskey list...  Killer place right across from our hotel room. It was packed and I could totally see why. Their whiskey list was two full Excel spreadsheets with every type of whiskey you've ever known and then some. The service was nice, too. If you're looking for a hard-to-find scotch, they probably have it.

We stopped in here since it was the closest, open, bar to our hostel on our first night visiting Edinburgh. The decor was very nice, and the people-watching was even better. The crowd skewed mostly older but there were several incredibly attractive and well dressed women in their 30's here when we stopped in.  There was a folk guitar band playing, which was a little too mellow for our tastes. The selection of whiskeys though was phenomenal, and the bartenders were very skilled. The whiskey sour and hot toddy were particularly good! It's a very upscale and classy place.  The bathrooms were clean, and had a goofy condom dispenser that sold "Whiskey Flavored Condoms". We got a good laugh out of that, especially the fine print "Do not Use While Driving".  Good place to stop for a meal and a warm-up drink before heading out for the clubs.

Dipped in here on day two in Edinburgh. It was a late morning start and we wanted breakfast. I'd noted another spot that would have been a good mile walk down the way but the driving rain and cozy exterior beckoned us in. One side of the restaurant is a whiskey shop. Impressive array of different types of whiskies - I had no idea or interest as I am not well-refined in the whiskey world. If you are DEFINITELY stop in or shop here. whiskishop.com. We both went with specials. I had the starter and main combo of raw Scottish salmon with a frisee salad and creme fraiche, followed by crayfish linguine. Yum! The salmon was fab, especially when dragged through the creme, followed with a bite of fresh-baked crusty bread. The pasta was lovely as well. Flavorful and cooked al dente with oil, peas and the star - crayfish. Yum. Most UK restaurants have some sort of starter/main special and I highly recommend going this route when possible as you will get a nice variety for your dosh. Man had the Gambon ham and egg special with chips. Gorgeous plating. Egg cooked to perfection so the yolk slowly spilled out over the ham. Chips - awwww! Why can't we get chips this good at home. Thick-sliced but not soggy or under/over done. Crisp and hot. Made with love. So delectable that ketchup is superfluous. Nice price point and very pretty interior. Comfy banquette seating - try to get next to the window to people-watch. Staff were sweet and made sure our coffees and waters were filled. If it hadn't of been morning with a full itinerary ahead, I definitely would have sampled some whiskey. Last note. One of the other Yelpers mentioned the cutesy spelling - it almost threw us off as well but the downpour helped settle our minds quickly.

Quite possibly the best pub we ate at while in Edinburgh for holiday.  I had their sausage and mash of the day which was a Mediterranean pork sausage. It was excellent.  Their selection of Malt Whiskys was as good as advertised.  The service was spot on. This was definitely not what I expected from a very touristy location on the Royal Mile.

Amazing haggis. Made me a believer!  Try the Balvenie 14 yr Caribbean Cask, it's amazing.  Bangers and mash had the creamiest mash. Wait was long, but the bar area welcomes you and will transfer your tab. Great experience.
Good bar food - great selection of scotch!  Very helpful in selecting my whisky flight.

Went for lunch, and the only regret I had was that I didn't go for a bigger meal for dinner!   I got a glass of hot toddy and a starter of spicy prawns with bread. Both were absolutely mouth-watering. I'm very glad I tried my first hot toddy here, and my meal was also delightful albeit only a starter portion. I left feeling happy full.   I absolutely adored the ambience as well. Typical Scottish bar type of place but more sophisticated. I liked their selection of music in the background. They have live music every night at 10pm, so try it out if you can!  Great place on Royal Mile, definitely give it a try!

We were drawn to the Whiski because they have live music, which didn't disappoint, even though we sat in the back. However, their food and upscale yet cozy atmosphere made it outstanding. I tried the chicken breast with wild mushroom sauce, which was made with tarragon. Really tasty! My husband had the sausage and mash, and devoured every drop. We finished with the sticky toffee pudding, which seems to be an Edinburgh classic. One bite, and you'll see why.
Good location right on the royal mile. Great service food was good not excellent. The ambiance was cool, Great setting with life music. The staff did a great job.

First vegetarian haggis for me. I need to say I'm not a huge fan of it but it was a good dish. The haggis is really special and a little bit to heavy for me. However, the whisky sauce and mash potatoes were both amazing. My bf took the real haggis and he enjoyed it a lot !  Really appreciated the service, nice staff, very welcoming! Thanks for the discovery :)

Super fantastic place! Both the food and cocktails are firing on all cylinders! It was our first official meal in Edinburgh and it was the best introduction! The food is great quality and rich with flavor. It was our first intro to haggis and we had them in spring roll form and it was fantastic. Wow! I had no idea I would like it so much. Great flavors! The saltiness of the haggis paired perfectly with the sweet plum sauce. The Cullen Skink was a hearty and smoky haddock soup. Mmmm. Definitely grab this traditional dish! The steak and ale pie was great looking and my friend enjoyed it thoroughly. The whisky drinks were top notch! I could have had the Monkey Kilt all night. I can't wait to bring this recipe back stateside. We liked this place so much for dinner we came back here the same night for a night cap. The place is also warm and inviting and warms the soul on a chilly day. So happy we found this place.

What I Ordered: Haggis Tower Flavor: I honestly wasn't a huge fan of this Haggis, mostly because I disliked the whiskey sauce.  I'm sure I would have liked it better if it was dry. Service: Friendly and attentive. Atmosphere: Nice decor. Price: Pretty pricey for the portion size as it's right in the middle of the Royal Mile. Location: Great location.  As mentioned above, it's about as central a location as you can get if you're in old town Edinburgh

Cool looking place, awesome food and great selection of whisky!!  WHISKI was the perfect end to a long day of travel in Scotland. 3 of us all shared "WHISKI' most popular" whiskey flight, we were not disappointed. We also all shared the Haggis stack, sundried tomato and pork sausages and mash and the salmon. Everything was incredible and trying haggis for the first time, the whole thing was a lovely experience!!

While The Whisky was supposed to be the one place we 'just had' to visit in Edinburgh, I wish we had skipped it.  It was crowded, which I actually enjoy in a pub-style  restaurant.  It was also quite unique in the large variety of Scotch flights available, though I am not a  Scotch drinker, others in my group enjoyed it  The dinner menu was good but lacked anything for the smaller appetite, especially when considering appetizers in advance.  The food was delicious, but here is why I can only give 2 stars (and that is generous!)  As I mentioned, it is an evening, starters to dessert and coffee.  I wanted to enjoy everything to get the full Scottish experience, even if it is pricey.  By the time my delicious burger arrived, I could barely eat more than just a few bites. The burger was 22 and reckoning it might make a great middle of the night snack, I asked for a takeaway container and the waitress seemed appalled and said 'NO!'  She proceeded to look down her nose at me with a bit of contempt and tried to take my plate. I told her I would keep it a bit longer and she rolled her eyes and rushed off.  We sat a bit longer and I could feel the waitress staring at me from behind, just waiting and watching for me to figure a way to take the burger with me. At that point, she said it was against the law for me to take food (which I paid a lot for) away from the restaurant.  I don't like wasting food or money and I especially do NOT like being treated like an idiot.  I did wrap the burger up and left it sitting on the table deliberately.  If I'd had a pen and paper I would have written a note of some sort to her, but alas I did not. If I  could have, the note would have asked her if this is how she would like to see her mother or sister or friend treated in public. Would she appreciate it if someone she held close was utterly and completely humiliated in front of not only family but the entire restaurant.  I work in the service industry, but in commercial aviation.  If this were to happen on my aircraft it would be the last day of that individual's career with my airline.  I would make sure that a proper apology was made to the guest and suggest a different career path  Our bill was close to 600.  That was not even close to what it cost for ruining the rest of my trip to Edinburgh.  Enough said. I will never return to The Whiskey and probably not to Edinburgh, either.  Save your money for a place that sincerely VALUES its guests and treats each with care and respect Delete review

My wife and I stopped in here for dinner one night and had a fantastic evening.  I got the scottish salmon with lemon sauce, which was cooked perfectly and the sauce was delicious (not too lemony/acidic). My wife got the WHISKI burger which came with haggis and whisky sauce! Despite it's somewhat impractical size, she managed to finish most of it and enjoyed it quite a bit.   After dinner we decided to try a whisky tasting. Whiski helpfully provides a selection of whisky tasting flights to choose from on their drinks menu. This was perfect for us, since we did not have any prior experience in this area. In particular, they have a whisky flight for beginners which we shared. They flight came with four whiskys and a helpful information pamphlet describing the smells and tastes the whiskys were supposed to evoke. Trying the different whiskys with my wife was a lot of fun and stimulated some really enjoyable and amusing conversations!   I would recommend Whiski for their food, but I especially would recommend coming here to try out Whisky Flight #1 if you've never tried whiskey and don't know where to start.

WHISKI is a fun, if not touristy, bar and restaurant right on the Royal Mile. They have a massive whisky collection, a wide selection of local beers, and really decent food. They also have a large number of whisky flights to choose from if you'd like to sample a variety, complete with tasting notes. Staff are very friendly and knowledgable.   I opted for the Whiski Burger, a rather unwieldy burger topped with haggis and a whisky sauce. It was really good, but pretty unmanageable, and a bit expensive (though that's to be expected as this place is in tourist central). Brandon A. got the salmon, which I tried and was really fantastic.    Nice, casual place to get a solid introduction to whisky, and sample some decent Scottish fare. They also have live music every night!

Haggis! I have been waiting for a month to experience my very first bite of haggis because I might have taken it a bit too seriously ( just kept searching Yelp...). Finally I ended up at the WHISKI bar & restaurant!   Started the meal with a traditional Scottish soup: Cullen Skink, which was my favourite dish of the day. Super yummy. The must-try Haggis tower came in a very generous portion, that tastes more delicious with oak crackers. And finally the Whiski burger(with haggis on top), I was kind of stuffed full of haggis..so I am sorry, Whiski burger, there was just no room for the chemistry we could have had. Service-wise, the waiter is attentive and very knowledgeable about whisky!   Will I come back? That's for sure. It's a great place to start tasting Edinburgh and be introduced to scottish cuisine!

Absolutely a must not miss.  We stopped in mid-afternoon and grabbed olives and the cheese plate to share over ciders and whiskies. And is was the perfect relaxing and tasty paise in a great Edinburgh day!

Came here for dinner, and ordered Haggis and steak & ale pie. Both were wonderful. So flavourful and tasty. I give 5 to the food. We also got the luxury ice cream. I wouldn't recommend that one. Otherwise, everything else was great. I would definitely come back.

First timer. I was part of a 3-hour Food Tasting Tour in Edinburgh, Scotland (secretfoodtours.com). We stopped here to taste whiski. I am not a whiski guy (rum guy) and I did not liked the whiski because is not my cup of tea. Good experience.

My wife and I stopped in to this fun Royal Mile pub and had a late dinner and listen to music on two consecutive evenings. Although crowded on both nights, we were able to secure a small table new the front door where the live music played. The service here was very friendly, welcoming and attentive. The food here is delicious and filling with many traditional Scottish meal items on the menu. My wife order the cheese board which she enjoyed. I had the steak & ale pie with chips and vegetables which was outstanding. The live music which starts between 9:30-10pm added to the pub atmosphere. The prices are very reasonable for both food and alcoholic drinks. #edinburghpubs #edinburghlivemusic #edinburghrestaurants

We ate here on the night the Eiffel Tower burned - I don't think I'll ever forget walking inside and gasping with surprise when I saw the TV over the bar, and then watching in horror alongside everyone else at the bar. Anyway, onto the review. There weren't any tables when we arrived, so we started with a wee dram at the bar. As you would expect from an establishment named Whiski Bar, there was a very extensive whisky menu. They advertise as having 300+ to choose from, but I didn't count them. After quite a while waiting at the bar, we finally got a table. It would be almost an hour after that before our food arrived. I'm dinging their rating quite a bit for such a long wait, and for not being upfront about the delays. The waitress's excuse was that there was a large party further back in the restaurant, but surely a restaurant this large right on the main tourist stretch ought to be better prepared for busy dinner hours. The food itself was good but unmemorable. I think I had haggis neeps and tatties, but perhaps that was a different night at a different place. We skipped dessert, because we were tired of sitting in the same place. Verdict: don't come here unless you have a lot of time to spare. I'm certain that there's better places to eat in Edinburgh.

I'm not normally so hard on the Royal Mile pubs. Yes they are nearly all marketed with some collage of Scottish themes to pull people in, trap them, then take all their money, but ironically they often end up being a lot more welcoming than a lot of the local pubs in Edinburgh.  But I felt WHISKI was verging on the exploitative. Okay so nothing was that bad. The food is alright and they have a good selection of whisky (I agree with Kate about the whisky cider). But the prices were just too much. I resent having to pay almost 10 for a main course of average pub food. Plus whilst the staff weren't rude they didn't seem interested either. Also why is the name in CAPITALS? I feel like I am being SCREAMED at.  Perhaps I will try WHISKI again and have a better experience. Perhaps like a good Scotsman I should just stick to the drink.

This is your bog-standard Edinburgh tourist pub. It's named to attract tourist, it's decorated to attract tourists and it attracts tourists. It's very Scottish and very traditional, it embodies everything that is deemed Scottish. As a Scott, I avoid these places like the plague and I am reminded why when I go in - I'm almost a novelty to tourists when they hear my northern accent. No, this place is definitely not for me, but tourists lap this stuff up. Not very authentic, but a nice enough place if you're visiting.

Whiski is divine and hosts one of the best Scottish beer selections in the city, the restaurant food is also rather delightful!   The decor is very warm and manages to stay the right side of kitsch, and a plus point for all you visitors with children, it's on the Royal Mile & has high chairs.   Try the mash!   ess

I visited Whiski after a recommendation from a friend and I have to say it lived up to my expectations! The staff were so polite and friendly I was slightly taken aback- well, it's not every day someone behind a bar asks how your day was. And yes, I'm pretty sure it wasn't flirting!   The staff were particularly accomodating when my German friend, who was fresh off the plane, was asking for Scottish beer recommendations.   The interior is lovely- very Scottish and traditional but it avoids being dark and dingy. Great place to take a friend and show off Edinburgh's pub culture!
Great food, great whiskey selection, a good time.  Went with a bunch of Scots and even they liked it.  I had the haggis which was divine.

Got Haggis tower. It is fine dining meets Haggis. It's delish. I also orderered whisky (Scotch, for us Americans) on 2 separate occasions.  Ask them for the whisky guide, it will help you choose from the giant selection of whisky. This place generally seems crowded and full of tourists.

Great selection of Scotch, naturally, as well as beers and cocktails.   Didn't try the food, but the music was great.  My boyfriend and I danced along and somewhere a couple of girls have video of us!  Great place.

Love this bar/restaurant one of the very few real Scottish ones left in the capital. If you like whisky and good food you will not find better anywhere , has huge variety of Whiskies as well as great fresh homemade food , Steak Pie is legendary in Edinburgh , staff are very good and has good selection of beers/lagers. Scottish band plays about 3 nights a week as well. Families welcome which is rare in Edinburgh.

First bar/restaurant we ever visited in Edinburgh and the only one we keep going back to. Food on both occassions I've eaten there has been a bit small in portion but very tasty.   However, the best thing has to be the service. First time we went we wanted to try some proper Scottish whisky so we asked the bar man for advice. It was quite a busy evening yet he spent about 30 minutes with us describing each one, brought us a couple of samples (which we paid for) but never asked us to buy any bottles or anything.   Probably the best customer service I have ever received in this country for anything and worth going for that alone.

I love going here for a drink - the atmosphere is warm and inviting and the staff are friendly. Just don't have the food and you'll be right. I had dinner here at two occasions (vegetarian and fish dishes) and on both occassions it was awful. But for a drink it's great! They have a good selection of wines too!

This is a fantastic pub, great food, a huge selection of whisky, and even if you dont drink whisky ( I dont) there's plenty to interest you.its a great place to go for a night out, they do regular live music nights, and you can take the kids in for lunch during the day. Top Class.

This is the only bar that I would go into in the Royal Mile as it has a really inviting ambiance with lots of candles and does really excellent food for a bar. The service can be a bit slow but the staff always emphasis that the food is homemade and fresh and that is why it can take a bit longer to serve when it is busy. Hard to get a seat sometimes.

Great place to get a lively feel of Edinburgh without the tourist traps (although there were a lot of tourist in there). Space is tight. Food is good. And they have several awesome whiski flights! Great place to get a feel for Scottish pub food followed by some whiski sampling.

I had a little look through other reviews and think I may be the only one so far who was not really massively impressed by this place.   It was a lovely Saturday afternoon and after a childish wee stroll through camera obscura I took my friend here for lunch. He is very much a soup and a sandwich type of bloke so the fact this was on the menu here was a bonus. We arrived and were told that there were no tables, even though I could quite clearly see one, and that they were unsure how long the wait would be. A couple of moments later this was corrected, and we were promptly seated.  The menu here did not blow me away to be honest, pretty much as I expected, soup, sandwiches, the usual scottish fayre really. I had a salmon, lemon and creme fraiche sandwich and he ordered the sweet potato soup with a chicken mayo sandwich. There really was quite a wait for drinks, and for food.
