They do great burgers and big fatty sandwiches, as well as the usual American type food. I love their desserts, purely because they are huge and full of things which are bad for you but taste oh so good. Give me a Sundae and I will love you forever.  Occasionaly (special occasions, such as pay day) my flatmate and I will come in here for cocktails. He seems to spend his life going to various cocktail bars in Edinburgh and seems to think the best cocktails are to be found here. I agree they are very good. The whole experience ends up being very expensive though.

This is not a restaurant I would go to regularly but occasionally it's fab! The portions are large and the food is generally good. The pig sandwich is my favourite-messy but yummy!   The staff can be a little on the over helpful but at least this means the service tends to be fairly quick.   The noise levels can be pretty horrific when there are large groups in coupled with the loud music.   Not somewhere for an intimate meal but for big portions of good food this is a great place!

I don't like the Hard Rock place at all. I have been for a couple of work night outs over the years and have always found it completely under-whelming.   The food is boring and predictable and over priced. The service has always been ok but nothing great. The drinks are fine but never been very impressed with the cocktails.   This place has been going for so long that I would have expected them to have got the formula right by now - maybe that is the problem - it's a tired and jaded formula now. I can see it appealing to small children but not really anyone else!

Just another Hard Rock Cafe and it's no better or worse than many of its contemporaries around the globe.   It's set in a nice old bank building on George Street, but that's about as interesting as it gets when you're listening to Billy Joel and munching on your burger with curly fries.   The best thing about this place is probably being able to come here for a late night (over-priced) cocktail. However, if you're coming to Edinburgh, do yourself a favour and go somewhere a bit more extravagant.   I give it two stars because the staff are friendly, the location is good and they make nice cocktails. The rest is just rather dull without being offensive.

I have to say I was very dissapointed here, we waited an hour to be seated, whilst they were quite happy to sell us alcohol, we were then told they thought we had had enough because we had the giggles.   I found the staff to be rude and quite different from what I have come to expect from this food chain who usually go out of the way to give good service.   Found it strange how they didn't think we had had enough for the hour they were taking our money at the bar, and couldn't even be polite about it.   Would never go here again out of principle.

I have been twice, and the both times I went I enjoyed my meal and the music playing :)   although it's a bit pricey it was worth the money   Oh and their chocolate bownie sunday is to die for and its HUGE! need two people to help finish that.

For a chain this was a great experience.   American food outside of America is often kind of gross.  This was decent.   Not excellent but decent.  If this was in the states It May get one less star,  it this one is in Scotland.    The beer selection was underwhelming.  No dark beers on tap.  Out of the darker bottled beers.   Had a "Bourbon" and coke with Jack Daniels.  Jack Daniels isn't technically a bourbon, but close enough.   Also had one of their concoctions.  Was so sweet it should have been a lollipop.    Tried the cauliflower buffalo wings?  Because why not.  It was actually quite good.     The Guinness burger was acceptable.  Good for American food abroad.    My mother's drink was too sweet for her to possibly drink and they took it right off the bill and were very apologetic.     Great staff and management.

I only stopped into the Rock Shop on my most recent visit, but I have dined here on previous visits. This is one of the very few Hard Rock Cafes with a classical interior design & stain glass windows, which you don't see in newly opened or redesigned locations. The restaurant had a great atmosphere with plenty of guests on a Saturday late in the afternoon. The Rock Shop was well stocked & I was able to pick up a shot glass & city design bottle opener.

Typical hard rock, nothing really special compared to the other 20+ hard rocks Ive been to. When I was  here it wasn't very busy at all so service was quick for a drink anyway. Located not far from Rose street and the Royal Mile is a 10min walk away.

My bucket list is to attempt to visit all HRC locations!! So, I'm now crossing off Edinburgh location!  Was thrilled to walk in with my family and enjoy the history of the Cafe. HRC is a unique experience for some, you come for the music, appreciate the history and reminisce past visits. Staff was friendly, food is consistent and was thrilled to pick up some classic pins.

When we first arrived in town we wanted to find the Hard Rock Cafe.  Although a bit pricey for lunch, we really enjoyed our meal and our waiter. We would recommend having lunch or dinner here if you are not on a set budget. Thank you

Burger and cocktails... That's what I wanted and needed. Nothing else was open so I really had limited choice to quench this craving so I ended up here.   Hard rock is a typical chain but what's cool about this place is that it offers a Scottish burger...pretty touristy but at least they tried eh? The Scottish burger of course has haggis with the typical hamburger ingredient. The best part of the burger was the brown sauce that came with it. I'm not sure what it was or what it's made out of but it went really well with the haggis burger. The chips were blah and the cocktail was ok... Huge portion though! If haggis on your burger isn't your thing, they also have a couple of other burgers that sound pretty decent. In addition to burgers, the menu also have pasta and meat dishes as well as many typical American appetisers.   My friend and I also ended up getting dessert... A big bowl of warm brownies with ice cream. Nothing amazing about this desert other than its size.   The staff is cool and there's free wifi-fi. This place isn't really amazing, and a bit over price. Certainly paying for the name and the big portion, cause it's definitely not the flavour of their dishes.

Never thought I'd end up here, but I did. We've been with our arabian friends which seemed to make a good impression. The prices are quite high and I was kind of glad I didn't have to pay :D the fish was delicious, but it was so much that I could not finish it at all!  A quite nice restaurant with good service, but there's comparable food for less money!!

My experience in this hard rock cafe is by far inferior compared to other countries. My recent and (I believe) final visit in Hard Rock Edinburgh was a Saturday afternoon where my friend and I fancied some cocktails along with food so we ended up there (since Fridays have permanently closed). Since we had to wait for our table we decided to had our drinks ordered at the bar: a lime margarita for me and a long island ice tea for my friend. Both standard cocktails to make, yet the bartender failed to do make them good... On the first sip both were tasteless (especially mine).   By this time our table was ready and we moved there, hoping that we could ask our waitress to take care the matter. Our food arrived, yet we weren't asked (as usual) how it was, so we informed our waitress that unfortunately we weren't enjoying our cocktails and we would like to cola colas instead. Yet she didn't express any apology our willingness to resolve this, just asked "so, two cokes?" (for which as expected we were charged on top of the cocktails we left -as you can see in my picture). Usually, in a restaurant that wants to please it costumers they offer to take an item that wasn't satisfying back, offer an alternative or waive the charge to much cheaper options we had to go by. Not at this restaurant... We were really disappointed to choose this place for the cocktails that were such a let down, along with an unhelpful service.

Broke all my rules coming here. Usually avoid chains and especially avoid American chains abroad. But it was cold and rainy in Edinburgh in December (what a surprise!), and I was on a mission to buy a friend a Hard Rock Edinburgh T shirt, so I thought I'd check it out. Given the limited and simplistic menu, and the prices, one would hope they'd go the extra mile to make their simple food special. Nope. To their credit, the hamburger bun was toasted brioche and the hamburger came out hot. The mushrooms were nicely sauteed. However the hamburger was rock hard (methinks machine formed and not enough fat) and cooked well, not medium well as the menu indicated. The Swiss cheese was slapped on and not even melted, making the whole thing fail to gel. The Parmesan fries for a pound extra just had some commercial pre-shredded parmesan dumped on them. Served with plain mayonnaise when a garlic aioli would have been so much better. Edible but with so many great bistros in Georges St, a complete waste of calories.

There was a time, no so long ago, that HRC was my favourite place in Edinburgh.  However - all that made it great for me then has been surpassed and bettered by other venues and also my taste has changed ever so slightly.   I am fed up with the 'Hi my name is Jack and I will be serving you tonight and I'm so jolly matey and pally you want me to become your bestest friend (for the duration of the meal). It is a way of engaging the customers that I think would befit a 5 year old. How novel and quirky it once was to have the whole restaurant and staff sing Happy Birthday I don't feel like joining in anymore and I cannot be the only one. Taking your 5 year old (or anyone under 18)  to HRC is not the done thing in my book - asking other diners to take a meal break and sing for a party of teens. no, no no .  I don't want to hear an infant crying when Red Hot Chili Peppers are doing their thing or Jimi is stoned on stage - That is my  niggly thing -  how and when did it became OK to bring kids to Hard Rock Cafe?  I am so over the 20 flat screens that are on every wall - that was great in the 90's and early 00's but these days I want to focus on my fellow drinkers / diners or even the food I am eating.  What I really liked about it (and still do) is their burgers, yes they are expensive but they do taste great.  That is it. All other parts of it are now found elsewhere - better.   The Music : great tunes and videos, but the constant assault onto my senses is making me feel dizzy, deaf and old. - I have Spotify at home and my local bar sometimes uses my list - I like that better as I can also talk and be heard. so in that sense it makes HRC redundant. I don't need, (made) to watch videos when I am eating or cocktail drinking.   Oh yes the Cocktails: what a shame - their Purple Haze, Gene Simmons' Bloody Mary and Long Island were staunch favourites, somehow over time they've lost their place on the flavour vs price pole position, as I think for example that The Last Word or  Bar Kohl has an up on that and for similar or cheaper prices and delivering better services.   The Hard Rock Buffalo Wings with a choice of 3 sauces is replaced - by WINGS (with a choice of about 50 sauces)  In the Hard Rock Cafe Shop - you can buy T-shirts and Rock Memorabilia - for a price.  With an HRC loyalty / membership card you get a discount on clothing and meals.  If you are a tourist and you are fine with having to pay a premium for a burger and you are used to the American diner service - HRC is your place. If you are like me and have a little more local knowledge about other places it is easy to go here as a place to meet up first before going somewhere else.

I got there on a quiet Monday afternoon, in "hungry" mode and was welcomed by a very friendly & chatty front of house dude who guide to my table.  My server Theresa was cool, professional & efficient, she was the only waitress on the floor at time of the day looking after 5 more tables.   I ordered the Santa Fe Spring Rolls stuffed with spinach, black beans, cilantro, corn, jalapenos, diced red peppers and jack cheese + crispy tortilla straws with a side of Hard Rock salsa and guacamole-chipotle ranch dressing . Starter did the trick as it was a crispy, tasty and abundant portion to placate my momentarily ravenous demons.   As a main course I ordered a Top Sirloin Steak medium rare, a cut which in principle was OK, but not properly seared, probably because the grill was not hot enough (should be, for my personal taste, at least 260oC or more) giving the inside of it the texture and flavour of "boiled meat" rather than grilled.   Meal was washed down with a couple of pints of Becks Vier at  3.80 each..still under the 4 quid mark...what a pleasant surprise... All in all a positive experience, place is baby & family friendly, WiFi is available....and the ubiquitous TV plasma screens showing, yeah... you guess it R & R videos. Enjoy your meal!

I went in with a friend just after they had opened, so they were working out the kinks. We weren't expecting perfect but unfortunately there were some issues.   We were handed to different menus, one being for a midweek 2 course special, and their regular a la carte. It might of been a good idea to label the 2 course special as a tasting menu, as there was a big difference in portion sizes between the two menus.  The food was good, but only good. Stockbridge has a good selection of great restaurants already, so I hope the selection improves.  Time will tell if this restaurant lasts in the very competitive Edinburgh market.

I went to Wolfits to get myself a fast lunch late one day a while back.  I was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food.    I ordered a red onion panini and the Thai red chicken soup.  The soup in particular was quite good - it was well seasoned, and the chicken was good quality meat.  You have the option to get your food to go or stay and eat there at no extra charge.  I decided to stay and very much enjoyed my lunch.  I'll be back!

Great little sandwich shop if you're in the area - make sure you're prepared though, it's cash only! The set-up is a bit confusing - there's no list of filling options anywhere, and items at the counter aren't labelled, so you essentially have to ask what everything is. Once you ask though, you'll find there's a very nice selection of fillings. I bought a toasted wrap with cajun chicken, crispy bacon, applewood smoked cheddar, rocket, pesto, and cranberry sauce. Delicious wrap, and only 3 (much cheaper than many of the spots nearby). My co-worker got soup and said it was quite nice as well.  Certainly will be going back next time I'm working nearby, and certainly recommended!

Honestly, I'm surprised I've not got round to reviewing Wolfits yet as I'm in here often enough!  Wolfits is one of those lunch places for office workers where you can order a sandwich, a baked potato, soup, or a big bowl of salad. They have a pretty decent selection of fillings too, much wider than a lot of similar establishments, which is what really makes Wolfits a good choice at lunch time. Not to mention the portions are very generous, a salad bowl could easily do you two lunches and the number of additions you can make is huge.  More often than not I pop by and pick up a soup. I tend to veer towards lentil, or lentil and bacon, and 9 times out of 10 it's a tasty, thick soup. Coupled with a buttered half baguette and I've spent less than 2.50 on a really filling lunch.  Due to its superiority over other make-your-own-sandwich shops, it does get very busy around 1pm, but the queue moves quickly as there are usually several members of staff on hand to help. It's definitely going to be my 'go-to' place for a quick lunch so long as I continue working in the area.

I do love a good sandwich bar.  There are loads springing up, along the lines of what is provided by Subway and Baguette Express.  Wolfits, on Rose Street, is one of these.  They offer a wide range of sandwiches, paninis and wraps, all made fresh on the day.  They can also make these to order.  They also do other hot food, like breakfasts and bacon rolls, so will cater for most of your snack-based needs.  Prices seemed to be reasonable, and the range of fillings and things available will easily compete with some of the larger high street chains.  I suspect that this is the sort of place that will get heard about by word of mouth, and that you will want to keep visiting.  I only sat in to get out of a heavy rainstorm with a refreshing drink of, funnily enough, water.  This gave me ample time to have a look round  the shop, and take in what was going on.    I was very impressed - clean and modern with a great range of stuff to eat.  Give them a go if you're ever on Rose Street and need somewhere to eat.

Wolfits is competing with many sandwich bars in this area, but it does a bloody good job!  Selling sandwiches and panini's etc, Wolfits manage to cater for an amazing variety of tastes by offering fillings from brie to salami! You can opt to keep it plain and no frills or you can deck your sandwich out in loads of healthy and continental fillings. They do salads with a number of garnishes too if you are looking to get some of your five a day.  If you really don't fancy being healthy, they also have a huge selection of temptingly cheap breakfast rolls. If you're going to go down the fry up road, you might as well get a double up. Go on, treat yourself!  Teas, coffee's and hot chocolates are all cheap and tasty. The staff are efficient and although this place is busy, indicating that it's good, you're not left hanging around unassisted for too long. More upmarket and contemporary than a lot of sandwich bars, Wolfits nevertheless offer hearty, simple rolls. A safe bet for any hungry citizen of Edinburgh!

Wolfits is one of many sandwich and salad bars in Edinburgh, but it is worth a visit. Situated on Rose Street, Wolfits is right in the centre of the city and it is just around the corner from the main shopping area in Edinburgh, Princes Street, and so it is a convenient place to reach.   They serve a whole range of sandwiches, baguettes and rolls, as well as lots of salad options and soup. I have been here several times over the last few weeks to buy my lunch. They have a deli type section displaying a range of filings such as meats, cheeses and salad. I have played it pretty safe here and stuck to their steak and cheese baguette, which is really tasty and very well priced at less than 3! Breakfast rolls are also available here so it would be a good place to stop by for a bacon roll in the morning.   This store is pretty much an extension of the big sandwich chains such and Quinzo's Subs and Subway, but if you want to buck the trend and buy your baguette from a local business, Wolfits is definitely the place to go.

I spent my honeymoon in Edinburgh in September. We stayed at the Caledonian, so we found ourselves strolling down Rose St. every day. After two days of passing, we decided Wolfits looked like an easy bite to eat one morning. It was difficult to tell what we could actually put on our sandwiches--where were the labels? Our sandwiches were good, although my silly husband thought it would be a good idea to drink coffee and put jalapenos (chilis in Edinburgh terms) on his sandwich before starting out our day of exploring on a unseasonably warm day. "Sweat, baby, sweat"  I got my dose of UK gossip as I flipped through a trashy newspaper and watched music videos on the TV. This is a nice little stop if you need a sandwich, soup, salad or coffee.  Alas, there isn't wi-fi.

So far so good. I've been here a couple times, firstly because i was very hungover, wanted a panini and couldn't find the place i was planning on going so i went here.  I asked for a bacon, brie and cranberry panini, but they were out of paninis (it was about 3pm so this was fair enough), but she gave me a couple of other options and i had a toasted baguette instead. No complaints at all and it was delicious.  Second time was on my lunch break at work. I asked for the same again (creature of habit) but this time they didn't have any brie. I was a little saddened by this, but i prompted them for substitute suggestions and we decided upon mozzarella. It wasn't the same but still tasty.  It is pretty much like most sandwich shops, they the staff are lovely and friendly, prices are fair (panini was 2.85) and there is a wide selection to choose from. So far so good anyway :)

Having worked in various locations around central Edinburgh over the years, I like to try out the local Sandwich shops that cater to my lunchtime needs, and out of them all, Wolfits gets my top spot.  Now, this isnt fancy dining, this is soups, sandwiches, salads, paninis, baked tatties etc, so it's simple food, but I constantly have my mind blown at how easily people cock this type of thing up.  There is a lot of competition in the area, from similar independent shops to chains such as Pret, Baguette Express and Boots.  Where Wolfits excels is the quality and variety of the ingredients, the professionalism of the staff (hygienic, friendly, efficient), the presentation of the results, the size of the portions and the price which all in all offers great value for money.  They have a variety of soups, all thick, fresh and tasty which is a welcome change from the watered down nonsense that is all too common.  They have a variety of sandwiches and salad pre made, but they will custom make anything you want, and have a range of rolls/baguettes too. For both the salads and sandwiched there is about as big a selection of salad and deli items that you could want (all laid out for you to easily see) along with a good range of dressings too.   There's nothing mind-blowing about what these guys do, they provide the same breakfast and lunchtime staples that a thousand other bushinesses in Edinburgh offer, the difference is the variety and quality means these guys do it better than just about anyone else.
bacon and egg rolls.  brown sauce.  yum.  (as you can probably tell, i've yet to try a sandwich from here... )

I used to make this my regular lunch stop when it first opened!  The soups are not what they could be, the fillings all rather dull! Just not very bexciting or special if i compare to the like of Bread&Olive.  Needs a good kick up the backside in my opinion!

Of the many sandwich/baguette/roll shops in central Edinburgh, this one seems decent enough. The only things I've tried are the steak baguettes - well priced at 2.95 and they avoid falling into the steak so tough you need a lion's jaws to digest them trap - and one or two of the paninis and fruit salads.   I certainly go here quite often.

The Barrelhouse is a recent addition to the Edinburgh bar scene, previously was Jocks Lodge, a bar that was to be avoided. Now has the same owner as the highly successful Espy in Portobello. Managed by Richard and his crew, they won Bar of the year from the Star Pubs organisation (in spite of some fierce competition from the other 500 bars in the group) who are their landlords. The pub is a slightly quirky addition to the Edinburgh pub scene, with a solid real ale selection, and some great whiskies and gins. The menu is a diverse and changes regularly. Well worth checking out.

Wow! I know it's not fair to credit somewhere because of inadequacies of its predecessors but Barrelhouse deserves lots of credit for taking on the poison chalice of the infamous Jock's Lodge, nightmare mafia pub. So now we have a cool southern US style BBQ joint which does great food with excellent service. Big portions - wings, burgers, etc - at a reasonable cost (burger 8). Kids options (3). Reasonable beers. Decent coffee. No wi-fi as yet and cash only but BT is promised to be booked in. Loved it here.

How does this place not have more reviews?! We were staying a the hotel down the block from Chop House and decided to have it as our first dinner in Edinburgh as we woke up from our afternoon naps. This. Place. Is. Bomb.  We were seated at the bar since we did not have a reservation. The bartender was very attentive and patient with our questions on the menu. 1. Scallop & pig cheek starter - So the pig cheek looks like bacon when it comes but can you imagine something more delicious than bacon? It's pig cheek. You have to get it. 2. Bone-in rib - We got the smallest portion since it was just 2 girls but it was a good size where we can barely finish it by stuffing ourselves. We both wished it was done a bit more rare (the hostess did recommend it at medium). Otherwise great flavor and texture. 3. Beef dripping mushrooms - A bit too salty but goes well with the steak 4. Oysters - We couldn't help but ordered 2 local oysters at the end of our meal even though they were a bit expensive at 2.5 gbp per. They were creamy, flavorful, meaty, delicious and fresh. If I were any richer (or more hungry), I would've ordered a dozen for myself. They make their own mignonette in-house from scratch!!!  The bill was definitely smaller than I expected since, in my opinion, we kinda went all out. Great service. Great food. Great vibe. Would recommend in a heartbeat to anyone.

I had a nice meal here last weekend but I admit to being torn between three and four stars.   The food was quite good, though in the case of the starters and sides I'd say they were quite pricey for quantity (2.50 for a single tempura prawn, for example) and over-salted.   We each had a cocktail which were delicious and probably the creative highlight of the evening.   Two starters, two tempura prawns, two mains, two cocktails, one glass of wine and one dessert - 100. It was never going to be a cheap night out but I do find that on the steep side.   I was a bit disappointed about being told halfway through the meal that we only had the table for two hours. As we neared our two hour limit, we were reminded again and invited to shift to the bar. I could have understood enforcing this rule if there was actually someone waiting for our table, but there wasn't. We both would have liked an after dinner drink but decided against sitting at the bar to do so.   All in all not a bad experience but not necessarily somewhere I would rush back to, but for the drinks. Definitely high marks on the drinks.

Clock this.  As with their other outlets, the Clock on the Shore is the way to go to score a great Breakfast / Brunch / Lunch. Cheap and great quality ingredients.   The Shore one is brilliantly located in the 'Clock Tower' and this just adds to the feel of authenticity, as if it has always been there.   The staff are always very cheery and polite. During lunchtimes it may get a bit busy so expect a little wait, but they seem to keep their act together.  They also do pre catering orders and take away, but myself I have yet to use these services.  Good business, good spot, good pricing.

Although a trifle underwhelming, you're not going to go too far wrong at The Clock. Dishes are to a good standard, and the welcome is friendly. Reliable, if unspectacular.  Overall, we said: "The Clock is really pretty smart, continues to be very popular, and is a good lunchtime stop. Its offerings didn't unduly quicken my pulse, but they provided good wholesome fare, and, with the warmth of the welcome, set me on my way with a smile upon my face."

Considering the number of times that I visit The Clock, I don't rate it that highly... am I mad?  Totally, but that doesn't take away from the fact that I can a) park around the corner quite easily and b) always get a quick lunch here that satisfies my basic hunger  The staff are nice & friendly, but the soup is often flavour-less and the baked potatoes are really hit or miss - quite often I've gotten home to find that my tattie is uncooked in the middle. (I'm an old-fashioned, proper oven-baked to within a "skin" of it's life-potato gal).  The wrap & sandwich selection look much better, but I'm not big on bread... perhaps that's where I'm going wrong?!   I would still recommend for a quick grab & run lunch in Leith... and the service has pushed up a 2star to a 3star... I'm nice like that!

Excellent little corner sandwich/soup/coffee shop. They have a great, unique selection of pre-made, fresh sandwiches ready for the go and soup...   I've gone back multiple times simply for the soups, which are in my unbiased opinion some of the best soups I've had in Edinburgh. You can't go wrong with these soups, made fresh from scratch everyday, and always very warmly, wholesome, warm, and tasty. I've tried all of the following and not been disappointed: Leek and Potato, French Onion, Chunky Vegetable, Lentil and Veg, Cauliflower and Veg. Get the soup!  My only complaint is the seating: it's limited to about four or five stools that face the window and one round table with a few chairs around it.   Otherwise, great place for a quick coffee or quality deli sandwich and SOUP. Just keep in mind if you're planning on siting in you may be out of luck when it's busy.

Looking out on to Leith Docks, Clock certainly boasts some great views.   The sandwiches here attract all the nearby  industrial and corporate attention.  After tasting a chorizo, Mexican cheese and salsa roll I was unsurprised at the afore mentioned attention.  There's a range of good deli's scattered around Edinburgh, and Clock can be proud to be one of them. The staff are talkative and inviting too.   Top stuff.

I nice little sandwich/coffee shop near the river. I was in Edinburgh on business staying at the Malmaison Hotel about a block away.  The Clock became a regular stop on my way to work every morning.  Friendly Staff Good espresso A small selection of pastries. But the best was the sausage sandwiches with HP sauce.

This is an excellent sandwich bar in an upcoming area of Edinburgh. The Clock is great for lunch. They offer the usual freshly made sandwich concept that most sandwich bars offer but the fillings are particularly good.   The soups are also excellent, they have three different ones on each day and are all freshly made.   The staff are very friendly and always really pleasant when serving you.   The only thing I can fault is the extra cost if you want to sit in and there is no free wi-fi. Other than that, I really recommend this place for lunch.

Given that they're more or less opposite my place of work, the convenience of this place is hard to beat.   But they also serve a fine latte and have a brilliant selection of quirky lunchtime choice on offer, either freshly prepared or lying freshly ready to snatch up and guzzle down in their chiller cabinet. So reasonably regularly, this might include felafel salad boxes, tortilla slices, soup (though not in the chiller cabinet), quiche, all kinds of homemade cakes and sandwiches including my new favourite combining parma ham, mozzarella and rocket.   They also have a fine array of drinks including enough flavoured waters to keep the most discerning and vitamin deficient drinker happy.
Today I went to get a small soup from The Clock- I recieved a cup of cold liquid, which had clearly been watered down. For 1.20 I am unimpressed!

A favourite lunchtime haunt of local office workers, this deli on the crossroads of The Shore, Bernard Street and Commercial Street has a daily changing menu of delicious takeaway treats. There is a choice of two homemade soups every day and a hot meal as well as an astounding range of sandwich fillings to fill every type of bread you could think of. The serving team are friendly and efficient, dealing with the inevitable queues politely and quickly. The meatballs are particularly delicious and, heaped onto a baked potato on a cold winter's day, these will warm you up for the rest of the afternoon.

It's really close to my work so I used to get lunch here a lot. Their sandwiches and soups are usually quite tasty. However, one day my colleague bought a baked potato and coleslaw there and the coleslaw was mouldy. I will never go back now...

Awesome banquet meal! 12 each every Sunday. Had never hard of this place until a few ago and now I'm a regular.  Lovely naan bread, nice starters and fragrant currys they have. A tapas Indian style.  Great evening out and a great meal.

Jashans it is you, not me. Over the last few weeks I have been making an effort to try new and different curry places, sadly this has had a knock on effect. Jashans just isn't as good as many of the options on Gorgie or Dalry road, which are both easily within walking distance and deliver to the area. I'm going to do a bit of a deconstruction, so here are the places that for me Jashans has got it wrong:  1. The takeaway set meal - normal practice, if a set meal is offered in an Indian is to provide a starter, a classic curry (the ones everyone has heard of) and some sort of rice or nan offering. This is not the case in Jashans. It is just 1 standard starter, main, side and rice + plain nan. The lack of variance means you won't take advantage of the set meal very often...  2. It is expensive. All the curry shops in the area are cheaper and most are at least as good or (more likely) better. for example 3.25 for pilau rice, one of the most expensive I have seen!  3. Still on rice, I just don't like their pilau (something in the flavour) and tried the ghee batt (3.50, for rice fried in ghee with onion) as a replacement. Sadly this was a clean white colour, that tasted a little of ghee, but didn't look fried.  Ok, that is my big three, but I have an overall sense that Jashans perhaps believe they don't need to compete, being the only Indian on Slateford Road and hey they seem to have got away with it this long. Thing is I have no issue walking an extra 10 minutes, heck it might even make the curry a bit healthier, or so I will tell myself. The curry itself is still ok, but this curry lover has found better options so I doubt I'll be back.

We recently moved to this part of town and are venturing to try to find our new local spots for lazy night take out. I love Indian and would argue it is something that never tastes the same at home, but my experience at Jashans made me think differently. We called on a Friday night, and granted, probably the busiest night for take-out, but there phone manor was very rushed and not very organised, as my boyfriend was passed to two different people, and then someone tried to dial out while we were on the line. They said delivery would take an hour, so we opted to collect it, as I was to hungry to wait.  We order garlic naan, butter chicken, potatoes/okra and onion bhaji. It did come well presented and neatly packed, but needless to say, the food was so disappointing. It didn't taste bad, but it certainly did not taste like Indian food. Mine was suppose to be medium, but was super oily and had no spice or real flavour to speak of. It was like tomato paste and oil had been partly mixed in, but nothing else, and the okra had no flavour. I don't eat meat, but I tried the sauce for the butter chicken and it tasted just like honey, and no spice there either. My boyfriend said the chicken tasted overcooked and he was no impressed with my dish either.   The naan was very dry and lacked any hit of garlic, which was super disappointing. The onion bhaji tasted nice, but could have been crispier. It did some with some nice sauces, but not sure what they were, some sort of mild chili sauce maybe?  Overall, it wasn't a good experience and for over 20, it definitely wasn't worth it. As nothing made an impression on us, we aren't keen to go back and give it a second chance. I read the reviews beforehand and since they are seem fairly positive I was surprised it was so far from the taste I was expecting. I would not recommend this place to anyone, and will continue my search for good take out near by.

I do love this place but I'm only going for 4 stars as this review is based on takeaway, not the full restaurant experience.  It has been opened now for about a year and replaced Oscars on Slateford Road. There is a restaurant which seems to do pretty good business. I popped in before 7 on a Friday for a takeaway and it was pretty full which is always a good sign, with lots of other popping in to collect takeaway too.  Their takeaways are awesome. First visit at New Years was for meal deal for 2 and we added extra bits (pakora, naan, extra rice) on to make it a meal for 3 - seriously, there was tons of food, even feeding three with pub munchies, meant there was still another meal and a bit left for another day. Meat is cooked amazingly - we had a chicken korma and there was a lamb dish with mint whose name escapes me. I would never order lamb normally and didn't intend on even trying it but it was awesome. Totally melt in the mouth gorgeousness.   I tried to look for it last night but probably missed it on the menu due to tiredness and starvation so I opted for a chicken dupiaza. It was lovely, subtly spiced tomatoey sauce with huge chunks of tender chicken and slices of red and green peppers and onions - yum! I ordered boiled rice to go with it and when I opened the bag at home, not only did I have my order, but a 2 little tubs containing a chopped onion salad and some mango chutney. I think this is a Jashans thing as there is always some kind of salad and sauce thing that comes extra which is a nice touch.   So, yep, Jashans is worth checking out. There are deals on for the restaurant on Sundays, and lunchtimes during the week,if you fancy a bargain lunch treat. The staff are lovely and the restaurant is really nicely decorated, very modern, but with lots of red, orange and gold accents to reflect the Indian and Bangladeshi theme.

it was sunday night, it was late, it was cold, it had been snowing on and off all weekend, neither me or my boyfriend could face cooking dinner so we decided to finally try jashans which had opened up down the street from his flat a number of months ago.  we phoned our order in and headed over to pick it up.  i was a bit shocked entering the restaurant itself, as it really rather quite posh looking.  all rich sumptious colours and dark wooden tables.  i was definitely impressed, perhaps less so when we had at least three different waiters come up to us to ask what our take away order was.  um we already ordered and we are just waiting for the food now... it also took about three attempts to pay.  about 10 minutes after our arrival though, we had paid and the food was brought to us and we hopped in the car to head home.  i unpacked the items which included poppadums, onion salad, garlic chicken, green herb chicken, saag aloo, pilau rice, and a peshwari naan.  i did like that the food came in tupperwares which meant for less chance of an accidental spillage while carrying it from car to flat, but i found that the food was barely on the hot side, more warm moving to room temperature.  to be fair the curries were perfectly nice and i really enjoyed the naan, it was lovely and coconuty and sweet but without that weird hideous orange dyed coconut colour that you usually get.  but i felt like this place fell short of the other amazing curry houses that edinburgh has to offer as i can really only describe my meal as nice and not overly memorable.  it was also a bit more expensive than i would have expected for a takeaway.  so sadly, it's only A-OK and i may encourage my boyfriend to order from a different establishment the next time we opt for an indian to take away.

I came alone for an early dinner after traveling all day, there were Indian restaurants all around, but I just so happened to stop by in here because it was recommended to me. It was quiet and I was the only customer inside until I was nearing the time to leave when a couple came in, too.   I got a mango lassi, which is always my favorite, can't go wrong with a lassi. Also, I got lamb tikka masala, the sauce was so well prepared and tasty. However, the lamb itself felt a bit overlooked? Possibly dry? I would say that the sauce made up for it because it was hands down the best flavor I've ever had. I also got it paired with rice, which strangely I found wasn't included in the meal? I know it is another way to make money, but why would someone have just ordered a bunch of sauce and 5 cubes of meat. I feel like the rice should be included, because that's the meal. Regardless, it was worth the extra 3 in my opinion to complete the meal.  Although the waiter was a bit inattentive and had to be called over for everything I wanted, we did have a nice chat and he brought what I asked for. Also, he boxed up my extra food when I was leaving, and put it in a bag with a spoon for me, which was nice. Lastly,  I got galub jamin (spelling?) for dessert, and they were amazing. Best dessert I'd had in weeks maybe. They were so sweet and soft and I could have eaten possibly 4 more orders to myself!

My family and I were visiting Edinburgh for a few days and happened to walk by Golden Ambal on our first evening - so glad we stopped in!! We ordered the lamb biryani, chicken tikka masala, a masala dosa, and a piece of naan to go. Everything was super flavorful and delicious. Also, our order was done really quickly, and I thought the prices were really reasonable too. We only saw the top level of the restaurant, which is just a few tables, but I think they have more tables downstairs. I've tried a lot of Indian restaurants before and this was the best I've had in a long time!

After a busy day of baking 500 cupcakes (don't ask) I was needing feeding and I was in the mood for a curry. Our local favourite had recently closed so we needed to find somewhere new. The spot which is now the Golden Ambal has changed hands several times in the last year so we were a bit skeptical but based on recent Yelp reviews we decided to give it a shot.   I ordered the Paneer Dosa and a side Makhani lentils. David had a lamb dish and a naan, we shared some onion pakoras too. We ordered a collection on JustEat and our order was ready to pick up from the friendly staff in snazzy gold waistcoats when we arrived.   The food - tremendous!! My dosa was light and the filling beautifully flavoured. All the accompaniments came individually packaged and included a delicious home made mango chutney. Far better than the sickly sweet jarred stuff. The onion pakoras were light, tasty and not soaked in grease. David lamb was amazingly tender and in a rich spicy gravy. The star of the show were my lentils. They were awesome! So rich,creamy and delicately spiced.   We were both very pleasantly suprised with the food and the price, coming in at under 20.  I hope it stays around longer than it's previous owners as we have found our new favourite!  Cheers, Amy

This has been a tricky spot in recent times, with three restaurants failing in this spot in the last three years. Fingers crossed for Golden Ambal because I was quite a fan when I visited for lunch. The lunch deal was very good value and the a la carte menu looked to hold some potentially interesting dishes. Worth a go, I'd say.  Overall, we said: "I was highly pleased with Golden Ambal. This hasn't been a fortunate location, but this iteration is well-equipped to flourish as the fare on offer is very good. I look forward to visiting again, particularly to give their dosas a try. I'd recommend a visit."

I'd been eager to check out Norn since it took over from the Plumed Horse location earlier this year and hearing a lot of good things. It's a high-end restaurant that does some stunning food, and it was fantastic.   You don't really get a choice on what you eat here for dinner, only how many courses; 4 courses for 40 or 7 courses for 65 (which is comparatively good value). I think if you come here you really owe it to yourself to go all in and get 7 if you can, because you'll want to try everything on offer.   The menu is pleasingly unfussy. It comes on a little folded up bit of paper simply outlining the ingredients e.g 'mushroom, turnip, cheese'. You don't have to spend the first part of dinner on google trying to decipher gastro food speak.  Each plate of food was delicious and beautifully presented. The chefs will come out to the table and talk you through the dish, and even some of the story behind how they were conceived. The mushroom and the lamb dishes were highlights, and the buttermilk dessert held it's own against the rest of the meal. We didn't go for the matching wines but were talked through the wine menu to help pick a nice bottle. We also went for a cheese course to share (an extra 10) and did not regret it.  The venue itself is relaxed. It's surprisingly bright and well lit; it's not a cosy dinner by candlelight kind of place. It's simple, minimal and not too fussily decorated; the food is the focal point here. It was a little cold inside, especially sitting near the door, but improved as more people came in.   It can book up well in advance but for a great dining experience it's definitely worth it. I hope to come back for lunch which at 20 seems like a bargain.

Norn seems to be the restaurant that everyone in Edinburgh is talking about at the moment, so I knew we just had to go along for dinner when we were in town for the weekend. We'd booked back in July so had no issues getting a table but I believe that's changed now and you'll might have to wait a while for a booking.   We arrived right on time for our booking and were shown to our table which had a good view into the open kitchen. The decor is very basic, stark and minimalist - I quite liked it as there's no frills or pretentiousness. It actually feels quite casual and the staff were all chatty and warm, so a nice relaxing vibe for a Saturday night meal.   For dinner, there's two options - a 4 course menu for 40pp or 7 courses for 65. Seeing as we weren't sure when we'd be back, we went for 7 courses. There's the option of matching wines but I just had a cocktail and a glass of wine as I went as I wasn't sure I could drink that much (...again, anyway - we'd had dinner at the Kitchin with matching wines the night before).  The menu is very simple - doesn't tell you much about what you'll be getting but we aren't fussy eaters and don't have dietary requirements so just went along for the ride. Firstly, we were treated to a bonus course of a carrot dish with oyster which was a light, refreshing start to the meal. I liked how all the dishes were introduced by a different chef. The bread and butter was absolutely delicious. The bread they served is made with a wheat which is only milled off the coast of Scotland with a nicely whipped butter beautifully presented.   So onto the tasting menu - 1. Mackerel, tomato, squash, onion. Plump pieces of fish and tangy tomato was a delicious start and this is probably one of my favourite dishes of the night. There's no OTT presentation here - just perfect crockery and relaxed plating.  The next dish was my other favourite purely because it was a real surprise. 2. Halibut, cauliflower, cobnut and nut milk. I'd never order this because I hate cauliflower but actually, the cauliflower in this dish was delicious! Finally. I love being impressed by a dish so much that it changes my opinion of an ingredient.   The rest of the dishes (see pictures attached):   3. Venison, celeriac, sorrel 4. Guinea fowl, cabbage, barley, corn 5. Beef, kale, turnip  We couldn't resist the addition of the bonus cheese course here even though I was already bursting!  6. Plum, buttermilk, fennel 7. Bramble, chocolate, bay, lemon  I won't go into details about the rest of the menu as I think I'll exceed the word limit. But I do have to say that this meal is the kind of meal I feel like I'm constantly looking for - unusual combinations of flavours, impressive taste and lots of surprises. That's what makes a good meal for me. There was only one dish for me which wasn't totally perfect which was the third one as I think my portion didn't have enough celeriac (or apple, whatever the small cubes were). But that is the most minor of complaints in an otherwise perfect lineup of dishes.   Notes:   * the menu is seasonal and I believe it changes at least weekly. There's no menu on their website. As I said, we don't have dietary requirements and pretty much eat everything, so we were happy to be surprised. I'd recommend calling them if you do have a particular requirement/question.   * it's a casual restaurant - I was wearing a nice dress but with sneakers as I had sore feet and I didn't feel out of place.   * they also offer a really great priced lunch menu - 3 courses for 20 which I really want to get back to try, now that I've been and seen just how good it is.

The Slug and Lettuce in the Omni centre is a decent enough pub for one that belongs to a chain. The decor is pretty standard for this type of pub, with large squishy sofas and comfy seats to encourage you to stay longer. As with all chain pubs, it's slightly lacking in atmosphere and the bar staff aren't terribly friendly, but no worse than i expected.   The drinks are a bit more expensive than other places in the Omni Centre, but watch out for their promotions as there is always something on special offer. The food is over priced and really of a pretty poor standard. There are so many other places to eat in the centre that taste nicer and are much better value, so i generally avoid eating here.

This is a good place to go and relax after work but it's irritating how they do table service in some parts of it as you end up waiting for ages sometimes and they don't like it if you go up to the bar to buy drinks seperately!   However it's still good for a couple of drinks and their chips with tikka sauce is great it's about 3 but you get a huge bowl of them!

Slug and Lettuce... what an awesome name, I wanted to like this bar so much more than I actually did but unfortunately it was just a bit too flat for my liking. Sure, it's not bad for a swift drink but it's really nothing to write home about unfortunately. The decor is very modern and minimal and the prices are quite reasonable too but it just doesn't have any real atmosphere or charm that would make me want to come back time and time again.
Not bad for a chain pub. Huge food portions and comfy seating. Best bar in the Omni Centre, and rarely too busy.
Food's okay but for up market pub grub I think it's a little steep. There's a nice comfy atmosphere and it's in a handy location a little further on from Prices Street and all the shops.
For such a central bar, reasonable prices, and great wine. Defintiely check out mid-week deals, such as any bottle of wine for 10 on Wednesdays. We may have made too good sue of that one!

i like this pub/restaurant. Nice surroundings and food not bad either. mid priced - good for something to eat before the theatre or after the shops. Access to car park without having to go outside as it is in the omni centre. always nice and clean and set out so there are lots of areas for a chat. Do a good range of snacks as well as meals
A great family resteraunt to go to located in the omni centre.It has friendly staff and theres always great offers on even through the week.The staff are also approachable.

Not a bad chain pub. It's reasonably priced with a good selection of food on the menu. Of course it is the usual heated up fayre you normally get in chain pubs but that seems to be the norm rather than the exception these days. All in all a great place to stop in for a bite to eat and a drink when enjoying a day shopping in Edinburgh.

To be fair, I've only ever eaten at the Slug and Lettuce on their half price Mondays. I think it's a bargain for the amount of food you get, but if I were paying full price, it would be a tad too expensive for what you get. Overall, staff are always as attentive as possible, considering it can be quite busy on a Monday with all the penny pinchers like me!

The Slug and Lettuce is fine for a drink before or after the cinema but it has no real character or charm, as with most chain pubs. I had the worst nachos here, they used flavoured Doritos instead of plain nachos and there was hardly any salsa or sour cream, it was really just a plate of dry Doritos. It was very disappointing and I won't eat here again. There are so many pubs in Edinburgh with character and atmosphere and this one just didnt stand out in any way for me. The sofas were comfy though.

The Slug in the Omni centre is a great little pub. The drinks and food are part of usual fare you get. The atmosphere of the pub is really nice. It's central, great to meet people, with plenty of options around to continue the night. Sitting on the sofa's out the main door is great for people watching. Good place to visit!
This is a great bar for pre-theatre at the Playhouse. Food is distinctly bar food and average but does the trick. Friendly staff but chaotic service or no service at all if they are busy!

Overall not impressed. I wasn't really expecting very much and certainly wasn't disappointed. The cocktails were cheap, so that was good but as I ordered the same one each time they all tasted very different as did my friends, food took an age to arrive ( I think about 40 mins) and it was fine. All of the staff chatting round one end of the bar however wasn't fine, I know it was a Sunday but if you are working pay your clients some attention! Overall the decor is nice, the food is fine, tastyish and cheap but service terrible x

For some reason my friend always wants to go here for drinks, even though it's in the omni centre. I think the reason might be the half price cocktails! :D I don't really like the omni centre because it's full of expensive fast-food chains, the slug and lettuce is the best option from all of them. It looks more charming and relaxed than the other places, and the food isn't horrible. With the look and feel of the place, I kind of expected a classier menu, but it is just pub food! Don't be fooled :) The 2 for 1 cocktail deal is really the reason to go here with a group of girls, not the atmosphere or the food. The cocktails are delivered quick, they're cheap and they're well tasty :)

The slug and lettuce is good for food but having tried every mocktail available, all 4 of them I have yet to find one that doesn't make the back of my throat feel like I've swallowed razor blades and disappointing that a virgin pina colada isn't on the menu, and I'm no snob but sometimes the clientele of the slug and lettuce is like a night out in Mood. This would be on the bottom of my list of places to go. Harsh but True.

Slug & Lettuce makes me think of a restaurant in an airport.  The food is alright, I enjoyed my Italian Burger, a chicken breast with pesto, mozzarella and tomato. The chips let it down a lot. I wasn't impressed by anything they brought out but I was filled with chicken so fairly satisfied. It was a bit pricey given the quality though.Think Wetherspoons-esque menu but a burger is a tenner.   Cocktails are half price at the weekends. There's a decent selection but honestly Ms. Lightweight over here could barely feel them. They were tasty in that 'Sugar is tasty' way.   The restaurant and the bar are separated, which I approve of and the tables and chairs were well spaced out. We didn't have anyone earwigging and it was easy to ignore those around us. The whole place has a 'modern' look to it, which is where I get my airport impression. You can tell they've gone for simple and reasonably minimalist but didn't want to go too far. The crowd was mainly tourists it seems, with a few locals, particularly large groups of wine drinking middle aged women. There was a few lads dotted around who I imagine would be 'suits' Monday-Friday. They clearly get a lot of the out-to-the-cinema trade too.  The staff were lovely. They were clearly run off their feet but they were on the ball and friendly whenever they came over or we called them while they were in the middle of something. There was even some banter.  Overall it was a decent meal in a decent place but if I had a choice I'd head somewhere with more character.

many years ago i crossed the thershold of Slug and Lettuce for a post movie drink on a sort of date/sort of not a date evening.  the venue was fine, my gin and tonic was fine but besides that i can't really remember much else.  however i was pleasantly surprised when i crossed the threshold again this past friday for pre movie dinner and drinks with some friends.  the place itself has had a massive refurb (i think quite recently...) so it's now all bring colours and fancy light fixtures.  the refurb has really made it into a nice light space which if i recall correctly is certainly an improvement from itself previous look.  now coming to a chain restaurant i don't set my expectations high.  food is usually standard and very often not made entirely on the premises.  so with this in mind we looked over the food menu and decide to share the poppy seed crown with warm manchego fondue and veggie crudites and a  chicken flatbread tostada between three of us.  this was accompained by a few cocktails as their whole cocktail menu is half price on friday!  normally i probably wouldn't have bothered as their cocktails are fairly pricey- nothing under the 8 mark on the menu, but half priced meant i could basically get two for the price of one.  food arrived and we were pleasantly surprised by how tasty it was.  the manchego fondue was quite nice although came in a rather small pot for a sharing dish.  the poppy seed crown was warm and although possibly just heated up in the oven seemed it could also have been fresh baked.  the flatbread tostada was more like a wrap that had been topped with some chicken and cheese/artichoke spread then slightly warmed.  it was ok, fairly tasty but not by any means amazing.  since all this sharing meant small portions we decided to have dessert as well and i ordered the chocolate and caramel bar.  this actually turned out to be incredibly good with a nice balance of rich chocolate and salted caramel toffee sauce in the middle.  it was also a good portion size that would make it ideal for sharing.  after finishing off our second cocktail we paid our bill and were on our way.  while two courses and two cocktails only came to 20 i'm not sure how value this was for money.  the cocktails were just ok with my passionfruit bellini tasty mostly of sugary passionfruit syrup and less of the actual prosecco.  the amaretto sour i had was nice but again not very strong on the alcohol front.  so overall for a chain restaurant this place is decent, it has good menu options and half priced cocktails on a friday.  it's definitely a step up from the nearby wetherspoons and i'd happy go here for a quick cheap eat before a movie again.

I don't mind this pub as maybe I should do. The whole thing is very easy-wipe pleasant with no real heart and soul. The surroundings aren't bad and everything's mid priced.  It's main selling point is that its convenient for a wee glass of inoffensive wine before the cinema, but if you're not pushed for time then just toddle along to broughton street where everythings a bit more special. Fit for purpose non the less.

The Slug & Lettuce is modern with lots of nice cozy sofas and plump chairs to relax in after a hard days shopping over the road at Harvey Nicks.  This bar is in the Omni Centre so its really handy for having a swift pint or two before watching a movie or grabbing a bite to eat at our fav tapas, La Tasca.  They have a full menu but we've only had the starters here - they were pretty tasty though. Service is good and the barstaff are always pleasant.   There's parking right underneath as well which is a plus in this city !!!

Located in the Omni Centre, this bar is ideal for something to drink or eat before the cinema or theatre. As Michael said, there is plenty of nice big leather sofas to collapse into for a night of drinking.   It is like Wetherspoons but one up the posh scale. I haven't eaten here but have seen a lot of cheap deals on Student Beans for this chain, so might be worth a go. There isn't anything overly special or exciting about this bar. Just a standard bar with comfy sofas selling reasonably priced drinks and food.

I arrived at the Slug and Lettuce having spent roughly 6 or 7 hours in a car home from Alton Towers. I had a numb bum, tired eyes and a rumbly tummy so we decided something quick and easy will do. My friend was desperate for a Sunday Roast so this place fitted the bill.  Or so we thought, after being shown to a table and deciding on what we wanted we were told there was no Sunday Roast left...... I saw his eyes sink a little. Gutted. On a side note, please either decide if you are going to have table service or order at the bar, I find the mix of the two really rather bizzare.  So, I ordered a Mojito as cocktails are half price at the weekends!? Meh, I would not have it again if I were to return. It was a little lacklustre. I then had a butternut squash, spinach and goats cheese lasagne - sounds yum, tasted yum. Up until an hour or so later, I did not feel well and having eaten nothing else I can't see what else could have made me feel so queasy. Rather disappointing really, wish I had gone somewhere a little more exciting.

Distinctly tepid soup, an eclectic car-crash menu, and friendly but slow service. This is not the recipe for a happy lunchtime.  Overall, we said: "the Slug & Lettuce wasn't great. They absolutely, categorically need to chop their menu at least in half, if not further than that. They have eight different burger options, sitting next to a similar number of curry options, sitting next to a broad range of pasta options, and from what I could see, none of it looked too appetizing. They need to focus on a much smaller number of dishes, and try to inject some quality. For now, I couldn't recommend the place."
Good place for coffee and snack, quite spacious so there is no problem with finding comfy seats.

The Slug and Lettuce may not be exciting or original but it is a reliable go-to if you are after a few drinks or bit of food before the cinema or theatre.  There's loads of space and a section at the front with really comfy leather and seats and couches if you've had a long day and want to relax.   There's quite a varied menu and everything I've ever had has always been tasty and good value for money - particuarly love the risotto and tostadas (somewhere between a fajita and a pizza) and the puddings are generous and yummy aswell. They also do an offer on Monday's where all food has 50% off which is a great bargain.  The cocktails are really basic, don't expect anything authentic or memorable but at least the service is good so you'll get it quickly!

This place always gives me the creeps!! I'm going to keep this short and simple....  It's dirty, the carpet always has food mushed into it, the tables are never cleaned properly, the wine is warm (!!), the food is horrible re-heated crap, the prices are extortionate and the staff are moody.  I;ve been here several times and come to the same conclusion. I thought it was ok because it was beside the cinema etc etc - don't make the same mistake I did!!

This bar is absolutely fine to pop into for a drink. But I'd never eat in there again. We'd stopped in for lunch one day and I'd ordered a pasta with roasted peppers and a tomato sauce. Only it came with virtually no peppers at all (I was lucky if I had two slivers) and the sauce? What sauce?   I don't agree with paying around 8 for a bowl of bland pasta with virtually no vegetables or sauce. Hell, for that price, I could have got myself a decent two course lunch elsewhere.   Needless to say, it didn't do much for my hangover, and I couldn't bring myself to finish it either. My mate wasn't exactly fussed on hers either - so that too got left.   Bland, microwaved pre-cooked food. No value for money at all, and I just can't recommend it. Stick with the drinks. You know where you stand with those!

I was very let down by this place, as i have been to various other establishments owned by the same company and the food and service was far superior! I had ordered a chicken and pasta dish, and my friend had ordered a pasta dish which was supposed to have roasted vegetables with it. Instead my chicken dish came with the roasted vegetables and my friends dish came with a miniscule amount of pasta sauce! The service was not great either, oh, and my chicken was dry! I did have soup for a starter though, and i must admit, it was nice. Thank goodness i did have that as i'd been leaving the place as hungry as i was when i walked in otherwise! I dont think i'll be back!   It is a nicely decorated place, and i have been in for a quick drink before heading to the cinema, but food wise, i'll give it a miss in future!
Reliably great taste and portion sizes.

Juice Bars are easily my favourite things on this planet, from the whole fruit smoothies to the fruit and veg blended juice drinks, I am in love with it all. This is some of the best I've ever had. And I've tasted a lot.   I was in Hula Juice Bar today and had the Blue Hawaiian smoothie, which contains blueberries, strawberries, banana and apple, and was absolutely beautiful. I didn't try any food but I'll definitely be back to do so as it looks amazing. I have so many reasons to come back; hundreds of juice and smoothie combinations to try!  The venue itself is so accommodating and friendly. The vibrant colours and the eccentric mismatched chairs add a happy atmosphere, which is helped along by the friendly full-of-smiles staff, who seem to know quite a few of the regulars by name.   If you're craving a juice fix, I insist you head down to the Grassmarket and try some outstanding smoothies. You'll thank me later!

Fantastic place with fantastic staff!!  Combination of fresh and frozen fruit chosen to best suit the smmothie makle this one heck of a place. Amazing taste and produce these guys really exel healthy treats.  If you are a fan of hummous try theirs its top notch, staff are very helpful and will even consult with you on what smoothie you will enjoy based on your taste  Brilliant wee place means Jd = happy man!!

I've come here a couple times to meet Miss Jenny L, and have really enjoyed being at Hula both times!   The staff here are so very welcoming, and are very nice about altering orders. I had come here once before and ordered a cinnamon latte. When I returned for my second visit, they didn't seem to have it on the menu. But when I asked about it, they were more than happy to make me one! Delicious..  They have just undergone renovations, and it looks great! A lot more Hawaiian/hula themed, and just as cosy as before!   The soups of the day are fantastic and I would highly recommend them. I've noticed that the ingredients they use seem very fresh. Definitely my lunch/coffee place of choice when hanging about the grassmarket!

Good for juice but staff not really friendly, crowded and  feel rushed as not much seating!  Was actually asked not to eat some food bought from the market inside even though me and my friend got drinks AND food!  Not very impressed and have been here multiple times.

At one point there were juice bars every where it felt like. Hula seems to have been here for ages. I often make a point of popping in on sunny days, hang over days etc for a take away juice to energise while wandering around town. The juices are great, not inexpensive and not expensive. Staff seem nice enough. I haven't tried the food but it looks nice if a little pricy for a sandwich. All in nice place with great juice.
I've only tried their pastries/desserts but they were very good and they have vegan options for anyone looking!

Hula is cute, quick and affordable - the lunch time menu soup and bagel/wrap is super cheap and filling. Smoothies are lovely too! If you're looking for a quick and quite healthy fix for lunch I'd definitely recommend this place. The Popeye juice is my favourite!

Friendly service, smoothie was extra good but I didn't really enjoy the smoked salmon bagel...the salmon was ok but not the freshest. Bagel was crispy and yum though. We thought the price was a touch expensive compared to other places for what you get but overall a positive experience.
Good as always. Had the pesto chicken and sun dried tomatoes on a bagel ! Plus for the meal deal for lunch and got the zesty tomato coriander soup! DELICIOUS!!!!  Love this place

a winter in edinburgh generally means grey days, cold and wet weather, and a total lack of colour and sunshine.  and then there is winter inside Hula Juice Bar...color, sunshine, smoothies full of fruity goodness!! oh yes, i felt like i'd stepped into summer time a few months early when i came here on tuesday night :)  the shop very kindly stayed open for an extra hour so the cake committee could come and meet about setting up a bake off for charity!  all very exciting, but made much more so with the dominant yellow colour that was on the walls, chairs, and counters of hula.  and then there are the juices, my betty ford was a pretty pink, the popeye was a lovely forrest green, and even Susan M's tea came in a beautiful blue teapot.   all delivered by friendly smiling staff :)  so yes the colourful environment was very pleasing, but so were the lovely juice blends they had!  i found myself debating between a few of them but went for the betty ford that was lovely and full of strawberries and peach with just a hint of banana.  it was just the pick up i needed after scoffing a birthday cupcake during the afternoon at work.  i left feeling revived and healthy and sunny even though it was dark and cold outside.  i'm definitely a fan of hula and hope to get back there soon to try some of their tasty food offerings in addition to more juice!  i only wish this place was closer to leith...or that they had a second shop in leith!!

I am a smoothie-addict, and therefore I am quite fussy about what I drink. This place has not failed to impress me. The manager is a very friendly and dedicated lady and this adds to the quality of the experience. The menu is very rich and it always includes a fairly good selection of cakes.  I personally love thicker drinks, so I definitely appreciated the possibility of adding frozen yogurt for only 50p. It makes the smoothies absolutely outstanding without ruining the taste.  The place is very tidy and colorful, it offers free wi-fi and it's an option I would reccomend to anyone happening to be in that area.

Last time, I gave Hula 4 stars - they charged for GF bread so that ticked me off. Didn't stop me from going though and I do visit more regularly than my check-in's suggest - namely because I head in, grab food and then have my hands too full to use the Yelp app (and iphones are fragile little darlings and don't react well to cobbles) as I'm walking up Victoria St.  I love Hula. When I'm tired I head to Hula. When I have crap hair and dodgy skin, I head to Hula. When I've walked into town and need refreshments, I head to Hula. So why is this? I love their smoothies and juices. As I said in my last review - I eat my veggies, but as far as I was concerned, veggies were for eating, not drinking. Now, I drink my veggies courtesy of the Popeye - spinach, apple, lemon and nutmeg. It is divine! It is my cold curer - get in there as soon as the sniffles start and if skin and hair looks ropey then I order a large Popeye and I soon have a ready-brek glow.  Food is great too :-) No charge now for GF bread - hurrah but something happened on my last visit. Something immense that only GF people can understand. Normally chicken soup is off limits. Creamy (not overly so) chicken soup, with chicken bits and is good for the soul, but usually comes packed with wheat flour so is off limits. But at Hula - I HAD CHICKEN SOUP FOR LUNCH AND IT WAS AWESOME! It was gf, had ginger in it - ha! potential cold had to go somewhere else after that - and it was so damn good and reminded me that I miss having chicken soup for my lunch if I'm out and about. I had the soup and sandwich deal (gf bread) which was tons of food with my sandwich packed full of spicy tuna and only 5. Worth more for the virtuous healthy feeling I had leaving Hula.  So, yep Hula is well worth a visit. You know already that it's a great wee colourful haven on a dark, cold winters day with friendly staff, free wifi, awesome drinks and food, so if its been awhile, its time to get reacquainted.

Now I know what all the fuss is about! I swear I've passed Hula by unaware of its very existence! And now, I find that in that very spot exists the infamous, wonderful smoothie hula haven I've heard so much about! (And they really do go to town on the hula theme!)   Hula is just the right sort of small to feel cosey and not cramped. The staff were super welcoming and it was great to see that we got 10% off our order when we checked in on Yelp. Hooray!  I went for the Betty Ford with strawberry, peach, apple and banana and my smoothie significant other went for a Ginger Jack fruit juice with carrot, ginger, apple and orange. Wow! I will not accept any less than the smoothie scrumminess that is Hula. They tasted like pure fruit and were blended to perfection.   With our yelp discount, it came to about the average cost for two large smoothies at any smoothie bar. But tasted like one of the best smoothies I've had. And I've had a fair few! (Got to get them fruits!) Now to say I'd get the train to Edinburgh just to get my Hula fix would be a crazy lie. (Boy, I wish I could!) But when I'm in town, it's first on my agenda!
103-105 West Bow, EH1 2JP. Craving your daily greens juice or a really yummy breakfast? Here.  Emily Rose Reeder

Lots of character in the main part of the cafe but I was seated in the side room which had no atmosphere and had terrible acoustics.  Seated quickly and the service was prompt but wish I'd waited for  a table in the main part.  The decor is bright and funky, the art work being displayed is up for sale.  I Ordered the soup of the day mushroom with Stilton, it was accompanied with cheese on toast which was very tasty as the cheese was  Mull of Kintyre.  The bagel with baked ham and Mull of Kintyre  cheese was good also.  The milkshakes are delicious we ordered nutty professor, peanut butter, banana and frozen yogurt and frangipani,  banana, cinnamon, honey and frozen yogurt both delicious. Xoxo

We were staying in the Grassmarket area, and after a night of drinking all I wanted was a green juice.  Low and behold, Hula appeared like a beacon and gave me what I needed.    I told them what I was looking for, and they recommended a juice not on the menu - all I can recall was mango and spinach (I think apple too?  Ginger?) but once I heard those things I was like - SOLD.  We got a wheatgrass "booster" too which didn't affect the taste like I thought it would, fortunately.  I think it was about 5 for a large with the booster.  Worth it!  My fiance and I shared it, though I drank most of it because it was so addictively good.  So fruity and yummy, you'd never know how many vegetables you were consuming!  I watched them make it, which was really fun, they have these crazy industrial blenders and just jam whole apples in there.  Service was really friendly, took a while to get the juice but the cafe was so cozy and cute that I didn't mind waiting.  We didn't eat there, but their menu looks so wonderful and healthy that I hope to grab a bite there another day.

This little cafe was a wonderful find!  We tried the acai bowl (which I now want to eat everyday for the rest of my life!) and a Scottish porridge with blueberries (will add this to my lifetime menu too!).  The waitstaff was quick and very pleasant.  I will definitely be back every chance I get!

I came by here to get some work done and treat myself to the Nutty Professor. It was a good smoothie, but I easily could have made it myself (if I wasn't living in student accommodation with no blender). The service was really slow, but that might have been because I was on my laptop so they didn't want to disturb me. The food and desserts looked really good, so if you're planning on sitting in, I would suggest getting a full meal and not just a smoothie.

Hula is a place I have always wanted to like, and despite a few nice experiences here with smoothies/juice, I have a slightly "meh" feeling about it nowadays.   It wants to be a healthy cafe, it wants to be a hip eaterie, it's colourful and on Victoria street. There is wifi. It has a lot of potential.  I got soup today. Tasty, but at 4.25 a little on the steep side given that so many other places in town offer more for less. My friend paid around 5 for her smoothie, which though tasty was certainly not worth the high price tag.   I had a look at the cakes before leaving the shop, a few gluten free options but nothing particularly inspiring.

This cafe is nestled along the Grassmarket, almost on the corner up a very steep street. It's very cozy and deceptively larger than I thought (but still not that big). There is outdoor seating along the front for nicer days. Inside in the main room there is some seating but if you venture in, there is more seating! Very comfy and cozy place.   We didn't stay, I ordered the Popeyes juice cause I love those super-jam-packed, full of vitamins and goodness type of juices. It was very tasty and my toddler approved. We also got a veggie wrap which had some creamy guacamole and loads of fresh crunchy veggies!   All in all  very tasty and one of the only places in Edinburgh to offer fresh juice. And by fresh juice I mean, freshly squeezed or liquified right  in front of you. None of this bottled none sense. Fresh and unapologetic.   Definitely will be coming back! Child friendly and good wholesome fresh food & juice. Really couldn't ask for more.

This healthy cafe was directly around the corner from the flat we had while visiting Edinburgh and we enjoyed it so much that we visited 3 times.  It's a small spot, but with a lot of character and they like to highlight local artists on the walls. They have very impressive vegetarian and vegan options for those with dietary restrictions and they make truly wonderful smoothies if you're not in the mood for coffee or tea (seriously, you've got to try their awesome fresh fruit smoothies!).  They have some very unique menu creations which will keep you returning to try new dishes each time and nothing we tried was even remotely disappointing. Every bite was pure culinary genius!  If you're headed to Edinburgh, this is a really great place to get breakfast each morning.

Hungover on New Year's Day and in need of some warmth and a drink, we hunted down Hula after checking Yelp for suggestions.  Located in a great spot for tourists checking out key areas in the city, it's in an ideal spot.  It looked warm and bright from the outside so we headed in with ideas of coffee and cake.  They were able to accommodate five of us in a back room that you wouldn't know existed if just looking in from the outside.   Decorated with lots of cute pictures of animals it was a fun place to spend an hour warming up, reliving tales of Hogmanay and cure our weary bodies.  Once we glanced at the menus we all swiftly changed from wanting coffees to wanting to try something from their extensive juice and smoothie menu.  I opted for a delicious and zingy smoothie of Apple, lime, ginger and lemon, with an added energy shot of guarana and ginseng. Just what the doctor ordered!
