I think the worst thing I can say about this place is that they opened at 8:06 rather than 8am. The shop offers a nice selection of pastries, ornate cakes and slices, drinks, and sandwiches. As we were there for breakfast, we shared a raisin swirl, lemon meringue, and slice of apple tart, along with coffee and a refreshing peppermint tea. Each food was presented on small slate plates. Gorgeous and delicious.

I honestly love this place. La Barantine Victoria is a quaint bakery that offers delicious pastries, heart-warming lattes (with BEAUTIFUL art), and good vibes only. I enjoyed it so much that I came here twice with my boyfriend and we were only in Edinburgh for two days (we probably would've came every day if we discovered it during our first day).   The vegetable quiche is amazing and comes with a healthy portioned side salad (note: salad apparently doesn't come with quiches when you do take away). Their cappuccino had some of the best art I've seen, and their croissants are to die for. I ordered both a chocolate and a regular croissant and was planning to save one for later but couldn't because they were that good...  Come here if you're visiting Edinburgh, you won't be disappointed! P.S. They do NOT have WiFi in case you were wondering (as of Oct. 2018).

What a charming little French cafe in Edinburgh. The cafe culture in Edinburgh is something I haven't been able to find yet back home in D.C., and La Barantine Victoria adds a lot to the offerings that Edinburgh has.   The atmosphere is quite nice, combining the old stone look of Victoria Street with that French charm. I ordered a cappuccino and the Le Normand sandwich. The cappuccino was the best I'd had in Edinburgh (I'd had about 4 in my 5 days there). I also really loved the sandwich. It came on a baguette and was filled with butter, ham, brie, and salad. It's something I would have eaten on my many days in Belgium and it made me feel like I was back in my childhood, which was a great feeling.   I would recommend La Barantine Victoria if you're walking down Victoria Street looking for a place to grab a quick bite or a coffee. Their pastries and viennoiseries looked really good too!

French patisserie cafe close to Edinburgh castle.  Ordered a small hot chocolate, and a salmon cream cheese, tomato baguette. Crispy, savory, and paired very well, they offered a variety of other desserts from fruit tarts to French macarons; this place was a nice cozy pitstop to have a quick bite .  Definitely a nice place to dodge the rain and have coffee or tea.

Cute little shop just off Grassmarket. Great sandwiches and coffee. I had a very ample flat white that was absolutely the best cup of coffee I have had out in some time and I'm pretty picky when it comes to coffee. I had a croissant with butter and jam that was nice too. My wife and daughter had sandwiches which they both enjoyed as well. Definitely worth stopping in for a bite if you are in the neighborhood.

In a 6 day stay in Edinburgh, I came here 4 times. I would swing by to grab a baguette or sweet to take back to the apartment we rented.   Every time the food was flavorful and fresh and the service was lovely.

La Barantine Victoria is an OK coffee shop; the venue is in a really nice setting, and the overall quality is better than a typical chain coffee place.  I came here for breakfast and ordered an eclair, which was acceptable, though nothing to write home about.  It was just short of being too dry, and didn't really taste like it was worth the 6 it cost me for that an espresso.  That price would have been fine if the quality had been better, but it was just too high for the quality I received.  Given the fact that the staff wasn't particularly friendly or welcoming, and I didn't go away with an overwhelming desire to return.  The girl working the counter really brightened up when a person who was apparently a regular came in, which made the lack of welcome I encountered that much more noticeable.  Bottom line: There are a number of places close by where the coffee and food are better, and you're likely to be greeted with a smile even if you're not a regular.

Every time I entered this cafe I had the feeling as if I was suddenly finding myself in the streets of France, in one of those small cozy cafes full of tasty croissants and other bakery sweets. And the coffee here is just perfect. I adore the soft and slightly bitter taste of cappuccino which wakes me up instantly. Well, the owners did a great job with that place and i'm thankful to them. I think that everyone should come here at least once and feel this peaceful atmosphere.
Charming cafe with outstanding croissants. Friendly staff and reasonable prices.. Indulge in the amazing French pastries

28-30 Grassmarket, Edinburgh, EH1 2JU 0131-225 6464 Bruntsfield Store Take Away & Delivery Tel: 0131 229 7008 mammaspizza.co.uk Real American pizzas in a very cosy environment. Family friendly, the perfect lunch/dinner to fill the whole family. close to city centre and buses. Very friendly staff who are more than happy meet your needs in creating your favourite pizza.

Ordered take away at 2110 on Thursday evening. 14 inch seafood. 16. prompt service but not great value for a slightly too soft pizza. I suppose that crisp delivery pizza is almost a contradiction in terms.

Yum! This place sure does do good pizza - I particularly like the range of toppings - they have very few set-topping pizzas, mostly you just mix and match and put all the things you love most on - I had tuna and artichoke, mm mm! The dessert menu is also rather good, especially for chocolate lovers like myself - I had THE richest chocolate cheesecake ever, couldn't finish it, always a good sign! The waiter was very friendly, and although it was busy so that service could be a little slow at times, it wasn't really a problem. A good evening was had by all.

Had a great Sunday lunch at Mamma's. Had a voucher from last years Radio Forth Help a Child Appeal that had to be used by the end of the month (they normally contribute quite a lot!) The voucher was for a meal for four up to the value of 80. This was for food only. We started with a variety of starters, garlic bread with cheese, mushrooms baked in garlic butter & buffallo wings in honey & garlic sauce. Garlic seemed to be a bit of a theme there. We all opted for fillet steak as a main course, this was seared in the kitchen & brought to the table on a lava rock, which was very hot. The idea being that you cook each bite of your steak just how you like it. The steaks were served with potato wedges & a variety of dips. The lava rock stayed hot throughout the meal & came in handy to reheat the wedges also. Three of us ordered dessert, which were served with a choice of cream or ice cream. A chocolate brownie, baked cheesecake & a Choco woco whako, a chocolate overload, chocolate brownie, chocolate ice cream, chocolate sauce & goodness knows what else was in there.  The food was great & no complaints about the service which was cheerful, helpful & timely, despite the waitress having a bit of a mishap with a glass or two. I will most certainly return, perhaps I may even get round to trying the pizza, which looked delicious!

As a visitor in Edinburgh I was pleasantly surprised by this place as it is in the heart of major tourism. The prices were good: starter of cullen skink unusual in an Italian but tasty. Pity that they had no mushrooms left. Pizza piping hot and we did add haggis! Wine was fine at 13 but a screw top. We enjoyed our meal.

Fantastic pizza shop on the Cowgate where you can buy a slice of delicious pizza to take away, or sit in and try some of the combinations that they offer. You can choose any topping you like - including chocolate, marshmallows and other crazy taste sensations! Prices are good and the pizzas are tasty. I recommend BBQ sauce and blue cheese - sounds mad but it works so well!

Like this place but it has gone down in the last couple of years as it has rested on its laurels. I think it produced the best pizzas in edinburgh once and now it is just a lot better than average. Still of you want a huge pizza and not a huge bill you cant go wrong

Decent pizza, fast service and open later than most nearby restaurants. There is a nice selection of bottled beers, but they are perhaps a bit overpriced. The extensive pizza topping selection caters to all tastes!

Good pizza but takeaway is painfully slow and you don't get any confirmation. A number of times, I've been round to flats where people have given up on the Mammas order and decided to go somewhere else assuming they didn't get the order. They then turn up a few hours after your dinner demanding money, once as much as five hours after the order had been placed (and two hours of hungry waiting before my friends ordered elsewhere).

Tasty pizza in a relaxed venue which a huge choice of toppings (everything from pepperoni to ice cream!). This cosy little restaurant tucked away in the Grassmarket is a great place to eat, although if eating at lunchtime, be sure to arrive in plenty of time to beat the lunchtime rush. The restaurant itself is colourfully decorated with plenty of seating crammed into the small space. The restaurant also offers a gluten free base for every pizza on the menu, as well as the option of spicy or non-spicy sauce, so there's an option to suit everyone. Reasonably priced and freshly made, this is definitely one of Edinburgh's best pizzerias.

I have only ever had takeaway pizza from here but I think it serves the best takeaway pizzas in Edinburgh, serving real Italian pizza instead of the doughy, stodgy offerings from Dominos, etc. The takeaway prices are slightly more expensive than other takeaways but it's worth it for the fresh bases and good range of topping choices (eg, haggis, aubergine and other unusual options). They will also make gluten free pizzas on request for a small surcharge - one of the few takeaways in Edinburgh to offer this. The only downside is that, probably as a result of their popularity, you have to be prepared for a long wait as delivery usually takes a minimum of an hour.

This is one of the most popular pizza restaurants in Edinburgh and is situated in the busiest street for pubs - the Grassmarket. When i last went, it was very busy but we managed to get a small table for two. There was a great mix of people there both young and old and familes. The staff were very efficient and seemed to know when to come over and take our order or drinks etc, despite being so busy. The tables were crammed close together but the staff can carry the huge pizzas above their heads and weave through! The pizzas are excellent as are the barbeque chicken wings for starter - be ready to share them as the bowl i got was huge!

Mama-Mia-American-Pizzeria is alrighty for Jungleboy.  The place is a jolly, colourful, multilevel building with alcoves and indoor window gaps. They have personally painted the walls with a  surrealistic piece depicting flying mushrooms, chili-pepper butterflies and a Pepperoni-Man saving the day. Funny!  We sat down on a table for two and we ordered our pizza - 9" with 3 toppings - I got pepperoni, mushrooms and chili-peppers (was I subliminally influenced by the painting? Yes I was..) It was a very well filled pizza and very tasty.  I enjoyed the pizza crust, which I normally don't(!) and appreciated the laid back, but precise way of serving. They enquired if we were OK, we got our drinks served in time and we got to take the left over slices with us.   I did find it a bit cold near the doors and I had a good view of all the people on the outside who peered in to see what this place is like. I made an effort to smile and wave to many of them to show how  good it was - but somehow the peepers backed away from the windows very quick when I did that.   Recommend for a quick visit or even a nice afternoon late snack / meal with a bunch of friends or family, they had a cartwheel of a pizza available to serve to a big table of 8 - it was huge!

I always feel bad when I am writing a negative review when I ate the goods for free. But, I did, and I wasn't impressed.   But - the good stuff first - Mamma's does a whole range of different pizza and caters for gluten free, which is always worth an extra star. But, the pizza I tried had really meagre toppings and a heavy base. Seafood, vegetarian, they all looked sparse and personally, for me pizza is all about the toppings, the base just holds it all together. When the balance is lost, you have lost me as well. Sorry, Mamma's, as I did eat for free at a Yelp even, but there is just better pizza in town.

My first full day in Edinburgh 18 months ago, I found myself in an Internet cafe and was googling 'gluten free in Edinburgh'. My fingers hovered over the keys as I waited, breathless with anticipation, as to what results google would yield.  I nearly exploded with excitement when I discovered I could get gluten free pizza at Mamma's in the Grassmarket. Armed with a 'leaving gift' of my Edinburgh guidebook, I headed towards the pizza.  I loved Mamma's and have returned tons since. I was able to 'recreate' a Sloppy Giuseppe (chili beef, onions and peppers) and grab a GF beer at the same time (heaven). So, it was a rainy day but I was in a little sunny corner of America, munching down on pizza, drinking beer, and listening to classic eighties rock.  Whilst loitering between interviews, I found myself with time to kill and I headed to Mamma's last week. The pizza base was thinner than before (good!), nice and crispy (hate doughy pizza's). The tomato sauce base comes in mild or spicy - I went for spicy but there was a little too much sauce and it was slightly bitter but the other toppings were generous. No sides this time but the sweet potato fries seasoned with paprika are am-az-ing and if in full pig out mode, then the warmed chocolate brownie (speaking from one who has GF brownie fatigue) is great with vanilla ice-cream.  Edinburgh is served well for GF pizza lovers but as my first love in Edinburgh, Mamma's has a special place in my heart....

it was a very rainy sunday evening that brought me to Mamma's for dinner with friends.  as the grassmarket is a fair trek from my part of town, i hadn't visited before so didn't really know what to expect besides the offering of pizza.  the menu is pretty standard for a pizza place, loads of pizza toppings to choose from, a variety of pizza sizes, a number of sides to accompany, and pasta dishes if that is what you'd rather go for.  i got a small pizza with artichoke, olives, goats cheese, and garlic tomatoes and we all opted to spilt a side of chili cheese fries.  food arrived fairly quickly, but i was left less than impressed.  my pizza was ok, the toppings were nice but the sauce lacked any real taste and the base was a bit too stodgy for my liking.  the chili cheese fries were tasty though so that was a bit of a saving grace.    while the service was good, i feel like i can't really comment on that much as we were pretty much the only customers in that night.  the waitress was friendly though which is always appreciated.  however, the restaurant itself is a bit tired looking and could use a good clean... not a great thought when you're sat down for a nice dinner.  i think this review might have been three stars but i felt that the price i paid for mediocre food was a bit high.  if memory serves me right, i paid almost 20 for my pizza and portion of the chili fries, which was a bit high for something i didn't really enjoy.  so overall, not really impressed with Mamma's and i'm unlikely to make the effort to go back.

Mamma's is a great Italian restaurant in the Grassmarket which always gives a delicious, value for money meal with friendly service.  I've been here a few times with my friends over the past year and we've always enjoyed ourselves.  It's famed locally for its pizzas, but it also offers a good range of other authentic Italian dishes like stone baked steak and lasagne.  The meals are served in good, filling portions and I've never left Mamma's hungry, even after having just a main course. Pizzas, however, are their speciality and they offer a plethora of toppings, from spicy Italian sausage to haggis!  On weekends it gets pretty busy and can feel a little tightly packed.  Don't let this put you off as the food is more than worth it!

My husband and I decided to pop into Mamma's after reading the Yelp reviews. This is not a 4-star worthy restaurant. Their food is seriously lacking.  We ordered the garlic cheese bread (plus a side of pizza sauce to dunk said garlic bread into) and a pepperoni pizza. The pizza was flavorless and I had to dunk each bite into the side of pizza sauce to give it a little hint of flavor.  The best part of Mamma's was the service. I know, I dare say that service was good in the UK but it was. This is most likely because our server was Canadian and had just moved to Scotland a couple months prior. She was great and the Hoegaarden was great too but that's about it.  As a side note, they have a huge selection of gluten free options. I think that this is why Mamma's is rated so highly.  Dress code is casual - you can pretty much get away with wearing anything here. I would not dress up, that's for sure.

Thanks first to Claire L for this recommendation, it was a fantastic find!  I have seen Mamma's in the grassmarket for 3 years, but never thought about going inside. It just seemed like another tourist trap by the side of the castle. Then I found out I couldn't eat gluten anymore, and needed to find an alternative to my favourite foods.  I had heard that the beloved la favorita's gluten free pizzas were pretty lame. I rang up this morning to ask whether they made them up fresh, and they admitted that they made them all fresh in the morning, but not fresh to order. I love pizza dough which has just been cooked, and mamma's really does well in this respect.  My boyfriend and I went with another couple to Mamma's this evening, armed with Itison tokens (again, thanks Claire L): 11 for 2 9 inch pizzas or gourmet burgers with one glass of wine or beach each. This worked out as a really cheap meal, as we got to choose 3 toppings. I went for goats cheese, olives and pepper with a spicy pizza sauce. There were lots of other exciting options, including cactus, vegetarian sausage, marshmallows and chocolate! Everyone else had normal pizza bases, which were slightly more golden looking than mine, though I admit that it's difficult to make gluten free flour turn that colour. I admit my only criticism would be that the base was quite powdery underneath. Thery were generous with the toppings, and the base was pretty crispy-hate soggy/stodgy pizza bases. The pizzas seemed quite small on the plate, but were slightly thicker than Italian pizzas, so filled you up much quicker. I had a glass of nero d'avola, which was really lovely. The others went for a pint of beer.  Towards the end of the meal, my boyfriend found a piece of plastic in his meal. When the waitress asked if everything was okay, I said "Yeah the pizza was lovely, but we found this in his pizza..." She came back after 10 minutes with a gluten free brownie with vanilla ice cream, and a slice of NY vanilla cheesecake with strawberry ice cream. I quickly said shotgun staring at the GF brownie, which I put in my bag with the intent of eating it for breakfast, stuffed from the pizza. The others shared the ice cream and cheesecake, both of which said were lovely.  I can imagine this being slightly expensive if you were going to eat here without a discount, but with the discount we got a great deal, and the staff were extremely attentive and friendly.  The interior was very clean, and reminiscent of an American diner. I saw other diners going for burgers, milkshakes and rootbeer floats... Always interesting! Mamma's have a great location too, right in the heart of the grassmarket, at the foot of the castle.

I can't really comment on the interior or service of Mamma's, but I can comment on the food. A friend who had just moved into the area had a few of us round to the house and ordered in from this place.   We ordered a chicken, haggis and pepper pizza, with extra cheese, and a bottle of red wine! I haven't ever came across a takeaway that delivers booze but we got our bottle for about 9, more expensive than the off license but then we got it brought to our door! You can also get lager or cider too! Brilliant!  The pizza was absolutely superb, and I was glad I didn't get the weird pizza that my other friends ordered, which had banana, pineapple and pepperoni on it. No, thanks. You can get all sorts of weird stuff on your pizza in here! Chocolate, apple, baked beans....hmm.  I would definitely get a pizza from here again, and would be interested to go in and try the restaurant as I have only heard good things about the place.

I love pizza, and hence when I heard that Mamma's served the "best pizza in Edinburgh" I was excited.  And I wasn't too disappointed...  Mamma's offers both indoor and outdoor seating, although I'd highly recommend heading indoors just to enjoy some of the atmosphere.  Inside, it is very interesting.  There is lot's of retro, almost graffiti style artwork on the walls, the subject of which is largely caricatures of the available pizza toppings.  This artwork provides a contrast with the furnishings which are traditional and wooden.   The toppings available are fantastic. there is a variety of cheeses available besides mozzarella, including goat's cheese and blue cheese. You can have things I would never have considered putting on a pizza myself, including apple and even cactus. Furthermore, you have the option of having your pizza made with the mild or the spicy tomato sauce.  It's also not just pizza on offer. Other dishes available include steak and pasta. The pizza's have deliciously crisp bases and the ratio of cheese to other toppings is just right. A particular highlight for me was the prosciutto and pineapple topping.   While this place is good, if it wasn't for the 40% discount I receive due to Snapfax (a student discount book), I would consider it too pricey.  If you wish to eat out and it's delicious pizza you're after, this is the place to go. However, if you're not too fussed about the whole eating out part and are just after some delicious pizza, I'd recommend Papa John's.

This Italian restaurant at the Grassmarket was worryingly empty when a friend and I walked up to it; it was good weather and we'd just spent a lovely hour lunching and lounging at Made in Italy. All the outdoor seats of the restaurants and pubs we walked past were full, except for Mamma's. However, we did check out the menu, which is definitely unique! You've the option of truly creating your own pizza, with banana and Danish blue cheese amongst the choice of toppings. Their pricy mains, such as seared steak you can cook yourself on a hot stone (original!) and Cajun salmon, may have contributed to the empty seats, which really does puzzle me because the menu looked awesome. So awesome I'll upload a picture.

Mamma's has got to be one of my favourite places to have a pizza in Edinburgh. Over the years this place has not disappointed!   Situated down at the Grassmarket, Mamma's is not small but not large inside, just the right size for an independent pizzeria. The interior is slightly retro with lots and lots of literature and posters about upcoming gigs and comedy shows!   Apart from this, I suppose the pizza is the main attraction. With nice, crispy Italian bases, the pizzas are fantastic! From a margarita to a hot and spicy Americano, the pizzas are full of bursting flavours! Furthermore, you do not just need to sit inside to experience the taste of the food, you can actually order and pick them up, and eat them in the luxury of your own home!   If you want a great meal in Grassmarket, you will be hard pushed to find a better place, and for pizza, it is simply one of the best in Edinburgh!

As an American who has experienced loads of pizza back home, I was expecting a bit more from this place. The pizza was actually some of the worst Pizza I've had in Britain. Pizza Express is eons better. I ordered a 12 inch pepperoni pizza- it had too much cheese and only about 8 pepperonis on the whole thing. The chicken wings left something to be desired as well. For the same price we ate at a fantastic Italian place down the road.   The service was bad. When it came time to pay the bill, we waited at the table with our bill and card clearly visible and didn't receive any service. We then decided to go up to the counter to pay where we stood for about 5 more minutes waiting to be acknowledged by the staff. It seemd like they didn't want us to pay for our food.  Serious disappointment.

mama's is still my favourite pizza in edinburgh! tonight i had it with jalapenos, bananna and green olives!!!...quirky i know, but so unusual and good! the waitress gave us a couple of free cokes because our order took so long which was kind and thoughtful!

I've been coming to Mamma's for my pizza fix for as long as I can remember. It is one of very few independent dedicated pizza joints in Edinburgh, I'd be hard pushed to name another one - they must've scared the competition away! Mamma's definitely knows how to do pizza well: thin and crispy bases with lots of exotic toppings (marshmallow anyone?). The menu has a few starters (go for the macho nachos), but the main event is obviously the pizza. It comes in four different sizes, helpfully illustrated by a ruler on the menu, and you're encouraged to order a large one and share it between your party, this adds to the convivial atmosphere and also makes things a little cheaper. There are gluten/wheat free options so those with intolerances can join in the fun too.  Tasty pizza, central location and student discount - what's not to love?

Has Mammas changed ownership recently?   Got a delivery at the weekend and the first thing I noticed was that it arrived in a generic box as opposed to a Mammas box. What was inside was just as generic (and soggy) and nothing like the Mammas pizzas I remember from the past.   On the phone I was asked if I wanted spicy or mild but that didn't seem to translate to much on the plate. They may as well have asked if I wanted bland or blander.   As for the Buffalo wings coated in Mammas secret spicy recipe and served with your choice of sauces, I think they may have waived a some BBQ sauce nearby but three of the wings didn;t even have any sauce on them. If they were coated in some secret spicy recipe I think the secret will be safe for a while.   I used to like Mammas but will probably be taking my custom elsewhere in future. The one star is for the quick delivery.
Did not enjoy my visit here.   PAINFULLY slow service and then they got my order wrong which led to another PAINFULLY slow wait.   Staff did not seem to care that much.

I haven't been for a little while as I moved house so it isn't so near any more. Was one of my favorite Edinburgh places for lunch when I did live round the corner.   As others have mentioned - the pizzas are great. I particularly like the fact that you can have a different topping on each half of the pizza - means you can have exactly what you fancy or share one with your partner.   Good range of beers to wash down the pizza.   In summer they have tables outside in the Grass Market and you can sit and watch the world go by.

Mama mia que pizza!  Very neat pizzeria in the heart of downtown Edinburgh.    1st of all -- check in using Yelp so you can take advantage of a special offer: 1 free stater (appetizer) with the purchase of an entree. You can pick from different items such as garlic bread, chicken wings, nachos...  We got the nachos which come with guacamole, sour cream, salsa, jalapenos and a spicy meat chilly (they also offer a vegetarian version).  We ordered their individual pizzas and be aware that they are big and can satisfy a couple of people.  We ordered The Hot One! Jalapenos, spicy beef, pepperoni, ham and red onions. We also ordered The Matador - Chorizo, pepperoni, chicken and red onions.  Washed it all down with some cold beers - Peroni & Barney's Extra Pale. The one thing they fell short on was that they have a limited beer selection.   Overall good service and awesome Red, White and Blue decorations.

Excellent service and good food.  The wings are cooked perfectly and a very good option. Probably some of the better wing quality I have ever experienced in Scotland although they are simply served fried with a side of ranch / blue cheese dip. They don't toss then in any sort of buffalo sauce which is a shame as the wing quality is so good.  The pizzas are pretty good although I prefer a crispier crust and whilst these weren't deep dish they felt a bit to thick for my liking. Still, very good quality toppings, generous portions and good sauce.  The service from the staff is very good. Mainly students as you will in the main find in this area. They are very friendly, interested and eager to please. Price wise it is very reasonable and i would recommend overall. I would rate 4.5 stars on the whole and will come back again.

Found this place along Grassmarket street. At first i was not hungry for pizza until I saw their intriguing sign that stated "how many inches can you handle" hook, line and sinker. Staff was great and very friendly.  As for the food my basic girlfriend got the basic pepperoni pizza (may need to find a less basic bae). As for me, I ordered BBQ D2. The pepperoni pizza, for a lack of better words was... basic. The BBQ D2 packed a flavor punch. It had sausage with a hint taste of bbq flavor in the sauce. The prawns were pretty good sized enough for a good bite. The red peppers packed a kick but also had a tasty sweet after taste. We could only handle 9 inches of pizza each. And each about 7 pounds, i would say it was a good deal for a good meal.

Pizza heaven.. so so happy that Yelpers reccomended this place, as this is how I found this gluten free friendly eatery!  We were quite hungry by the time we arrived here in the early evening, our huge hotel breakfast had worn off and our feet were weary from a day wandering round the world heritage city.    We both like pizza, but havn't had any since we became a gluten free home.. usually we go Indian when eating out as it's easier to see what suits gluten free diets, and we are still getting used to the eating out situation, but were trusting the Yelpers on this one.. the menu here is almost as if 'non GF' being the exception as you can eat everything except the items with stars.  Our waitress informed us we could choose half and half pizzas if we couldn't decide, there were at least 4 pre-suggested veggie choices, with loads of veggie toppings, and two different GF base sizes.  We like to share so got 2 x 12" GF pizzas and tried out all 4 vegetarian topping ideas!   We were both expecting one of those pre-bought bases which look less than appetising in the packet, but imagine our complete joy when hand made and superbly crafted pizzas arrived on silver platters.. made just for us!  Each pizza was clearly hand made with love, and we had 2 with 4 choices on halves: -The veggie = Mushrooms, Onions, Peppers, Garlic, Tomatoes, Black Olives -Cheese 3PO = Cheddar, Mozzarella & Swiss cheeses -Gusto del papa = Red Onion Marmalade, Goats Cheese, Fresh Basil -Club med = Peppers, Black and Green Olives, Red Onion, Garlic oil, Rocket (and no Parmesan, as this is not veggie)  The staff couldn't have been nicer, they know everything about the menu and all of their food and drink, and are super cheery.  There is free wifi, so you can easily pay with Zapper.  Everything about this place is 5 stars... thank you Mamma's :)

Was having a lovely meal with friends when I found a piece of chicken on my veggie pizza! That somewhat ruined the meal out and put me off. They discounted my bill by 5 and were apologetic but for me that is pretty bad as a really strict lifelong veggie and I don't think they grasped how unpleasant this was for me.   The rest of the table said there pizza was really good.

I had an enjoyable experience at Mamma's last night. The staff were really friendly and welcoming and it was a nice cosy atmosphere, with a mixture of locals and tourists. The pizza was very much just cheap, basic ingredients, which I unfortunately found somewhat lacking in flavour. The house red wine was quite nice though. And for beer lovers, they stock Barney's & Innis & Gunn.  They do gluten free pizzas too, as well as some snack foods, sides, salads and a there are a couple of burgers on the menu. If you're on the Grassmarket and craving basic pizza or nachos etc, then Mamma's could be a good option, but I generally like something a bit different when dining out, so I don't think I will be returning.

I love Mamas. Proper relaxed feel, superb pizzas and friendly staff.  On the popular Grassmarket in Edinburgh this is prime for attracting tourists, but locals shouldn't be scared off. It's cosy inside, but I've never had a wait long for a seat. Once your sat down, you start to browse the menu - and now comes the hard bit: choosing your pizza. Mama's has a couple of pre-assigned ones but the real star is the 'choose your own' - a basic cheese & tomato (you can have the spicy sauce, which I recommend) and then you can select from a long list of ingredients - ham, chicken, chorizo, spinach, peppers, onions, pineapple, black pudding, haggis (well this is scotland), banana, Nutella. Yup, there's a ridiculous choice of toppings!  Oh and I didn't tell you the best bit - if you're coeliac or avoiding gluten for health reasons, not only can they do your pizza base gluten free, Mama's also has beers to suit your disagreeable tummy!   Pop in and try my favourite pizza - black pudding, calamari and pineapple!

Good for casual quick food in the Grassmarket.   They don't have a full menu of pizza options but rather a dozen options and then a list of all the toppings you can put together in any combination you want. This is not so good for indecisive people like me as it gives me too many possibilities. The pizzas are good and come in a variety of sizes, the ruler on the back of the menu is especially usefully.   The tables are very close together so expect your neighbouring tables to be able to overhear your conversation and you to be able to overhear theirs.  They do gluten free pizzas and beer which are apparently awesome according to my gluten free friend.

We went here for a free event for toddlers during the food & wine festival. The event was very impressive, my toddler got to make a pizza from scratch all by herself and all for free! The wee pizza makers (the event had about 13 kids) all had a blast.    The owner of the restaurant hosted the event and was extremely fun and entertaining. He did a really good job leading the kids through the steps to make pizza dough. We were so pleased by our experience that we stayed for lunch!   We split a medium pizza between 2 adults and wee one ate her tasty creation. Our pizza was definitely reminiscent of pizzas I've had in California. Very tasty! The crust is thicker than italian style but not deep dish like Chicago style, quite similar to NY slices. We really enjoyed the pizza and would def return.   It would be fun to go back and have a pizza making event! Or a special bday party where a lucky few could make their own pizzas!  Or just go and eat some pizza.  Either way you slice it you're gonna have some scrumptious pizza!

We have eaten at Mamma's several times over the years and are never left wanting. We thought it would be a mixed bag during the Festival, but we were seated within minutes and the staff were very helpful and polite - which can often be hard to find in the city on a Saturday night - especially in the Grassmarket.  I was a bit disappointed with the lack of spinach on my pizza, and finding out after asking for more that I was charged for it. Also, they automatically add an optional 10% gratuity to the bill - however, if I ran a restaurant in the Grassmarket, I'd probably do the same.  Mamma's is the only pizza place I've seen that does a gluten free crust - which I'll definitely have to try next time.  Now to eat my left over pizza...

I'm a pizza lover and Mamma's didn't disappoint!  I had a 9" pizza with 3 toppings: artichokes, green olives and roquito peppers - nestled on a spicy pizza base. So basically, you choose how big a pizza you want, what kind of sauce (spicy or mild) and then what toppings you want. The toppings list is pretty extensive, you can even request cactus or marshmallows on your pizza if you so wish, but I prefer the more conservative options :)  The pizza was delicious, base was not thin but not overly thick either - somewhere between a pan pizza and a thin pizza crust I guess. It was definitely crusty which I liked.   Service is friendly. And the music - oh I could come here just for the music :)

The Globe is a great little sandwich shop on Broughton Street. It stands out from the crowd by offering a customers a good choice of breads, great fillings, soups, fresh coffee, hot pies and tasty pastries. It is quite a funky little place and the staff always look really cool, but they know how to knock up a mean sandwich. If you're stuck by the range of fillings on offer, the menu board lists some exciting suggestions - recently I tried Jarlsberg, Cumberland Sausage and Mango Chutney, toasted on an oval roll, needless to say if was delicious.  If you're looking for something a little different to a boring chicken mayonnaise sandwich on soggy sliced white bread, then look no further than The Globe. They'll even deliver to you!

Wasn't on the menu, but i thought I chance my luck and ask for a chicken, pesto and cheese sandwich (trust me, better than sex).   The staff had no problem fixing it up for me and charging me a little under half of what a normal sandwich costs.  Shame about the seating though!

In a state of major coffee withdrawal post-gym workout, I wandered into the Skylark cafe (mostly because the steps to grounds suddenly became so much harder!)  A very cute interior with additional seating in the back, this cafe is bigger than it looks.   The service was super friendly and I had a lovely chat with the Barista whilst waiting for my coffee.   Personally, I like my coffee strong and hot. What I do not like is lukewarm faint coffee-tasting milk. Unfortunately this was the latter, I think the cups are too big so it was a fail for me.   The saving grace is the great service and varied menu that I still very much want to try. They also stock pana chocolaye- the new craze from Melbourne (you're welcome!) to the UK. Skylark is now my official chocolate dealer.

I've walked past the Skylark a few times. Each time, I was drawn to it because it always looked so cosy and sweet inside.   I recently popped in for lunch, going for the soup and a sandwich; a lovely winter afternoon pick-me-up. I just love thicker blended soups and so the dreamy vegetable-coconut fusion du jour was heaven to me, and the mozzarella and pesto sandwich made for the perfect soup-dipping vehicle.   The sandwich itself was a lovely puffy pitta; somewhere between a flatbread and a pitta. The result made for a really filling lunch. Next time, I want to try one of their smoothies as the selection sounded delicious.  It's a lot bigger than it looks, with a hidden back room and a mini play spot for the little ones. Service was lovely and friendly too. - I look forward to my next visit!

I only came in here recently for a cup of latte and a bit of rest time with my toddler because I had heard this cafe has an indoor play area for kids. Although the play area was smaller than I expected, it was great to be able to let my 1.5 year old son play safely with the toys there while I relaxed with my cup of coffee. There is also supposed to be a music time for babies/toddlers each weekday mornings so I will have to check that out soon sometime.

New Hot Pot is probably my closest take away, but it's also often my take away of choice even when I'm getting food delivered and have the option of pretty much anywhere.  It's a no-nonsense Chinese take away, they have an extensive menu covering all the basics, and I've never been able to fault anything I've ordered.   The spring rolls are great, and my go-to lemon chicken with fried rice has never let me down. They often have offers on if you spend a certain amount you get free items like prawn crackers.  Overall, it's not fancy and the prices reflect this. Good quality, quick service, dinner done.

This place is our local, as the staff are super lovely, the food is fast and always consistent. We've tried lots of dishes, my favorite being anything with veggies or shrimp. If you order over 15 pounds you get free prawn crackers and over 20 you get free spring rolls, which is nice. We order over the phone and it never takes longer than 20 minutes to get out food. The salt and pepper squid is nice as is the veggie hot & sour soup. I don't eat meat, but my boyfriend has had the ribs and he really likes them. The salted tofu is nice as well. They do seem to be mainly be a delivery based place, as there is always a JustEat guy collecting food, but it means it must be good, I can't speak for the delivery, but if you live near by and don't feel like cooking, this place is a good option.

A decent enough local Chinese takeaway, most of their business seems to come from telephone order or just-eat meaning deliveries can be a bit slow. If you actually venture into the New Hot Pot, you normally have to wait no more than ten minutes, however you do have to tolerate a lime green and red painted interior...  The food is tasty and I prefer their fried rice and noodles to any of the other Chinese establishments in the area. Nothing particularly special but a solid reliable takeaway. I just wish they had thought about the colour scheme, suddenly it makes sense why most orders are deliveries!

So good we went twice last week. Making me the Duchess ;)!  The Walnut is the latest addition to the hip happenings of Leith Walk. What used to be Cafe No.9 has now been transformed into a very cute French bistro.   We decided to treat ourselves one Friday after a long week at work and as it is over the road from us we couldn't really resist! Table booked and BYOB wine in hand we headed in.   The staff are delightful and we were shown to our table. This place is not big - about 8 tables - and they don't have printed menus as this changes daily. Instead they ask you to look at the chalkboard mounted on the wall. The Walnut offers a range of starters and mains, all are very reasonably priced, I go for the chicken liver parfait and David decides to throw a curve ball and orders the cheese board to start :-/. For main, the roasted cod for me and the lamb hotpot for David.  As I said our waitress is great, she is adorable and very attentive. Before I know it I'm devouring my parfait. It is delicious made even better by the homemade oatcakes, I only got two though. More, more, more please!   Our mains were equally as delicious. My fish was perfectly cooked. The portion sizes are generous but not over the top so we were nicely full.There is always room for desert however. I went for more cheese and David went for the chocolate tart - nom nom nom.   All this came to 40! Amazing!  Go - go now!  Cheers, Amy

i just didn't believe this small, rather inauspicious looking bistro could be as good as it was cracked up to be. Lots of people said it was awesome. Turns out, it is better. Yes it's small, almost down at heel but it's instantly one of my favourite eateries in Edinburgh. So basically this is a Scottish bistro.  Menu had beef, chicken, pork belly and a good selection of fish dishes, and decent vegetarian options.  I had Loch Fyne scallops with a caponade and parmesan; my dinner companion had rollmops. Both were delicious (that's saying something when it comes to rollmops, which i normally hate).  I then had 1/2 chicken with hazelnut leeks and companion had fish stew.  Everything was delicious, with the chicken about the best I have ever had, moist and seasoned to perfection. I couldn't resist sticky toffee pudding, which was like the real stuff I've had in Cartmel; sublime. We brought our own bottle but you they have a license and a wine list.  We ended our meal with coffee which was top notch, again a good sign given just how many restaurants don't seem to realise how mediocre coffee can spoil a lovely meal.  Excellent service at a very reasonable price (75).  One of the very best places I have been to in Edinburgh.

JESUS the food is good here!! Super small place (make reservations no matter what). Wow the food and service is simply outstanding!  This is a foodie place bar none... so don't be a fool and stay in the tourist areas for food, come here. Oh... did I mention it's inexpensive? Yeah... it pays to explore!

Small and with a casual ambiance, this lovely little restaurant makes you instantly feel like at home. Located on 9 Croall Pl, The Walnut offers a variety of extremely fresh and hearty foods, which are a real treat on a lunch break after a tiring morning spent at work. Among its incredibly tasty appetisers, you can also find fresh crab at really convenient prices, which is quite a rarity in Edinburgh. Both fish and meat can be found among the selection of mains on the menu and everything tastes like your grandma would have cooked it in the warmth of her own kitchen.

Zizzi wasn't particularly bad, and I've no complaints. Yet, I don't think I'll be a regular.   The only reason I decided to come here for dinner was because I had a gift card. We were there between lunch and dinner times for a late lunch and the restaurant was lacking in atmosphere.  The calzone was HUGE, definitely a case of quantity over quality as I was most blown away by the generous portion as opposed to the filling and flavours. Service was friendly too. Perfectly A-OK; nothing blowing me away.  Other than that, I don't have a whole lot to say other than that Edinburgh has far more interesting places to eat and some awesome little hidden gems worth seeking out. - All things considered, Zizzi is fairly unoriginal.

I ordered the Casareccia Pollo Piccante pasta on the waitress's recommendation, and its described as a pasta with spicy piccante chicken in a creamy sauce with fresh tomatoes and baby spinach. No. Just no. This was some of the most mediocre and lacking pasta I've ever had. First off, the sauce was more watery and runny than creamy, and I was not a fan. There were maybe 2 tomatoes total. The chicken pieces were tough and I prefer my chicken more tender. And the overall flavors were lacking, and more on the bland side than anything else. So clearly I did not like my main dish.   But at least the dessert turned out well. I ordered the Vegan caramelized biscuit cheesecake, which was a dairy-free cheesecake on a cinnamon biscuit base with crushed honeycomb. It was definitely good for a vegan dessert. I liked the added texture of the honeycomb (cereal?) crumbs and bits they added on top.  Total was 18.25 pounds and wasn't worth it considering how little I liked my main dish.

I would say Don't go.  Food has no flavor.  When I pointed out to the manager my red sauce was very watery she said, "That is the quality of our sauce."  My husband had pizza that he request that chicken be added.  The waitress took it back to the kitchen and they threw some chicken it and brought it back to the table. It didn't have any flavor either.

The pizza here was pretty good, but then again I'm comparing back to the states. Service was not so great - took a while to get our food, and a while to get the check. 4 stars for the pizza and 3 for service
I like thin pizza a lot. I ordered green goddess salad as my main dish. Unfortunately, the staff forgot my order and when they brought side salad (very small and dry salad) which cost us 3.5.

I am on their mailing list so had a 30% discount voucher off all main courses.  I met up with the girls for an early dinner after work and we had calzone and garlic bread.  They don't have any veggie calzones on the menu but did do one on request.  The mushroom calzone was actually very tasty and I loved the rosemary garlic bread with sea salt on top.  Not bad price too with the voucher.  I ordered a sprite and asked for no ice and a straw, they did a weird thing of pouring into a short tumbler but then adding a long straw that just kept falling out the glass as it didn't fit.  I quickly ditched that.    I liked the food and the new decor but the tables were squished too close together and it took an age to get the bill.  The decor and food are great, the staff were wandering about a bit and not achieving much!

when trying to book a table the last friday before christmas i was stuck.  phoning a few places clearly showed that even at 6pm they were all booked solid for the evening and with a my fingers crossed and last bit of hope i phoned Zizzi to see if there was the chance of a free table.  the man who answered the phone very happily assured me that there was and took my booking.  now i know edinburgh is all about the independent restaurants and bars, but sometimes the reliability of a chain does come in handy.  especially when you're wanting a relatively quick dinner at a decent price.  when we arrived friday we were shown a table in the middle of the dining room but after seeing another couple more from a table near the window which appeared quieter we asked to be moved there.  they happily accomdated us and we were soon sat contemplating menus.  after a rather lengthy wait trying to get our waitress' attention we eventually managed to order and food arrived shortly.  i think it's hard to do italian wrong and Zizzi definitely is a place that gets it right.  i had a chicken and spinach calzone which was really quite good, full of spinach and a bechamel sauce with a dried ham on top.  it could have used a bit more chicken but overall it was quite good.  the white wine we got with the meal was easy to drink and a good price.  the only downfall was the wait to actually order food when it appeared our waitress had actually forgotten that we existed.  however for a quick meal on one of the busiest friday nights of the year this was a good option.

Bland and generic sums it up really.  I ordered a skinny Pizza( guaranteed to be under 500 calories) and It was like chewing cardbboard ( not that I have ever munched on cardboard, but you know what I mean) I should have gone for the full fatty pizza, which I have to say are pretty tasty, So if you do go to zizz's order a pizza as they are they best option on the menu. The pasta dishes are created by the chef who then  thin decides what should go into it instead of what you order/expecitng. Value wise it isnt bad but I think youd be better going elsewhere for 8-13 per main course. The decor is sligtly clinical with all the metalic tables and everytme I removed myself from the table I banged my head on a low light and I am only 5'5 ish ( 5'8 with hair bun) so its not the best designed. Its an ok establishment for meeting for a quick meal and catch up with friends, but If I wanted to make it a special occasion then Id choose somewhere else.

Blah blah blah, the most boring place on Earth.  Not bad, just not as good as anything else Edinburgh has to offer if you put a little bit of effort into finding somewhere a little more stylish and unique. It's a chain that serves bland Italian food to work nights out - come on people, keep our independent restaurants afloat by not going to mass-money-makers like this.   You can tell when a restaurant is run by the accountants and not a real passion for food.

I hate to kick a restaurant when it's down, but I couldn't agree with the other reviewers more when it comes to this place. A real let down, and I wanted to like it so much!  A friend, who lives in Edinburgh, invited me for dinner one night when she had a massive cooker disaster. It totally died on her so we had to decide whether to eat in or take out, so we opted to get the heels on and make a night of it. Zizzi's had been recommended to my friend by her college lecturer, so we decided to try that.  It is the fast food joint of 'Italian' restaurants. Everything looks smashing on paper but just falls short of the mark in a lot of ways.  -Olives and bread with dipping oil. Good, but not enough for two ravenous girls like us. -Garlic bread. Tasteless. I think she may have misheard us and just brought us bread sans garlic. -Linguine Gamberini. My usual prawn and tomato pasta. Lacking in something, namely the prawns which I think must have been some of the smallest I have seen. Not impressed. It was also cold, not sure how they managed that one.  Not good guys. I would like to think we caught them on an off day but sadly, by the looks of other reviews, perhaps its just like this at all times.
Nice place , crowded almost always but in a good way,   food was ok , nothing special !   staff were friendly!   prices are ok!   wouldn't really choose to go back unless i had no other choice lol

Quite a good restaurant for a nice chilled out bite to eat. They have a good Italian menu with nice pastas on offer. The staff are very helpful and friendly but they do not really wear a uniform which can be a bit confusing if it is busy.  However the last time I went the menu had just changed over to the summer menu and the prices had gone up, thr portion sizes had went downa nd the pasta was overcooked, hopefully this was just a one off though as it is usually very nice!

Zizzi doesn't pretend. It's a chain eatery and suffers from all of the drawbacks associated with that, such as a bland atmosphere, generic decor, and generally un-Italian ambiance. But don't let that fool you, as the food is great for the most part. The calzone I had on my last visit was copious and very tasty, and the pizzas my table ordered were delicious and still managed to taste authentic. One of my friends, however, ordered pasta and was not very impressed, but he works as a chef so might be biased! The service is also really good, they are friendly and not overbearing and give you the right level of attention. Also, as far as locations go, you can't much more central than Zizzi. Whether you want to ramble through the old town after your meal or go drinking in the trendy new town area, you're only a brief stride from either.
The food was reasonable, not amazing, and since they had lost our reservation, we were squeezed into a corner near the bar, I doubt I would bother going back!

I have only ever been to this Zizzi once and everything about it screams average, my friend and I only went because of a two for one offer that I'd come across. When we arrived at the restaurant, it took ages for us to get a seat because of the throngs of office workers taking up all the tables. Although the restaurant was physically clean, it seemed a bit grotty to me (like the way that a McDonald's is grotty). Our food was pretty standard; I had a pizza, which was freshly baked but could just as easily have been one of Tesco's Finest, and my friend had a seafood pasta, which was somewhat lacking in seafood. The service was alright, but not particularly friendly or quick. I don't think I shall be returning.

The food here is FANTASTIC. I went for lunch with my dad the other day, which came to around 25 with a glass of wine and it's well worth it. There's a nice atmosphere and the food is good quality, but the staff were a bit snappy and impatient, so only four stars.

We read several reviews and noticed Spatch close by and a high rating. Nice food, decent menu and a good selection of drinks. We had the wings and Spatchcock chicken and both tasted great! I really liked the Garlic Ranch! Service wasn't the quickest but we were not in a hurry so it didn't worry us. Worth a visit if you're in the area debating what to eat. I would eat here again.

This place is REALLY GOOD!! First off we went to their sister restaurant off the royal mile first called Burgers and Beers. There was a small wait so they suggested this place. It's like a 3 minute walk from B &B.  We ordered their wings, home made fries, an appetizer, and a kids meal. The wings are very good!! I don't even like wings, but these are so tasty!! Goes very well with their fries! Their fries almost look like wedges, but so very good. Their appetizer we ordered was their crusted green beans. OMG!!! They were the best I've ever tasted!!! Dipped in their ranch, it was B. O. M. B.  ORDER THESE, you won't regret it! The childs menu has some good choices. My daughter ordered their Mac and cheese. It was good. The decor in here was super cute- straight up Farmhouse style!! The service was good as well.  Eat here. You won't be disappointed.  Enjoy!

I really didn't know what to make of spatch at first but once I read the menu online I knew I had to go!  But what to order?? Just a spatchcock chicken, the cluck Norris burger, Clint beastwood burger, Cheezus loves you?? Of course once I had stopped chuckling at the menu I settled on a cluck Norris, buffalo sauce and peanut butter milkshake.   Arriving you immediately smell the cooking chicken and it's rather like stepping into a dream if that's your thing.  I imagined myself as a character in an old cartoon when a wisp of a scent picks them up by the nose and they glide over to the dinner table.  The decor is becoming a fairly common look in Edinburgh, recycled pallets on he walls, funny artwork and rustic light fixtures.  Although I have seen this before at spatch you really believe you have walked through the finished front of a building into a shack constructed on the rear.  Anyway, the food!  Dear god, this redefined chicken burgers for me.  The bun is perfect, crispy lettuce and tasty mayo however all this pales in comparison to the main event. The chicken breast is huge, succulent, well seasoned and perfectly cooked.  Quite honestly the first one I had I picked up and totally forgot I had ordered a sauce.  On my second visit I took full advantage. I urge you to turn the burger on its side, pour buffalo sauce along the edge and then take the biggest bite you possibly can!  Repeat until your hands are empty!  I for one will be returning at every opportunity and at each attendance I will endeavour to explore the menu but I have a serious crush on a buffalo cluck Norris!

Stopped by here for dinner after looking for something just a little different from the normal fish and chips and we were quite happy with the choice.  Had the wings with a mixture of piri-piri and buffalo sauces and they were quite tasty.  Staff was very friendly as well (helped fix a shaky table we were at and stopped by several times to check on us).   I also ordered the BBQ beans (skip those, you don't get much but the waiter warned me in advance).    There's enough on the menu though that you shouldn't be disappointed.

The chicken was dry, to bad because the taste was good.  The brownrice in de salad was  kind of hard to chew. The hot sauce was really spicy & hot, I liked it. The beef rib portion was huge. The staff was real friendly and the place has a great ambiance. I really loved the leather bar seats. The strawberry mojito was excellent. Great place to sit and enjoy food with friends.

The John McIntyre Centre or JMC, is the canteen area for Pollock Halls students who are at the university on a catered basis. However, it is also possible for members of the public to purchase a one off ticket that allows entry to the canteen. Ordinarily students are granted entry to the buffet style canteen with ID confirming that they have paid for the catered option. I used the JMC during my first year at university. You often hear of people moaning at how disgusting an inedible the food is, but this is simply not True. The food is not the greatest, but it does allow you to have a good nutritional meal. There is plenty of salad available and fruit juice and plenty of a variety of fruits such as oranges, bananas and apples. There is also an "unhealthy" option if you so choose offering pizza and chips. I went to the JMC before it was refurbished but have subsequently returned by purchasing a one-off ticket and the layout is not much better, and the seating arrangement is a lot less prison-y with round tables rather than long regimented tables. Further, the layout of the food is also a lot neater and there are even more options to choose from, especially in regards to the salad.

It's okay. I mean during conferences and special events during the summer it's not bad. The rest of the year, it's not worth the money for what you can get somewhere that's so much better and way cheaper.

Excellent Turkish restaurant in Edinburgh where the food was delicious from start to finish.  Started with the saksuka which was amazing followed by the sigara boregi which was crispy and full of flavor.  Came with bread and a spicy sauce and yoghurt sauce on the side.  Adana kebob was juicy and flavorful but the real knock out was the karni yarik.  An amazing tomato sauce with a hollowed out eggplant half stuffed with minced spiced lamb which was out of this world.  Service was pretty fast and courteous and prices can stack up quickly but worth every pound.  Would love to come back and highly recommended.

Nice ambiance, friendly staff, and great food at very reasonable prices.  The kuzu (Lamb) dishes were amazing.  They had great flavors and were good quality meat.  When we get back to Scotland we will stop here again.

Delicious!  Best turkish food  I have had outside turkey x lovely friendly smiley staff xx Great portion sizes, between 3 people we shared baba ganoush, prawns, whitebait and calamari. All were very very tasty  (especially the prawns ) then we shared 2 mains the chicken with baba ganoush and yoghurt harissa which was moist and juicy with a fabulous chargrilled flavour and the sea bass with prawns and white wine sauce- yum yum yum (( if anyone was a fan of La Favorita ' s faggotini this tastes better!) . Finished off with Turkish tea and coffee and turkish delight. I am more than delighted and will be visiting again often. Xx

edinburgh is a place of many restaurants, but it seems that turkish cuisine is never too high on the list.  i think it's a bit of a shame as proper turkish food is so tasty so i was really glad to see a new restaurant opening up just along from the playhouse.  when my friend and i were looking for a place to go for dinner i suggested Ada and we booked a table.  i think this used to be one of the many indians that was along antigua street but i can't quite recall.  anyway the restaurant has been totally redone and made into a really welcoming and light space.  it's a bit strange as the front is domineered by the huge grill and you have to walk past this to get to the actual restaurant space.  when i first saw the restaurant was open i actually thought it was only a takeaway because of the huge grill and counter!  however the space is well laid out with lots of bright colours and a good number of tables although all of these were taken when we went on tuesday.  the menu is extensive and has the typical dishes you would expect- hummus, swarhma, hot and cold meze, falafel, etc but also has a bunch of dishes that were new to me.  after a debate between three dishes i went with karni yarik- minced lamb with peas in a tomato sauce on top of an aubergine all oven baked with rice and salad on the side.  we also shared hummus as a starter and were given a an aubergine type dip compliment of the chef.  the hummus was a large portion and given with fresh pide that was really moreish.  the smokey aubergine dip was really tasty as well.  my main course looked massive but being post run i managed to finish it all as it was too good to leave any over.  the minced lamb was incredibly savory and the aubergine was super tender.  it definitely enticed me to come back and try other dishes to see what else they offered.  service was probably the only downfall for this restaurant.  initially the waitress was prompt and very on top of things in terms of taking our ordering and bringing food.  but she never checked up on us during our meal or even asked if we wanted more drinks.  we had to pretty much throw ourselves in front of her to get the bill as well so they maybe need to keep their attentiveness throughout the whole service and not just the first half.  definitely a very good addition to this part of leith walk and i can't wait to go back!
So good! Great service and super friendly. Chicken shawarma was out of control. Don't judge it by looks. Go!

If you ever wondered what Charlie Sheen does to fill his time when not in appearing in court or filming Two and a Half Men, take yourself along to Cafe Truva on the Cannongate. The resemblance with one of the waiting staff there is so uncanny, you should really check this one out for yourself !!   That's not the only reason you should visit this cafe however. Cafe Truva is so good that I've visited twice. In the space of two days.   I think it's the incredibly friendly staff which makes this cafe stand out from its neighbours on the Royal Mile. That, and the Turkish authenticity of the food, the decor and the coffee.It's a great spot for lunch or a cuppa (on visit #1 I had a strong brew accompanied by a yummy muffin) with a varied, reasonably priced menu (on visit #2 I had a roast veg & hummous wrap- DELISH!). Full marks.

Maybe I arrived a little too late, but the service here was so-so.  I probably could have left without paying (but didn't).  The apple tea was okay and the desserts were tasty - but the prices were a little high (maybe because it's still in the tourist zone of medieval Edinburgh).
Came here on vacation for an afternoon snack. Staff could have been friendlier. Pricey for the desserts, $3.50 for 4 small chocolates. Turkish Apple tea was very flavorful. Restaurant was clean.
Had medi wrap and turkish salad. Both are good but not really worth the price. The medi wrap filled with chicken, cheese, and dried tomato but the composition of fillings wasn't proportional.

We got a groupon for dinner here. I don't know if I would every really be looking for a place to eat in that area, but I imagine a large amount of tourist pop through there. It was good  and well priced for a groupon get got a main, chicken shish and a glass of wine.  It had more of a quick stop in cafe feel about it and it closed earlier then it said on yelp... but might have just been that night. The people that worked there were really friendly and nice. They have a large selection of cakes and turkish treats which look delicious. We had a slice of chocolate orange cake which was once again good but nothing I'd order again.

We had a nice tea/coffee/hot chocolate/sweets break here in the afternoon as we headed down the Royal Mile. The food was good and they had outdoor seating which was nice on a sunny afternoon.   They are near the bottom of the hill and there are some nice shops across the street that sell woolens Made in Scotland unlike some of the tackier shops up the hill.

I spent 5 pounds to bought a cheesecake and tiramisu, the tiramisu is sooooo sweet taste, and the cheesecake can not take any cheese flavor, the cake it's so hard not soft at all.. be honest, these two cakes is the worst cake I had so far. just ate little bit, then I throw it away.. : (

Lovely little Turkish restaurant/cafe on the Royal Mile worth checking out if you fancy something different. The staff are very polite and attentive.  I couldn't quite work out if the place was a restaurant or a cafe, looking around I was noticing some people sitting down to a dinner with a glass of wine and others were simply drinking coffee and chatting. This I found a little strange but maybe this is the feel the owners are going for.  I had the soup and lamb moussaka lasagne and my fiancee had the Kofte Gratin, all were very well cooked, not too salty and were delivered well on the plate, you even got a little dolma on your plate which I have been missing since my last time in Turkey almost 2 years ago. After dinner we had a look at their cakes which take up a large portion of their front counter. Everything from Carrot cake to tiramisu and all of them looked beautiful.  The decor of the place was very 1990's Scottish cafe. Woodwork that was in need of a little varnish, carpets that had a design that Pink Floyd couldn't create at their most "creative" and couches that had almost the same design as the carpet that hadn't been touched up in quite a long time.  Overall we had a very nice and enjoyable night and would recommend people to try here if you are at this end of the Royal Mile and fancy something different for dinner.

Nice little Turkish cafe :)  Nice selection of cakes and pastries, very scrummy. Turkish coffee was yum & latte not bad either!   We ordered sandwiches and they were okay - it cost  20 for 2 sandwiches and two coffees, which i thought was a little overpriced.   They chap who served us was super friendly.

The chain of Cafe Truva's are fast becoming a hit with me. Armed with a craving for cake, we marched through the crowds (even on such a rain drenched Sunday) wandering the Royal Mile watching Fringe groups tout their trade to find a coffee shop that would sate my need. Cafe after cafe we wandered until we hit Cafe Truva which had a nice looking array of choice. We plumped for two coffees, a slice of cherry and custard cake as well as a slice of apple and caramel tart. Both were super sweet. The cheery bit through the very custardy custard, while the caramel was the main star of the tart with strong support by the apple (could have been more apple though). The coffee helped clean up all that sugar.   Here, the service is very friendly and it was only when I paid (fifteen quid for the above) did I make the connection with the cafe in Leith. Turns out there is another at Tollcross (I think) which our waiter rated pretty highly. Seeing that I have been to two now, it would only be fair to visit the third, just, well, you know, because. It's a hard life, I tell you, but I'll do it, if only for the sake of Yelp.

This is a cozy little Turkish breakfast spot in Edinburgh. I liked it so much I came several days in a row. The cappuccino is delicious, and the breakfasts also sometimes include dolmas and olives sides. Yum!  The staff was very friendly, and the owner gave us a couple of free dolmas each time we came in, because we loved them so much.   This is a great spot to curl up and read the paper in the morning, or get some work done, while you enjoy a scrumptious breakfast.

A cheerful alternative to the corporate face of Starbucks. I love their coffee, the staff are always friendly and the wooden furniture inside has a rustic charm. Great for a light lunch or snack stop when on the Mile.

I'm surprised Cafe Truva hasn't been reviewed more and I'm disappointed by the low scores as I thought it was amazing! It's located at the bottom of the Royal Mile and like most cafes in the area, is always choc-a-block. Like most cafes on the Royal Mile, I had my reservations when I sat down for a cup of apple tea wondering if it was just an overpriced tourist trap cafe with no substance. When I saw their HUGE selection of tasty cakes all was forgiven and I spent ages deciding what cake to go for.   As it is a Turkish cafe, Cafe Truva has an excellent selection of Turkish foods and teas and as I looked around at other patrons I could see that there wasn't one thing on the menu that I wouldn't have liked.   I devoured my large slice of chocolate cake in mere minutes and sipped my apple tea whilst doing a spot of people watching.  Overall, this is an excellent cafe. It may be busy all the time, but I guess that says something in itself. Once you've had a slice of cake from here, you'll be going back time and time again for more.

I personally really like Cafe Truva. Perhaps because I am big fan of apple tea and finding somewhere inexpensive where its readily available is a rare find.  Cafe Truva is a Turkish cafe located at the bottom end of the Royal Mile, the slightly less tourist exploited end. It isn't the cheapest cafe, but its not bad, especially by Royal Mile standards.  I've been several a times and each time the staff have been very welcoming and accommodating. Apart from tea and pastry (which is lovely), breakfast at cafe Truva is also a surprising treat (served all day).  A potential tourist trap, Cafe Truva turns out to be much more, selling decent Turkish meals and snacks, good coffee, and all importantly apple tea.

A decent bar if you're in the area- best avoided during the day if you're not into sports though as on my last visit it was over-run with football fans. I've had a good Saturday night here - it's particularly student friendly.

Where do you start with the Three Sisters? We went there to watch a EURO 2012 match in the hope that we could watch outside on the big screen in the nice weather  it was cold and wet  so we went inside and found a table in there. There is a fair sized bar with plenty of staff who were always busy serving and clearing tables but the bar does always seem to be really busy. Our round of drinks which consisted of 3 pints of lager, 1 pint of Guinness and 1 vodka mixer came in at about 20, which seems a bit overpriced to me, especially as later on they started serving them in plastic glasses which is never a good thing. The toilets are terrible. I don't know what the ladies are like, but the gents toilet is tiny and nowhere near fit for purpose. The bar was mainly full of men, so there are always queues to get in which is really annoying. The worst part of our visit was of course, the clientele. The pub seems to consist pretty much only for visiting English stag and hen parties so as you can imagine, it's not much fun for those of us who want a good, but quiet night out. However, I think the courtyard is a great idea with a big screen and bbq on the go and I'm sure it will be great to watch a game there if we ever get a summer, but I don't think I'll be going back to give it a try.   A generous 2 stars from me.
Another very busy at the weekend/during rugby/football games pub. If the weather is good, its great to sit in garden courtyard on picnic benches. Food served on BBQ outside in good weather too.

rowdy n' raucous bar heaving with kids. hurling distance from the grassmarket. not-so-faint aroma of vomit permeates. it's a "must" stop on any drunken pub crawl of the grassmarket area. much quieter during the week, though.

Oh Three Sisters, how I love to loathe you. I used to like the place, but perhaps I've matured and can't handle it anymore. The bouncers, for starters, are power-hungry idiots who use their only bit of influence in the world turning back potential paying customers. If you're in a group that happens to consist of a slightly higher male-to-female ratio, you won't be let in. If you do get in, there is no room to move, and the queue at the bar is about 6 people deep. No happy mediums here. Everyone who visits Edinburgh has heard of this place and wants to go there, so I would like to put an end to the reputation as a must-see place. There are so many other places to go that are far less aggravating.

My night spent in the Three Sisters took on two very distinct, and very different characteristics.  Lets start with the good part of the night. A fine summers evening had drawn us to the huge outdoor seating area of the Three Sisters, and as my friends bought the drinks and a Three Sisters BBQ blazed in the corner, I had an excellent time. The atmosphere was great and generally I had a very large amount of fun.   However, then the second half happened - it was getting busier and attracted a hen party and a seperate stag party, which generally ruined the chilled, relaxed and fun vibe that we had before. The night was also growing colder so we moved indoors - well, I say moved, i mean we jammed ourselves inside bearly able to move in a hot mass of drunken people. I attempted to buy a drink next, and after waiting for nearly 10 mins, a round for 3 people came to almost 25 - extorsionate.  So there you have it - get there early and you will have a great time, get there after everybody else does, and you might not want to come here again.

Ok, when I was politely asked by my friend if we could nip in here when she came through to visit I was powerless to say no. Not because I was massively eager to go here, but because I hate saying no to my friends!  We turned up here around 4ish on a Wednesday afternoon to find it was shut until five. Alright, that's acceptable, it is January. So we went on to Oz Bar had a drink there and returned around 5ish when it opened. Needless to say, we were the only people there! BUT I like this bar, it reminds me very much of Waxy O'Connors in Glasgow, except much more reasonably priced drinks. It is kinda dark and dingy inside, kinda like a generic Irish bar, but I quite like that, gives it something resembling an atmosphere. And this place is huge! Plenty of room for moving around if it is a little crowded.  So, the staff were fine. The chap serving us was very nice, got us drinks but it did take a little while before all the cutlery and menus etc were put out on the table. Think this might be because they were setting up for a private function, but we were in no rush. The menu - if you don't like pizza or burgers you are kinda a little shafted. It was definitely not the sort of food I was expecting, it was better. I ended up plumping for the Godfella, a burger with pepperoni, sundried balsamic tomatoes and little balls of mozzarella. Yet again, I was not setting the bar too high, I mean, Holyrood 9a anyone!? This burger was immense. I mean really delicious. Plus they had a deal on for January, get any main meal and get the second for 1p. Hells yes I will.  So basically, we had two burgers, and 4 drinks. Less than twenty squidders. Boom. I want another one of those burgers NOW.

On occasion I have gone to The Three Sisters and it has been dead, other times you can barely move. Usually during the week its pretty empty with only a few guys watching the football or having something to eat.  The actual bar is quite nice with big tables and a large outside seating area with patio heaters and umbrellas. Crucial in this climate! Usually in the summer it is jam packed as they have screens outside with football/rugby on and a BBQ going.   By the time it gets to about 9 o'clock on the weekend this bar can be horrendous. Horrendous in a full of pub crawls/stag and hen dos sort of way. This seems to be the hot spot for these groups so as you can imagine it can get very rowdy with the odd fight or two and someone throwing up in the corner. I personally do not enjoy bars like this, too much pink cowboy hats and 'lads on tour' going on for me.   I have been to The Three Sisters and had a good time, more often than not you will make a friend from Australia while sharing a table outside so it can be fun. But lately I bypass it because from the outside it looks like its brimming with lager louts and incredibly drunk students.

Jumped in here to see one of the shows on at the fringe and enjoyed a relaxed drink beforehand with no hassles.  Reasonably priced with a decent food menu I regrettably didn't have the time to try out. It included champ! You don't get that everywhere.
