Their chocolates cone in all shapes and sizes (and prices) and they also have wines and ports that pair well with chocolates. Their port that goes with milk chocolate was delicious! They also have a neat home cooking items and I bought some chocolate pasta that I am excited about trying!  The best-kept secret about this place is that they have an amazing cafe area in the back. Their drinkable chocolate is to die for! I was surprised by how good the chili drinkable chocolate was, too, but I think the classic one is my favourite. I need to come back to try their mocha and other coffees!

The best part about this place is how innovative their flavor combinations are, because although the quality is great, there are lots of places to get quality chocolate. The prices are high, but in this case, I think justified. It's a great place for gifts because everything is packaged well, and there are a few sales if you buy multiples.   There is also a cafe in the back, as many people here have mentioned, which is clean and tiny. The wi-fi didn't work when I went, but it was okay, as I didn't plan on staying long. Trying to be healthy this week, I got one of the cocao infused teas (tea leaves & cacao nibs) which, at 2.20 is very reasonable. The hot chocolate was 3.50, but when something is unique and high quality, it will be expensive. The flavors change, and specials are posted on the board.   The staff is great as well, attentive without being all over you.
Impressive chocolate menus, many interesting chocolates and I highly recommend their white chocolate drinks( delicious!!)

This is one of the few places in town that, when you feel like you want to pig out and have a huge sugar hit, you can go to and be safe in the knowledge that everyone else in the store is feeling the exact same way.  Very nice touches include seasonal designs on their chocolates and offers and the staff are usually walking around offering free samples, which is always a winner in my book. For dark chocolate lovers, this little shop of high blood sugar levels offers 100% dark chocolate. 3 different types in fact!  The cafe is a lot more spacious than it looks which is always good because it looks tiny. I went for the salted caramel hot chocolate which was amazing. I'm not a hot chocolate connoisseur but I would say that a company that specialise in making chocolate that isn't mass produced crap are probably going to be one of the top dogs in the hot chocolate world.  Friendly staff, delicious smells and a huge abundance of sweet brown sugary goodness all around. Enjoy.
Really friendly staff... Love their drinking chocolate... Several deals too!

So glad that Yelp picks places like Hotel Chocolat for their event evenings!  We were able to sample praline hearts and peach and champagne chocolates, delicious. The gingerbread hot chocolate was very tasty indeed but the chilli was too spicy for me.   We got a hand massage trying out the new hand wash, scrub and lotion, makes me want to go to StLucia to go to their Spa!  I can see why it was a max of 20 people, any more and it would have been too busy.  The manager Mark Joyce is very knowledgeable and happy to help.  Been here a few times and really like the chocolates, my current favourite are the mojito truffles, I have to ration them to stop me eating them all at once!  This is top end of the market quality and it is worth it.

i don't even know where to start this review.  Hotel Chocolat is a magical place like a store version of Willy Wonka's chocolate factory but slightly classier and minus the oompa loompas.  but the chocolate....wow is pretty much the only way to describe it.  my first encounter with Hotel Chocolat was stumbling upon a shop during a trip to York.  i was so excited to see so many varieties of chocolate truffles available in addition to great big slabs of chocolate with various flavours.  i couldn't help myself and bought up about 30 worth of the selector boxes :)  my boyfriend was less than pleased with my lack of self control, until i offered him some....  when this wonderful shop opened in Edinburgh i was super excited!  the shop had all the amazing chocolates plus a little cafe to get chocolate based drinks!!  hello lover :)  i try to limit my visits as when i go into this place i tend to come out with a bag full of chocolate treats and a rather empty wallet.  but it's so worth it!  the salted caramel truffles are a favourite, but i've also enjoyed the purely praline truffles, and the bellini truffles with a hint of champange and a kick of peach, and the lemon berry truffles, and the millionaires shortbread, and well the list goes on and on.  my boyfriend says the whiskey truffles are marvelous and we both enjoyed the chilli ones.  i also have to say the gingerbread hot chocolate is maginificent!!  oh this shop, i can't stop singing its praises!  not only is the chocolate a delicious treat, but the staff could not be friendlier or more helpful.  i'm sooooo glad we have this lovely little haven in Edinburgh :)  when i've managed to demolish my latest supply of chocolates i will definitely be back for more.

Hotel Chocolat is a chocoholic's dream come True.  I'm not sure how this happened, but I have only been here once before, so when a Yelp event was organised, I promptly signed up!  We had the store to ourselves after shopping hours, and got a chance to sample some delicious hot chocolate with cardamom and another one with chili. Also there was a selection of chocolates to be tasted.  Hotel Chocolate makes the most of its space. There are wall to wall displays of chocolates with various fillings and flavourings on offer. It was so difficult to make a choice.. but I ended up buying a 250g variety box.  In the back of the shop there is a small cafe area where you can have coffee, tea, cakes etc.   The staff were very friendly and helpful. If you are buying a gift, this place is great as the chocolate is of high quality and the packaging is very elegant.  They offer something for everyone! e.g. if you are concerned about eating too much sugar, fear not - there is a 'Less Sugar more Cocoa' selection available.   I will be back... :)

Admittedly, I am somewhat of a self-professed food snob. I walked in to a tasting even here last night, and was excited to see so much chocolate, presented in such a minimalist, classy manner. The service at this event was superb, with extremely attentive staff, complimentary prosecco and a soothing hand massage using cocoa butter and cocoa nibs.  I have come in here previously and bought the pistachio pralines for myself, and the eaton mess slab for my boyfriend (he's more of a white chocolate kinda guy). They were both nice, especially the pistachio pralines, though the actual chocolate was not perfect. Looking at the ingredients, there are just as many mysterious ingredients in this chocolate as there are in well known brands like cadburies, if not more! Hotel chocolat still find it acceptable however, to sell a box of chocolates for 58.   The chocolates we tasted at the event were good, though I wouldn't describe them as luxurious. I particularly like the lemon one and the heart stuffed with cashew nut butter. The hot chocolate, I must admit, was a let down. I am used to thick Italian or Spanish hot chocolate, or at least hot chocolate with more of a rich kick. The hot chocolate here felt quite watery in comparison.   Though I felt as though there were quite a few gimmicks which used cheap ingredients dressed in fancy packaging (reassurances to those who have more money than sense, maybe), the dark chocolate at the end was serious stuff, was made of very natural ingredients and had a very strong taste. This is the kind of stuff which is worth good money. I especially liked the dark chocolate with a touch of chili.  All in all, the service here is wonderful, the staff are extremely pleasant, but the chocolate (for the most part), I feel, has a lot of pretensions to live up to. If I really had to spend a lot of money on good chocolate, I think I would go to the chocolate tree in Bruntsfield, where the ingredients are very natural and made on the premise. If I had a really bad sugar craving, I would go to buy an unpretentious bar of good quality milk chocolate, instead of buying commercial chocolates in disguise at hotel chocolat.  That said, do try it and I especially recommend the dark chocolate. Hotel chocolat also offer some quite unusual goods, like chocolate pasta and cocoa infused balsamic vinegar. I didn't try these but it's tempting, just for the novelty!

Hotel Chocolat is easily my favourite Chocolatier in Edinburgh!!  I have been in numerous times before, either for some delicious chocolates or for a coffee, and ive been a fan for quite a while, so when i saw their was a Yelp evening, I thought yaaaayyy!!! .......What a great evening! We were allowed to have a nosey around the shop after hours and, i am not joking when i say i could have bought everything! We were treated to a selection of chocolates, ginger hot chocolate and chilli hot chocolate that was just divine! I was then treated to a luxurious hand massage with their new range beauty range! ****happy carolann***** The staff were fantastic and Mark the manager was very helpful, when picking special chocolates for a gift!! I love love all the Yelp events, but I think this could be one of my favourites!!  Thank you Jenny and Hotel Chocolat for a srummy, wonderful evening :)

I've become slightly addicted to Hotel Chocolat. It is pricey but the great quality products are addicted and they do great truffles - I love the Kir Royale truffles.   There are usually samples of sorts to try, there are GF and vegetarians chocs and sweets and students - flash your card to get 5% off your purchase.  There is a little cafe at the back - the hot chocolate (real melted hot chocolate!) is pure luxury and delicious!

Small quiet cafe/bar down a small close off the Royal mile directly opposite Deacon Brodies Pub. Not a huge variety on the menu, but nice simple well priced food and drinks. The walls are painted with a mural depicting the life of the cafes namesake.

Really cute atmosphere. There are picture frames on the walls and lights throughout the cafe as well as a fireplace. We went at 9 in the morning for breakfast and were seated right away (table for 2). We ordered the eggs and they were OK.   The waitstaff is very friendly and polite. The bathrooms were clean. No free wifi!   Great location off the royal mile near the cathedral.

I think this place is a typical touristy joint that doesn't spring for service because it doesn't have to. Which is unfortunate because the decor is really lovely, and the building is very interesting. The food here was decent enough, if not overpriced, but the service I experienced was very, very slow and unfriendly.    I came here for an early breakfast, as it was one of the few places open at 8 AM on a Sunday. There were a few other people in the cafe, but it was far from full.   After our order went in, the kitchen staff and the servers just stood around chatting with each other for a good 15 minutes. I don't like to bash service, but it took nearly half an hour (!) to get a bagel with cream cheese and smoked salmon, and a cup of coffee (the bagel wasn't even toasted or anything... there is no reason this should have taken so long). My latte was also literally just a cup of steamed milk with what seemed like a drop of espresso in it... not sure if that was a fluke... I was in a hurry so I didn't bother asking for a new one, maybe I'll give them the benefit of the doubt?   Short version: the place was virtually empty, but it still took 30 minutes to get a bagel, and my coffee had no coffee in it.

A nice place that opens fairly early and has some pretty good options for breakfast. I've only ever stopped for some take away breakfast, which are usually the morning rolls, scones, or bagels.  Coming in early in the morning means there isn't much of a wait. The staff is nice and the service can be a bit slow but when one isn't in a hurry it's all right. (Not so good if you're in a hurry.) The interior is homey and seems pretty cozy. There are tables outside but I think I'd prefer inside if I were to eat in.  The bagels and rolls are good but the scones are better. I particularly like the apple and cinnamon scone, either on its own or with some nutella (when the scones sometimes seem to be a bit on the dry side). The portion sizes are fine with the prices just a tad much for what is offered.  Having said all that, I do like it and come back when I have more time in the morning to spare.
A nice place to catch a fine breakfast. Enjoyed it outside, even as we had to face the chilly september winds raging through the narrow alley.
We only had the cream tea, but the scones were perfect! Highly recommend!-----The shortbread was perfect!-----Great central location

Best breakfast in Edinburgh. Apple & cin. Scone with butter and jam was amazing as well as the black tea that came along. Also came back for lunch to have a wonderful veggie soup with a cheese scone. Prices were great, great atmosphere and attentive staff.
With 4 staff on it still took ten minutes to prepare a bacon roll at breakfast time, 1.75 for soft drinks struck me as expensive and I was short changed by 2. All in all not a good experience.

Popped in here for a quick coffee recently. Lots of tables outside, none of which had been cleared and we had to clear one ourselves. Hubby got the coffees and a bit cake for himself and it was very expensive and not terribly good. Staff couldn't care less and if they spent more time clearing tables instead of having a sly fag round the corner or speaking on the phone, they would have had more custom  3 times people came in when I was there, looked round at the mess, and left. No good for business guys! Can't really recommend it and won't be back myself.

Directly opposite Brodie's Tavern which is an overpriced tourist trap, I expected Deacon's House cafe to be pretty much more of the same.  I was pleasantly surprised then, when down the end of a wee close sat the quaint little cafe, which was full of tourists, granted, but very reasonably priced and cosy.  I was in there on my own, which I don't do often, and the staff were very nice and perhaps made a little extra effort to chat to me more because I was a nigel no pals! I had the soup and sandwich deal which was only just over 5. The lentil broth was tasty and piping hot, perfect for dipping my cheddar and ham sandwiches in. Bliss! For the deal and a coffee I left with a good couple of quid change from a tenner, which you can't often say after lunching on the Royal Mile!

Great little place down a Close off the High Street. You can actually feel the history and there are charming murals around the walls of the cafe with scribed explanations.   The atmosphere is as delightful as the staff, who couldn't have been friendlier or more helpful, making both children and the oldies like me very welcome.   The sandwiches and cakes are fresh and delicious, include all the favourites like smoked salmon, empire biscuits, good coffee, and best of all it's all very clean.   A True Scottish experience with friendly smiles all round.   Recommended.

This place was on the same street where Fringe festival was happening. We had to stop here as it was about to rain. I got Fish and chips and my wife got Chicken stuffed with Haggis. The food was good specially the gravy that came with the Chicken dish. The buttery gravy was the highlight of our dinner. We choose a table near a outlet so we could charge our phones as well. Overall good experience with friendly staff.

Extremely great atmosphere and attention to detail, the wall mural telling the story of Brodie was great fun to look at!  The cafe is in a great location, that isn't a far walk from the castle at all, the food was delicious though there was not enough vegetarian options, making us have a select breakfast of cakes, sweets and bagels (though i'm not complaining!) I recommend anyone in the area to stop by and have a bagel and coffee on their travels, can't wait to come again!
Lovely cafe! Had the hot chocolate with whiskey (and it was strong) and chocolate ginger tea! Both were delicious. Stay away from the fudge squarer...it was extremely sweet

Easy place in a great location for a nice meal. I went for breakfast and had a their cream tea. My husband had the bagel with cream cheese with a latte. Lots of simple options and all done really well in a cute little shop! They have nice outdoor seating off of the street for a nice day, but it was too cold when we went.

The first morning we got dropped of at Victoriastreet and were advised by our uber driver to go here. We absolutely loved it! It speaks history of the old town, the food was delicious and the staff was friendly also (hence why we went back the morning after). We felt really welcomed

I really enjoyed the food at this adorable, tucked-away cafe. I ordered the scone and tea on my first visit, and then a piece of millionaire shortbread on my second. Both were amazing and left me wanting more! Service could be a little better, as it seemed like we were rushed out of there after we finished, but the desserts were worth it.

Located near the Scottish Castle on Royal Mile in one of the prime spots.  The cafe has a figure of Deacon Brodie leading into a corridor and then the actual cafe. The place is rather small with seating inside as well as some outside. One must place the order at the register and they give you a waiting number which you display on your table and they will bring out the food to you.   They have cakes, crepes, tea, soups, sandwiches for lunch but the food was rather disappointing. Had the tuna sandwich along with apple scone and cafe latte. The sandwich did not have any taste to it and the scone was very crumbly and barely edible. Coffee was ok. Service was very slow and they took a long time to bring it out despite a reminder to the server. Very unfriendly at the register as well as serving too - everyone was just rushing by and were not courteous at this busy hour. I did not go back to this place and will not recommend to anyone.

Deacons house cafe was very busy despite it being hidden away from the main drag. The staff were very friendly and on the ball at all times, quick to clear tables and any spillages, quick to serve. The food, especially the cream cheese and salmon bagel was delicious and a pot of tea which all came to 9:10 which I thought was fair. The atmosphere was cosy and warm and there were points of interest on the wall; murals and information about Deacon Brodie, however unless the cafe was empty it was hard to take a good look around without breathing on peoples food while they eat but I would definitely recommend.

I'll admit to never having a scone before, but if this was my first in 41 years, it was well worth it. Holy cow. The apple and cinnamon scone was delicious, and clotted cream is ... whoa. Amazing. Even the cappuccino was fantastic. What a great little spot.

Excellent meats and great mash!  Staff was accommodating when we came in with 5 people and they were pretty packed.  We squeezed into a table for 4 and made it work.  We tried 3 different meats and 3 different mashed and enjoyed them all.  I also recommend the smoked sausage skins!
Great food and great service at this place. Who knew such great things could happen to mashed potatoes!

So good! I had a hard time deciding what kind of sausage and mash combo I wanted to make because they all sounded so good! I loved the food and I felt really welcomed which was really nice as I was traveling solo. I will definitely go again when I am in Edinburgh.

I intended to have a late lunch/early dinner on my way to the train station. But sadly this was not to be. When I arrived at 15:30 I was informed that they were only serving desserts and drinks. As I was tired and hungry I opted for the sticky toffee pudding and a black coffee.   The coffee was lovely, the pudding was okay except it wasn't very warm - I prefer my ice cream to melt on top. Whilst dining I checked the venue website and couldn't find any times for lunch and dinner menus. As if I'd known that hot food wasn't served for a couple of hours I could have planned my trip differently.

Had the haggis mash. Was good. I would recommend taking a mash that is not meat heavy, like garlic, to blend the flavours better. Had the black pudding mash and the black pudding was dry in it.  The sausage egg and hash started was really good.  The ox cheek was tender but tasted earthy.  Would recommend taking only 2 plates per person, as they are way bigger than on yelp photos.

Lovely staff, and so cosy on a cold day!  We were chilled to the bone after a day at the zoo, so here was a welcome place to sit.   Super lovely staff, nice range of drinks, and just lovely food. Stovies for starter, which really warmed me up, well seasoned and perfectly cooked, melt in the mouth meat and we both had the mussels for main, served in a big pot with excellent rustic bread, and they were lovely, quite possibly some of the best i've had, and in a really rather large good portion, especially with the value for money! Definitely a fan.
The English/Scottish food was great! Not very big, but busy in early May. Pretty tight seating, but we found this to be common in the UK....

I had the whiskey chicken and the crispy bacon and scallion mash. The chicken was fantastic and perfectly cooked and tender. The mash was awesome. The seasonal veggie was beets. I was apprehensive at first, but they were delicious. They seemed to have a "mulled cinnamon" flavor. My husband got the haggis with honey and turnip puree. He said it was five stars. We topped it off with the toffee pudding and caramel sauce. Five stars again! It was actually semi-gooey cake with toffee sauce throughout and caramel sauce underneath-with a scoop of ice cream. We left happy!

Fabulous! I had the lamb shank and it was done perfectly. There was also a order of duck confit and was good also a. The mashed potatoes are a treat! I sampled the mustard style and the horseradish sauce style. Both were equally good and worth getting again. Friendly staff and relaxed atmosphere worth it if you have the time and are in the area.

I stopped in without reservation and was very friendly greeted by one if the waitstaff to be sat anyway. Throughout my meal it was a combined team effort by the three employees to help me, and they were all more than willing and kind!   I got a cider and haggis, because when you visit Scotland you have to have haggis at least once. Well, it was absolutely amazing, and a large enough portion served with mashed potatoes (I got cheddar and chive), that you don't go hungry (: I suggest to anyone passing through Edinburgh to give this place a go, definitely worth it!

We came here as part of the Eat Walk Edinburgh food tour but it was a great stop! Very happy we got to come by here as I was introduced to two great items. 1) Black Pudding AKA Blood Sausage and 2) Edinburgh Gin. The black pudding was surprisingly tasty and wasn't expecting to like it, but I did! And then we had a the Edinburgh Gin in the Raspberry flavor mixed with prosecco and it was the perfect little cocktail. Really great stuff. Seems like a very nice place to come for a full meal. If we had more time I would have tried to stop back.

We came here on a weekday around 6pm without a reservation and were seated immediately.   First time eating haggis. Mini haggis was an excellent dish and I really liked it with the turnip and potato and a great sampler to see if you like this Scottish cuisine.   Ox cheek with blood sausage mashed potatoes also fantastic. Ox cheek very soft. Hard to taste the blood sausage since it was mixed into the mashed potatoes.   Fries with haggis was decent. I prefer the mini haggis because I couldn't really taste the haggis with the fries.   Solid dishes here to try Scottish dishes. Unfortunately I didn't get to try the Scottish eggs because they ran out.

Great food, really happy I found this place. Everything we ordered was delicious & the staff was really helpful and friendly. I think this was one of the best meals we had in our 3 day stay in Edinburg.

Such a great lunch stop!  If you're ever craving mashed potatoes, this is the place.  The wild boar sausage, Scottish cheddar and spring onion toppings made it perfect and kept me going the whole afternoon.

Secret tip: the vegetarian haggis and sausages are actually the same thing but shaped and cooked slightly differently. I opted for the sausages as they were supposed to be less 'mushy'.   Best veggie sausages ever? No, not quite. But they were good enough. Mash was decent but nothing spectacular. I was a bit disappointed that it only came with a bit of gravy and coleslaw.   My partner's gammon, while tasty, came as a thick slab which made is difficult to cut and eat. He would have preferred thinner slices.   That said, great selection on the menu. Something for everyone! And fun lively environment too.

Thanks to the Yelp Community for helping me and my friends find this fantastic dinner spot. It was very crowded when we arrived but we were given a pager and told we could go next door to the bar and have a drink while waiting for our table.  When seated we ordered a Scotch Egg appetizer (delicious) then went on to a different Mash for each of us. We ordered the beef haggis (A perfect introduction for someone who is never had it and afraid to try it), the Beef Skirt Mash and the Bonnie Prince Chicken Mash. All were outstanding and flavor and the portions were very generous. For dessert we split a Sticky Toffee Pudding Cake, the perfect sweet ending for an indulgent meal.

Yelp and Trip Advisor were spot on with all the great reviews of this place -- only a stone's throw from The Castle. Casual atmosphere yet fabulous food -- best place we went to in Scotland for AUTHENTIC SCOTTISH FOOD at a very reasonable price. Pick your main which comes with one of the many versions of their "Mash" (potatoes) 1. Haggis Starter -- came with mash and parsnips -- not strong at all -- a good "introduction" to haggis which you have to try. Tastes like minced beef with spices.  10/10 2. Lamb Shank - Falling of the bone tender with mild spices -- this dish was a real winner with a generous portion. 9/10 3. Honey Soaked Gammon - their version of ham but BETTER. 9/10 4. Desert - Sour Cherry Cake with White Chocolate Ice Cream (we usually get Sticky Toffee Pudding but was told this is the one to get here -- and it was amazing! 10/10 -- Don't pass this up!  Too bad we were only in Edinburgh for two days as I could eat here regularly -- HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

A fantastic place for our first meal in Scotland! Very convenient to the Royal Mile. We had two appetizers, haggis and the crowdie salad. This was our first haggis and it tasted just fine, like a good meatball. My husband had beer and I was happy they had Thistly Cross cider. Our main meals were sausage (for my husband) and orange duck. Again, everything was great. I've never seen my husband enjoy mashed potatoes so much! He thought the horseradish mash was incredible. Really, we found this place well worth the acclaim.

Thank you, Yelpers! Yet again, a tasty experience I probably never would have stumbled upon had it not been for finding the reviews of this eatery located an alley/block removed from The Royal Mile hustle and bustle. We were curious about the "mash" menu and had to experience it for ourselves. The mashes are smashed potato variations ranging from chive and cheddar to horseradish that paired beautifully with entrees like pot roast (crazy tender- the star of the show at our table).   In addition to the pot roast, we ordered the rhubarb soda (locally made and delicious), honey carrot soup, beets and local cheese salad, and a variety of the mashes. The horseradish was my favorite. The waitress was very sweet and friendly and you could tell this business was passionate about sharing their story and highlighting local Scottish farmers and producers through the clever layout of the menu. If you're looking for a spot outside, they have three or four picnics tables available under the tree. This ended up being one of our favorite meals during our time in Scotland.

My husband and I were in the mood to try some traditional Scottish food, so after some Yelp research, this place made my list of bookmarks. It was quite busy for mid-afternoon on a Tuesday, but we were able to get a table without a reservation; however, the service was a bit on the slower side. I should have known, being in the heart of the tourist area near The Royal Mile and castle, what I would likely be getting us into. The quality and taste of the food, in my opinion, is not worth the higher prices here. I ordered the lamb shank with spring onion and smoked sausage mash (I asked our server for their mash recommendation to pair with the lamb; I should have just picked myself, as I was disappointed that the sausage tasted quite a bit like hot dog). Parts of the lamb were tender and moist and others were dry and rough. I thought the Shiraz wine I selected paired well with the flavor of the lamb, which was mainly what I liked about my meal. My husband ordered the chicken with black pudding mash (just go with it, don't ask what's in it because it won't sound appetizing) and thought it was okay. The chicken was slightly overcooked (borderline dry) and didn't have much flavor to it. He enjoyed his IPA beer. The portions are pretty large and heavy. Overall, although this place seems overpriced, I'm glad we tried it for the novelty of having the opportunity to eat some traditional Scottish food; however, we weren't impressed and wouldn't return.

I ate here in July when some friends were visiting from the US and I wanted them to try haggis. We had their two course lunch meal (I think it was ~15 pp) and a nice glass of prosecco with strawberry puree. We started with smoked salmon and then had their version of haggis, neeps, and tatties for the main which was really delicious. The haggis was not overpowering and it was extremely high quality. The restaurant has a nice vibe, casual but 'upscale' enough for a special lunch and/or dinner. I will definitely be back!

This is a nice Scottish sit down restaurant with a few items on a lunch menu ranging 8-10 and a full bar with local specialty beers.   I have been here a few times, having a steak sandwich (very nice though slightly tough and small for the American palate), neaps and haggis (good if you like haggis), and stokkie. This has become a regular for nicer business lunch.   Just recently had the stokkie and was pleasantly surprised. Basically a soupy dish with potatoes, cabbage, and savory ham hock, and topped with a few slivers of steak. Very nice and something I'd come back again for (especially good for Scottish weather!).

I had a lovely dinner with a friend here. The ambiance and decor was great, and the server we had was really nice and friendly. We came on a voucher deal and enjoyed prosecco and the lamb and mash. Part of my lamb was cold which wasn't great but otherwise the dish had good flavour and was a very big portion. Once we had finished, both our normal server and another server kept coming over to ask if we wanted anything else. Although  they were probably trying to be friendly and helpful, it felt like they wanted us to buy more or head out although there were empty tables around so we weren't in the way. Overall, it was a nice dinner but I wouldn't rush back if not on a voucher.
Stopped in while on a tour - so not a full review, but we certainly got a feel for the place.  Had some black pudding and a drink - both were good.  Servers were nice.

Situated right next door to the esteemed Castle Terrace, Il Castello offers the standard menu of Italian classics. My starter wasn't particularly great, but the main course of lamb cutlets was really good. It's very reasonably priced and the staff are friendly, welcoming and knowledgeable.  Overall, we said: "I rather enjoyed Il Castello. Their take on melanzane wasn't for me, but that aside it strikes me as a very reliable, friendly little place. And what's more, their espresso was so good that I had a second one. Next time you're in the environs, pop in for a warm welcome and good Italian fare."

Taking its name from the most famous of land marks whose shadow it sits in, Il Castello is a dissapointment from the moment you walk in.  Despite being recently redecorated, the outside still seems shabby, and already the place is starting to look as though it could do with a lick of paint on the inside. As we arrived we were greeted by a surly waiter who communicated soley in grunts, and then promptly forgot about us. It took almost 20 mins to get a seat in a deserted restaurant.  The menu is huge, so there is little chance of finding something you dislike - but the food itself was on the tasteless side despite being well priced.  Overall, Il Castello wont be somewhere I will be frequenting.

This is a lovely little, family oriented Italian restaurant. It's popular with office workers from nearby Castle Terrace, especially on a Friday, although I've never had to wait for a table. The food is delicious and the portions are a good size for lunchtime - satisfying without making you feel too full. The waiters are very friendly, and happy to chat away to customers as if we're friends, which creates a great atmosphere. The food appears freshly prepared and the service is quick enough to comfortably fit into a lunch hour. This place might be quite small, but it's a regular venue of choice for a Friday lunch out that's inexpensive and tastes great!

No nonsense when it comes to ale in Camra's Edinburgh pub of the year 2015. That award in itself pretty much negates the need for me to write any more.  The pub does all the current ale-related stuff of Meet the Brewer events etc., is dog friendly, has a good regular turnover of ales as well as an inviting selection of whiskies and other spirits and enjoys the atmosphere of a well patronised & well-loved local establishment.

I have visited this bar quite a few times, after spending a bit of time at the Stockbridge Market on a Sunday afternoon "The Tap" is just a minutes walk down the road for a refreshing pint or two.  The decor is fairly basic, with mostly plain wooden chairs around plain wooden tables with a couple benches and sofas. On an average day you'll find that most of the customers are locals/regulars and the bar itself can get a bit crowded while the regulars chat with the bar staff and each other, but the bar staff are friendly and efficient and will serve you as soon as possible. On a sunny day the large windows at the front of the bar give it a bright and open atmosphere, the evening we visited it WAS chilly (perhaps about time to put the heating on in the evenings?).  The Stockbridge Tap is an independent bar and not being tied to a specific brewery it has an excellent range of beers with about 7 cask and 4 kegs on tap at any given time you'll find a variety of beers from mostly smaller breweries around the UK. The bar staff are knowledgeable about the beers on tap and will happily tell you about them and let you have a wee taste to help make up your mind. The bar also a menu with a wide range of Whiskies which the bar staff again will be happy to help you select from.  Food is served all day and is of a high quality, ranging from open sandwiches and a variety of burgers to chicken, fish and steak pie (mostly around the 8 mark). The sandwiches and burgers are served on a wooden platter (bad idea in my personal opinion) main courses are served on normal plates. They also do a daily special and homemade soup.    Four of us visited on a cold and wet September evening for their "Autumn Real Ale Festival" (which ran for 10 days between 13th Sept. to 23rd Sept 2012), it was busy all evening but not overly crowded. After a couple pints of ale we all ordered food which included: Steak & Chorizo Burger with hand cut chips, Steak pie with Black Isle Porter gravy and mashed potatoes,  Fillet  of Haddock dipped in Black Isle Blonde Batter with hand cut chips and Roast chicken stuffed with Haggis and wrapped in bacon served with chive potato cake and steamed greens with a whisky honey glaze.  I had the chicken which was good, not spectacular, I've had better, but I couldn't really fault it. I suspect everybody at our table was of a similar mind, everybody said they enjoyed their choice and that it was good but nobody "raved" about their choice.  Stockbridge is a nice part of town to visit with a variety of shops and cafes to browse, Inverleith Park and The Royal Botanic Gardens are nearby, The "Stockbridge Tap" is worth a visit for a drink and/or something to eat, I'll certainly be returning soon.  It is dog friendly and has a TV for major sporting events.

Good beer, mixed service  Ok, so I do enjoy drinking here, its probably my favourite bar in Stockbridge, but I live in Newington so I don't go out over this end of town much. They have a good range of alternating beer. It's a cosy enough place, and you can watch the sports, or sit by the window and watch the world go by.  I think the service is mixed here, on my last visit it was pretty rubbish. The bar tender grunted mostly and got restless when we took our time to order, nobody else was waiting to get served. The Rugby was on and they all seemed more interested in that or chatting to each other.   Saying that, I have been there at times when the service has been great, but normally when it is dead - the place just seems a bit too drab and lifeless.  They do occasional tap takeovers which are the best things a beer lover can attend - unless it is on a school night, in which case they are quite risky.  They also do food, but I have never eaten there.

Watch out for the broken sofa in the back - there's a reason why it's the only seat left available.   Sofa aside, I'm a big fan of the Tap. Great place to try a variety of beers (many local), and their whisky list is user-friendly. I've found the staff to be quite welcoming and happy to help with your decision-making if you're stumped for what to order.   The kitchen seems to be closed frequently and on a schedule that I am unable to predict, so I have not yet tried the food here.

I have been here a few times now and I have always been very happy with the drinks and the quality of service.  As well as having a few local Stewart Brewing beers on tap there is always a good selection of other craft beers/ciders from across the UK every time I have been in. The staff are very knowledgeable and always make good recommendations depending on what I or my friends have been after.  It's a cosy atmosphere in the place, lots of locals (who come from many different countries I should add) who appreciate good drinks. I haven't tried the food yet, but it looks good.  if you are after good craft beers, this is a place for you. If you want the usual drinks you'll get everywhere else, this place is not for you.

When I walked into the pub, my friend called out to his friend "Hey Alice (or insert here appropriate name)!" and all the locals pretty much just looked like they'd tolerate him. But barely. I mean, he's a funky looking kid with long hair and a rucksack. But they've seen him enough times to tolerate him.   So, that's the kind of attitude you'll get from people in the Stockbridge Tap. Which is not necessarily a bad thing. I mean, I always tend to look down my nose at people who've decided to make their way into my regular pub. And be loud and obtrusive. I mean, they're drinking my ale. Sitting on my seats. Etc.   And their choice of beer more than makes up for the initially intimidating atmosphere. It's a matter of holding your ground, you see. The regulars are just testing you. So grab a good pint of ale and seat yourself for the long run.

The Tap is more of a drinking pub than an eating pub, but has a proper selection of beers, wines and spirits to please the discerning drinker. There is a long line of ales on tap giving you more choice than the typical pub, especially if you're bored of the usual big brands. And if it's whisky you're after, there's a comprehensive selection, as with most pubs in this part of the world, but I really liked the small educational board standing on the bar that helps you pick your whisky depending on when you like it light or rich, smoky or delicate. Very helpful for those still learning their whiskies! This is more of a blokes pub really, a bit spit and sawdust, full of locals and sport on the TV. There's not been much spent on the decor for a while, but the atmosphere is good and I get the impression this is just how the locals like it!

The Stockbridge Tap is clearly a bit of a popular institution with Stockbridge locals, and it's been around for a while to prove its worth. The Stockbridge area has become, or probably always was, a really effervescent and hip area to go for a drink, although I think more people are body swerving some of the over frequented bars in the centre of town, to come ten minutes down the road to Stockbridge for a more individual experience.  The Stockbridge Tap sits at the more traditional end of the bars and pubs in Stockbridge, with its wooden barrels, classic wooden decor in general, and the no frills, straightforward drinking feel. This is a decent place to have a chilled drink and a chat, and it has a huge whisky menu, which is great for cold nights, when you need some traditional banter and that warm, fuzzy feeling (otherwise known as the onset of tipsiness). I like my traditional pubs slightly cosier than The Tap, as I don't feel quite as comfortable as I would like in here, but I would still recommend stopping here for a beverage if you're doing the rounds in Stockbridge.

Hang on a second? Where did this place come from?  I remember it being a total sh... I remember it being not so good. After wondering in and looking in the menu I realised that perhaps it still wasn't the most exciting place on Earth.   The lick of paint and the Ikea-esque surroundings have disguised it from being the dirty old man pub I'm sure it used to be but really it's not got much else new about it.  The menu, not hearty enough to be pub food and not exciting enough to be more upmarket let it down and I still automatically ordered a pint because that's what the atmosphere dictated me to do. The regulars were still gathered at the bar and when I walked in and asked to look at the menu one muttered under his breath "hmmf.. tourists". What? because I don't look as Scottish as you with your tartan cap and Scotty dog outside, hmmf.. regulars...

Plenty of real ale on tap and being in Stockbridge are the 2 things going for Stocky Tap. On their own, big positives.   On the downside, service can be a little snooty and there is definitely a preference shown to locals when queueing for drinks...or at least that's what I've experienced...too many times now not to comment. Lift your service Stocky Tap.

Dogs are allowed inside (no judgment, just an observation).  We had two open sandwiches, a pint, and a 1/2 pint and it cost us 15.  The sandwiches came with 6 chips each and were served on cutting boards.  We were both pleased with our sandwiches and the portion size was probably just right for lunch.  There was an odor (from the dogs?) upon entering but by the end of our meal it no longer bothered me.  The service was friendly.

We were not expecting much but this place delivered!  Finally --- cream, butter and milk-free options.  Leek and potato soup was smooth, delicately seasoned.  But the REAL star of Scottish food is the salmon.  It is indescribable.  I can't get enough if it ... Divine.

Stopped in for lunch during a visit to the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. It was a nice day, so I ate outside, which was lovely. Had the Fish & Chips with an Iced Tea. The fish was nice and flaky and the chips nice and crisp. I probably wouldn't stop in here just to have lunch, but was a nice place to grab a bite when visiting the Botanic Garden.

It wasn't planned for lunch but some things are good left unplanned.   Yes I'm saying it's good.  All three of us ordered something from the sandwich part of the menu.  Portions were big. So tick for value. Tasty too, so another tick. We ordered Mayo but original waitress forgot it and we had to reorder. Service, average, speedy.   It's really a nice setting but it does have an open feel about it.

Thankfully the Royal Botanic Gardens are still free. If this addition to the site was any indicator of the way forward then it would become an expensive pleasure to enjoy.   Whilst the absence of a service charge is laudable the price of 10.50 for a Full Scottish Breakfast makes it clear at what end of the market the restaurant is pitching itself. At some point I may bite the bullet and sample this but currently I doubt, as with all such prices for such a meal, that it will be worth it.   Unfortunately I forgot to photograph the two starters I had in today's visit (the five main courses were all dearer and seemingly more filling than I was after that early in the afternoon) but safe to say that nouvelle is the name of the day. The food itself was dubious - pumpkin soup heated to within an inch of it's life in the microwave (tasty when an asbestos mouth was not required to eat it) served with a decent slice of walnut bread (memory fails me on that note) and butter that was rock hard from only just coming out of the fridge - a schoolboy error if ever there was one. The duck liver parfait was a good size but, as with many places, the amount of accompanying substance on which to spread it was rather too small to stop one feeling like a pig when making it go 4 ways and then filling one's gob. The chutney was in a dinky wee glass jar but that was also one affectation too far.   No complaints about the staff and service or the general ambience and I've chucked my business card into the bowl in the hope of winning dinner for two but that's probably the only reason I'd go back to eat here. In future the most I'm likely to bother with is a cuppa.

Poor. Museum cafes are always going to be a bit of a fleecing but to be a fleecing with such rotten service is very special indeed. The food was so-so. 9 for a sandwich and chips with these presented in a silly, pretend frying basket. (Hate that). The main issue was how glacially slow this entire proceeding was. Our kid's ice cream never arrived and the excuse was an overwhelmed kitchen staff. In a half empty restaurant? It was more likely to be a poorly managed kitchen and poorly trained staff. We asked to pay without having received our child's dessert. We were not charged for the dessert.  I asked the manager what the deal was and she said they had let in too many people who did not have reservations. Smells like bull to me. Don't bother. The Botanics is always a nice treat but step out of the place for a snack. Really.

Unless you are looking for a completely uninspired breakfast experience, I would give the Gateway Restaurant a miss. I had heard that lunching here was recommendable and so, I hoped that perhaps breakfast might be worthwhile. Of course, the venue is beautiful, located as it is in the John Hope Gateway. But, warming the croissants could not mask how stale they were. The Aberdeen buttery did not seem much fresher. The stacked Scotch pancakes, were unimaginatively presented. Do not expect the wait staff to be able to provide any details about the presence of nut contamination in any of the food - despite the menu stating that they will.  The reason that our waitress could not give us any details about possible nut contamination of course, was because all pastries are bought in from outside. This is not the first time I have been confronted with this issue and I still find it unacceptable that a restaurant, even if a food item is brought in from a bakery, cannot furnish the customer with details of ingredients, or other information relevant to the food item. Most disappointingly I suppose, was the fact that the food was not made in house. Why is it that a restaurant cannot bake/make its own food? I assume that they do have a kitchen and cooks. I know from personal experience that a scone, a pancake, a loaf of bread are not complex undertakings in the kitchen.  I cannot fault the wait staff; they were pleasant enough. (Though some training from management might have been in order for our poor waitress was most thoroughly stumped when we asked her to enlighten us as to what an Aberdeen buttery was).  Pleasant service though cannot make up for poor quality food. So, if you want to impress out-of-town guests, serve them a nice breakfast at home and head straight to the botanic gardens bypassing the Gateway Restaurant.

a very grand place to eat and prices to match, however the food is delicious. It has fantastic views of the botanics, and u can sit outside in the summer. you can get breakfast, lunch etc. There is also a childrens menu to my delight

On a hot Easter Monday afternoon, we swung in here for afternoon tea. It was meltingly hot in the glass framed building, and we were desperate for a drink of water and looking forward to a proper tea service. But thanks to the waiters to seemed to idling around chatting, we couldn't order anything and after a while sweating in the heat, got bored. So left. The manager kindly noted that I left my bag but didn't bother to ask why we left without ordering. Oh well!

december is a month of non-stop christmas dinners, drinks, and nights out.  so arriving at La P'tite Folie for my third dinner of the festive season i had relatively moderate expectations.  christmas dinners are not always the best way to try a restaurant for the first time, but i needn't have worried about it this night.  we were a table of six and had pre-ordered our food already.  however, we were still brought the wine menu and when asking for prosecco (which they serve in Le Di-Vin) i was told they only had sparkling wine.  we all decided to go with that anyway after a brief description by the waiter and it was shortly brought over to us.  before starters arrived we were also given a bread basket and a massive bowl of salad which was a nice touch.  starters arrived and i was well pleased with my smoked duck, blue cheese, and pear salad.  it was delicious and the duck was so tender and just mixed perfect with the blue cheese, pear, and salad.  it was probably one of the best starters i've had this whole christmas season (only out done by my smoked makarel salad at Field).  for mains i had the salmon wrapped in phyllo dough with season veg and mash.  another really tasty course with the salmon perfectly cooked and the mash and sauce just really incredibly good.  after a short break and an order for coffees we were brought dessert. i had tart tatin which was nice but not as good as the previous two courses.  all throughout dinner we were made to feel very welcome, with courses arriving in good blocks of time instead of being rushed through the meal.  when booking we were told we would only have the table for two hours, but as the restaurant was not too busy they happily left us to sit there for around 3 hours instead which actually allowed us to enjoy the meal instead of feeling that we were on the factory line of christmas dinners like other places i had been.  if i was rating my christmas dinners by the quality of the food and service this would definitely come near the very top of my list.  the only real negative point i can think of was that for 6 the table was a bit small.  we're fairly small girls (all of us being runners) and even for us the chairs were a bit close together.  but it's a small quibble for what was a really enjoyable evening with good food and good friends.

Not very authentic and bad service   They have a very limited menu selection and nobody spoke French in the place. They are very small with only 4 or 5 tables and the bartender is also the waitress. I have to say that she made our party feel like we were bothering her, since we were all enjoying our conversation along sipping on some wine but when she would come over to ask if we were ready and we weren't, she rolled her eyes clearly showing she was annoyed.  The food was also not very good!!! I asked for the Aberdeen Angus Beef with Gratin Dauphionois and Turffle jus and clearly asked to replace the truffle jus with some "Cafe de Paris" butter, when she brought it, she forgot the butter, so I kindly reminded her and again she rolled her eyes, took my food up the stairs and came back with a BIG piece of FROZEN butter which of course made the whole steak very cold and not enjoyable at all.  We started with warm duck confit, served with pomme puree, honey, and apple jus. (This was OK).  Finished it all of with sticky toffee pudding (this was OK). My first choice which was hazelnut bavarois but they were out, so that was disappointing.  Again I want to emphasize that they had a very limited menu choices and no escargot

We had a bit of a mixed time at La P'tite Folie. From my perspective, both my dishes were very good, but MJ's dish was really pretty ordinary. The location is very smart and the service good, though, so If you order well, you'll be very pleased with the place.  Overall, we said: "in terms of the food, I did very well at La P'tite Folie. The soup and the seafood were both very good indeed. But MJ's dish was not right, so once I got over my triumph, I did wonder at the potential for this place to be a bit hit and miss. But I have to go on what I was served, and both dishes were very good. So, as is often the case, careful ordering is richly rewarded. Beyond that, I have a feeling that other places operating within this milieu (L'escargot Blanc to name but one) are likely to serve you to a more reliably high quality level."

This restaurant in housed a pretty magnificent building, which is called Tudor House, so go figure! It's one of the two "little madnesses" situated in New Town, and the dishes are extremely french!  I haven't had any main meals here, but did take a glance at the menu and saw duck, risotto and some pretty pricey filet. My friend and I had decided on a whim to go have dessert at some fancy restaurant, and chose this one. I'm hoping to take my parents back there one day, so they can treat me to a FULL dinner, because all I've had so far was their creme brulee which was absolutely delicious.  The restaurant itself isn't intimidating at all, and was quite laid back when I was there.

Myself and a group of friends went to Nandos on Lothian Road a few nights ago for a friends birthday, and we were sat right next to the door , that swung open ever 2 seconds, blasting us with cold air Brrrrrrrrrrrr ...its was freezing outside and not much warmer inside either. I cannot enjoy food feeling cold. The table was a massive round one - probably the biggest they had and I guess whilst it was good of them to accommodate a group of 10 of us, the table was so large you could not talk to the person opposite you. Hmmm. This was my second time in Nando's and I remembered why I didnt think it was anything special the last time. We choose what we wanted and headed up to the counter to order, of which only two were serving, sometimes one and their was already a queue. My meal cost 12.  I ordered the chicken wrap, with cheese and medium salsa and Piri Piri Fries. When i got my food i found i had very little chicken barely any salsa or cheese - so no 'kick' at all to my food, and mediocre fries sprinkles in the piri piri.  They were keen to get us in and then back out, and the ladies toilets had no toliet roll...I can think of plenty of places id like to eat alot more for 12, and like alot of chain restaurants, it wasnt anything special.

My friends and I decided during the summer to go to the Nandos on Lothian Road for dinner on our way into town. We asked for a table for 7, but we were told we'd have to wait at least half an hour. Then one of our dining companions cancelled, so we went straight back in and asked for a table of 6. We were then immediately taken to a huge booth at the back... with 7 place settings.   We decided to order two jugs of sangria, both at the same price. The first arrived and was considerably bigger than the other. When we complained, the waiter tried to tell us that the volume was the same. So we drank the biggest jug first, then poured the smaller one into it. Lucky if it was 25% of the volume (we did film this).   Then, our food arrived at different times. We could see it sitting on the hot plate, but the waiter decided that instead of serving us all together it would be better to leave some people's dishes to get cold while he visited other tables.   All in all a terrible experience and I haven't been back since.

Wow, I love Nando's. I have to be honest, it's only a recent discovery for me but I'm so glad I've finally experienced the goodness of Nando's. It's yummy, reasonably priced and best of all; messy. There's nothing more satisfying than eating chicken wings with your hands and getting right in there to enjoy it.  On my last visit here I got a chicken wrap with chili jam and mayonnaise, served with a side of corn on the cob and some spiced mushy peas - it was delicious and only came to a reasonable 8.90. Awesome.  The sauces in Nando's are phenomenal and I usually go for the hot peri peri as I love spicy food. I recently bought a bottle from ASDA and have been drowning everything in it ever since. Yum.  Unlike the other reviewers, I like the fact that Nando's has no table service. It's exactly the way it should be as it's such an informal dining experience. It means you don't have to rush your meal or have an annoying waitress ask if you're sure you don't want another side, a dessert or coffee, tea, macaroons. Argghhh, leave me alone to eat! I love the relaxed feel of Nando's.  If you have any left room over after your meal I highly recommend the chocolate cheese cake - it's to die for!

I'm not really a fast food kind of girl and I consider Nando's to be fast food - they might try to convince you otherwise with their waitresses and restaurant style premises, but this is fast food through and through. A friend once described this place as KFC for WAGS and they pretty much hit the nail on the head. Sure, the chicken isn't fried but I have doubts over its original source and wouldn't be entirely surprised to find out it comes from the same supplier. That said, the food doesn't taste bad, in fact some of it is rather good and I quite like the spicy stuff they give you to sprinkle over chips. However, there are far more exciting and better value places to eat in Edinburgh, so I won't be making a habit of coming here.

I'd never been to Nando's before visiting this branch, I've now been twice with colleagues since May.   There's usually always plenty of tables available and the staff have been really friendly and helpful when I've been. One of the things I like about it is going up to order and pay before the food comes to the table as it's easier to keep tabs on how much you're spending and it saves time trying to catch someone's attention to ask for the bill at the end.   On both occasions I've been there I've had the mango and lime chicken breast burger with fries. The first time we went I had garlic bread too but it wasn't that appetising for me, it had too hard a consistency and just wasn't that good. I love the taste of the chicken and it's great being able to choose from all of the different sauces. The only thing that I don't think is worth getting is the side of a 'roasted whole Portobello mushroom' it really is just a single cooked Portobello mushroom in a small dish for 2.70 which seems a bit overpriced in my opinon!   We've tried a couple of the deserts, the mango sorbet's been my favourite so far.   I'd reccommend trying Nando's, the food's nice and it's not too expensive. However, if you're not a fan of spicy food avoid the chilli salt on your fries as it was too hot for me despite my friend saying it wouldn't be!!

How can anyone not love Nandos? Food is seriously addictive, I think its the spices that keep you coming back! Ordering system is quick, & the whole atmosphere is very relaxed. Ok maybe not the best venue for a slap up special dinner but day to day this is great for so many things... the best being a hungover get together after a night out. Nothing cures a hangover like a Nandos! Staff in this one are friendly & look happy. Is in a good location & seems to have shorter waiting times than the one at Fountain park (maybe due to the cinema?).Try the mango & lime sauce mmmm.
I like this Nandos, but then I like all Nandos. Food is amaze, staff are really friendly, it's clean and they give you a free chicken if you eat there enough times. Winner.

Very tasty. Yum yum. Go here every couple of months. More often I I could. They even do rewards. a stamp on card every time you enter. 6 stamps= 1 quarter free chicken. 9 stamps= half a free chicken. full card =    a whole chicken free.

It was actually a visit to this Nando's that sort of won me over to the Celebrity loved eaterie, as I have never been entirely convinced before.  For a start, I don't like the fact you have to go up and order your food. This is a restaurant, so in my opinion it should be table service. I also don't actually like any of the pouring sauces but somehow I always convince myself to tip a little next to my chips as if this time I'll have developed a taste for it. I haven't. I sort of agree with Emma C about it being fast food, but I have never once been to Nando's where I haven't been ravenous by the time they mosey out with my meal, plus the chicken isn't fried, and chuck it in a wrap with some salad and you sort of feel like its a healthy alternative.  At this particular Nando's I had a medium hot chicken wrap with cheese, side of chips and spicy rice and some grilled holloumi. It did take ages to come out, and then when it did, it had mayo on it which I explicitly asked to be omitted about 4 times at the till. Funnily enough, my replacement came in double quick time so who knows what took so long to bring it the first time. I dread to think!  It was tasty, again, I tried the garlic sauce, it was rank, the hot sauce almost burnt the nostril hairs off me too. For the wrap meal and a bottomless fizzy drink it was only about 11 which was pretty good value for money because this was a lot of food! The service, apart from being a little tardy, is friendly and they check a few times if you are enjoying your meal, so that'll do me.  Overall, a nice enough restaurant, acceptable service and good food, if not a little slow off the mark.

Had lunch here yesterday. This branch of Nando's is huge. We were seated by a very friendly receptionist who gave us a booth upon request though most of the tables were not yet occupied. The smell of food immediately gave us an idea of what to fill in our severely hungry stomachs. So off we went to get our food and sat down. The place is nicely decorated. Our wait staff was very nice and brought us oour food not long after we ordered. I thought this place was cleaner than the one in Fountain Park. The peri-peri chix is still our favorite.

Had to stop here after hearing all the buzz about the food. And it wasn't too bad. I love the concept of this place.   We walked in and were seated right away. Our waiter explained the menu and how to order. My boyfriend and I shared the chicken wing platter, with a side of chips and mashed potatoes. We ordered the wings with a medium peri-peri sauce. Peri-peri is their signature sauce which comes in many different varieties. I especially like the garlic and herb sauce. The wings and chips were great. I ddn't like the mashed potatoes-they tasted very fake.   I also ordered a glass of rose which was very refreshing. Food was also very inexpensive. Definitely try it if you are in the area!

The food was great.  The staff were lovely.  It's just the logistical concept that I'll never get the hang of. You're taken to a seat where you choose from the menu, then have to leave that seat in order to order, then they ask you questions at the till that you weren't expecting to have to answer, with options that weren't immediately apparent. There are contradictions: you tell them what you would like your chicken to taste of, then are directed to an area where there are yet more flavours, this time out of a variety of bottles. Do you take the bottle with you back to the table while you wait - that seems a long time for a bottle to be sitting on my table when someone else might like to use it, no? Fortunately there seem to be plenty of staff/helpers/carers on hand to help you get through it.  Nevertheless I've always like the 'Man eating chicken!' signs they have outside their various establishments. I'll go again, absolutely, but only with company that understands the process and can assure me that everything will be ok. Ok?

Ooooh Chicken, Chicken CHICK CHICKEN!! With Piri-Piri.. mmmm.  Wings, breast whole frikkin chickens..   This is awesome. I am a chicken fan. I go to the indy chicken places - but this place supplies corporate chain chicken yummy in my tummy.    I cannot really fault them apart that they should have more sauces.. like a wings place I frequent very often. Apart from that  this is a brilliant Hot Piri Piri Portuguese restaurant that serves chicken to make me purr.   They also have other stuff; like fries, corn cobs, salads and stuff - which are also very nicely prepared. But they ain't chicken!   I like the jovial waiters and the fact they do check up on you if everything is OK and it feels genuine. I also like the bottomless soft drinks, the beers and most of the wine. Very nicey Portuguesy, yes, yes.  Not too expensive and you choose your own portion size. Well done Nando's

Om with a little extra nomnomnomnomnomnomnomnomnom.  Nothing makes you feel more manly than eating meat apart from one thing. A WHOLE CHICKEN! There was no messing about here. A whole chicken, large portion of piri piri fries and two bottles of beer. I thought that would be a good enough starter.  Knuckle deep and my face covered from left to right in chickeny beautifulness, I made short work of what I thought would be a mountain of food but it turns out it served to be nothing more than an appetite catalyst.  Yes, it is a chain restaurant which means service and quality is pretty much across the board but when happiness comes with two wings, two breasts and two legs cooked in a beautifully warm spicy marinade, you don't really care about where you are.  Give me all the chicken and keep it coming.
Never had a bad nandos in this one the staff are always great. There's often not enough floor staff but I imagine they have as many quiet as they do busy spells so it's hard to balance the rota

I don't see what the hype is about this place.  My lovely British boyfriend wanted to go to Nando's for a quick lunch before we did some sightseeing and told me I would love it.  I mean, I like chicken and all, but I was extremely underwhelmed by my experience there.  It's just a chicken wrap with a choice of a few sauces.  The hottest hot sauce is WEAAAAAKKKK.  Seriously, I want to cry while I'm eating my spicy chicken wraps.  Also, I got the mashed peas as a side and it was the strangest thing on the planet - I do not recommend trying them.  I mean, I would eat here again, but wouldn't rate it high on my list of places to go to!  As a footnote, I also do not see the hype about Chick-Fil-A and Church's Chicken in America (down in the South) and everyone raves about both spots.

Whilst I do agree that Nando's is little more than glorified fast food, to stick it in the same bracket as KFC is going a bit too far. At The Colonel's place, biting down on a pus-filled tumour is more or less par for the course, as is finding a cockroach or two in your chips, but standards are much higher at Nando's.   Seeing them chuck a whole chicken on the barbeque is a buzz in itself, and when you get it delivered to your table, drenched in the hottest sauce they've got, the messy tables and rough-looking punters all become irrelevant.  The meats of fantastic quality, well cooked, and just a joy to behold really. For about 9 quid you'll get half a chicken plus a couple of sides, preferably garlic bread and peri-peri sprinkled fries, and you'll stroll out that door pretty satisfied.

Nando's be Nando's.  One thing I miss about Dublin is my Ma's roast chicken.  I just don't have the time to roast a whole chicken, let alone the appetite to eat it so Nando's always manages to cheer me up! It's healthy(ish) and filling, the fact they provide sauces means I can share chicken with the OH (he likes veeeerrrryy spicy, I am the complete opposite) and it's great for groups. Not only that but wherever you go in the UK you can find a Nando's.  This particular branch is quite nice, it's airy and in a convenient location. The staff are friendly enough, I once had a plate of chips poured on me and half the waiting staff were over in a flash to help.   Also I luuuurve Piri-Piri on hummus. Amazing.

I bope to change my mind about Nando so i am keeping this review open to be updated; went to Nandos for lunch with my friend and he has been selling the place to me big time so i had quite the expectation; we got here around 1245 and the place was packed; we got sitted right away and got to choose what we wanted; we then stood and went to place our orders; that took some times but nothing to be mad about; i got the 1/4 chicken with a slide of mash and one side of corn on the cob.. I believe they were seriously understaffed and our food took over 35 minute to come ; we both picked out some sauces and i got the lemon sauce and it was a good choice; the chicken was tasty and well seasoned and with the sauce, it made it very good; however i pretty much hated the sides.. The mash was dry not creamy and just looked like it was microwavable mash; the corn was dry.. Not even appetising to look at... Our food was probably ready for a while before actually being served because when it came most of it was cold..  I will give nando another shot but i hope it picks up from this disappointing experience

Our first night in Edinburgh and we decide to drop into the closest restaurant, which happens to feature Portuguese food.  Expecting something that would feature a lot of seafood, we were surprised to see that the major feature was chicken.  But we ordered a hummus starter, a bean side dish and a couscous salad with peri peri chicken and a couple of beers.  It was all very very tasty and just what we wanted for a light meal.  Imagine my surprise when I discovered that Nando's was a chain restaurant with 250 outlets in the UK.  This was without doubt the best fast food chain dining experience I have had.    The routine is different.  Someone shows you to a table, presents a menu, but then explains that you have to go to the counter to order and pay and fetch your own cutlery.  So it's not the fine food dining experience, but I have to say that the quality and taste of the food was a big surprise.  For what it Is I give it four stars.

hmmmmmmmmmmmmm Chicken livers......drool ......  Where to start......chicken livers.......drool......  Sorry ok this place is awesome I love love love it. Finally went in after walking by it almost everyday for the past year and tried the chicken livers that were recommended to me. If you hate or think livers sound gross well eat these and they will forever open your eyes. I have been to culinary school and worked in kitchens and it takes a lot to really impress me but these little babies are the best I have ever had and theres no way I could or even that idiot Gordon Ramsey could make better ones. The flavor and presentation of them is amazing. I like them with the medium flavor. I also love the chicken dishes they have which are also very good. The place is clean and has a little place to wash your dirty paws before you eat right in the middle of the restaurant. I really like that encourages cleanliness. The kitchen is open and you can see how clean it is. The staff are also friendly which is a plus.  This place will be my haunt when I am waiting for the bus and those livers ( I am starting to sound like Dr. Lecter) will be my little snack of choice when I need something simple and quick. I recommend this place to everyone especially if you like or only eat chicken!

Me Man.....me eat chicken!  Yes its a chain....yes they are all the same......but it does what it says on the tin! It delivers tasty chicken, with decent sides and its at a reasonable price!  Nandos is one of those very handy places to meet graba  bite to eat and move on. Thats exactly what we did last night.  The concept is a simple one, chose how spicy you want it, chose what bit of chicken you want, chose you sides..! I think the fact they give you options makes it to be honest. Whether you want a wrap, a burger, a pita or like me you just want chicken...on a plate its there for you.  They also have a surprisingly large ammount of options of veggies to their credit as well as the oblifatory salad options....!  For me it has to be medium spicy half chicken with chips & piripiri salad and colesalw.!  Simple...tasty...nom nom nom!  Happy JD
The food remains great, yet the service quality in this particular restaurant has dropped, that's why the -1.

Om nom nom nom! Peri-Peri chicken with hot sauce! Feel the burn, LOVE the burn!  Seriously though. Damn good chicken. Tender, juicy, and grilled to crispy awesomness. Getting hungry just thinking about it! I know why people are addicted to this place, cause it's really really tasty. Prices are good too! Huge plate of food and a drink for about 9 quid.  Dining room is really cool as well. Kind of like if a regular sit down place and urban outfitters had a baby.  Obrigado, Nando!

Great tasting food every time you visit! The food is always hot, fresh and have fantastic flavours! Your food does arrive very quickly compared to normal restaurants and they have great loyalty programme!   The Nando's on Lothian Road is really well furnished, with loads of space, comfortable seats and always clean. You are greeted by very friendly staff and the service is great.  Definitely place to go if you like chicken!

Carbonara, how I've missed you.  This veggie's little heart went soaring the minute she laid eyes on Nova Pizza's pasta menu and spotted carbonara. How had I missed it on my visit previously? Honestly: because this is the girl who goes straight in for the pizza. But, boy, oh boy; before I went veggie, I adored a creamy, rich carbonara. So it's been years since I've had carbonara.  I'm going to go all out and say that Nova Pizza have created the best veggie carbonara you will ever feast upon. I dare the staunchest of carnivores to give it a try and truly tell me that something's missing. The smoked seitan fills the meaty void just perfectly and the dish is wonderfully rich and creamy, just as carbonara should be.  Portions are generous. I wasn't uncomfortably stuffed but had a pleasant satisfied feeling that lasted well after the meal. The ingredients are high quality and it shows. Most dishes can be made either vegetarian or vegan.  Please do pay a visit and indulge in Nova Pizza's wonderful creations. I'll be back soon and I'm going to make sure I have a starter to sample more of the menu. Oh, and there may just be room for the disaronno affogatto for dessert. Why, it would be rude not to!

Novapizza was a great experience, the food variety and quality is very high and it is tasty .  I ordered the spaghetti with puttanesca  sauce and it was excellent.  The size of the portions is generous and the presentation was really good.  We also shared a pizza topped with carbonara sauce and home made smoked seitan , it was very fresh and the crust was thin and wonderfully crispy.  A great experience and will gladly come back again.

Such a unique place with endless vegan options! This is the fist time I've seen an entire restaurant conquer vegan Italian! And they're killing it. The vegetarian carbonara was very good. It was my first time trying seitan and I'm now a seitan fan because of this restaurant! Hail seitan!

I thought I'd already tasted the best pizza in the world but then had dinner in Nova and realised that this is the home of the best. Small, unassuming and homely in a traditional Italian red and white checked tablecloth style, Nova's ambience is cute and quaint. However the pizzas are seriously scrumptious.   With a full, extensive Vegetarian and Vegan menu boasting Vegan cheese, Seitan and every veg topping you could possibly desire my meal here on Wednesday 9 November 2016 was truly fantastic. Our party of four people, carnivores included, all loved Nova.   We ordered both Vegetarian and Vegan pizzas and calzones. My pizza which was called the "Vegan" on the menu came topped with mushroom, onion, sweetcorn, peppers, aubergines, courgette and Vegan cheese and was delicious. A couple of bottles of really great Pinot Grigio, a bargain at 10 each, complimented our food perfectly.   Although full after our mains we shared a Vegan peanut butter and jam cheesecake, just to sample it, and it was luscious. Nova definitely needs to be booked in advance, as there wasn't a free table during our midweek visit and we were very glad we had pre-booked a table.   A constant flow of people called in to collect takeaway pizzas, yet despite the fact that staff were extremely busy the service we received was flawless. The one and only problem being that there isn't a Nova Pizza in my own hometown of Belfast. I'll definitely be returning when I'm next in Edinburgh.

Came here after touring Edinburgh. Although not in the city center, its a walkable distance from Scott's Monument (15-20 walk). We got the gnocchi (amazing), white blue cheese pizza (amazing), and the Messicana pizza (also great). The only suggestion I would have is to reduce the spiciness of the Messicana pizza. I feel like the three spice symbols they put next to it are not proportional to the spice level of that particular pizza. I eat really spicy foods and I was coughing with how spicy it was. To be proportional the pizza should have 10 or so spice symbols next to it. Or would have the pepper served on the side. The other thing was that I made a reservation through the website but the waitress had no record of it, fortunately they had empty table when we arrived...

We just sat down for an excellent vegan lunch. Pasta bolognese and spaghetti carbonara (with seitan). This place has got a lot of choices, even for vegetarians.  I'd go with friends and share some dishes because the helpings are generous and it tastes great.  Buon appetito

I had wanted to try this place for aaaages! I made a group booking for a vegan meetup and because they only have around 21 seats they asked if I could send them a list of pre-ordered food choices. I made a Word table with everyone's names and their starters, mains, and desserts. I loved this set up and I think all restaurants should require the same; it really saves time on waiting for people to make up their minds!
