Howies is a fantastic restaurant. It is the definition of Scottish dining. Fresh food and cooked to perfection. I had salmon with samphire. I will definitely be returning to the restaurant as the staff were extremely lovely and so was the food!

Delicious! There was a nice selection of daily specials and the regular menu. The bread basket was also yummy. My favorite past of the meal was the sticky toffee pubbing, which was in a sweet, satisfying pool of caramel.

Great service, drinks and food.  Our family of 7 had a wonderful meal here after a long and hot day of touring the sites in  Edinburgh.  Every dish we ordered was amazing, and the whiskey flights were fun for the group to sample.

A real gem on Victoria Street - and I've been to the one at Waterloo Place and can verify that is equally as good.   The lunch menu here is perfect - two courses for just over a tenner. The service is professional and friendly. I opted for the chicken breast on a cabbage bed with mash potato, followed by banoffee pie. Everything was delicious.   The range of food on offer is excellent considering this is a lunch menu. All ingredients are locally sourced and fresh. Definitely recommended.
Squeezed us it even though we didn't have a reservation. Busy place. Servings are a bit small so definitely get a starter. Great staff! Food was out fast and delicious.

Howies beautifully presents delicious flavours of Scotland in generous portions served by smiley happy staff at reasonable prices in a warm, minimalistic setting.  I had a trio of salmon to start - locally hot smoked salmon pate, single malt whisky cured salmon gravadlax, seared smoked salmon with a fennel & citrus dressing; main of grilled fillet of locally smoked hake with sauteed new potatoes, chorizo & spinach and dessert of chocolate truffle and Oloroso whiskey torte with summer berry compote.  I don't eat in Scottish restaurants enough and Howies is reason to do so more often!
5 star local food at 3 star prices - go there now!  Absolutely fantastic local food at a brilliant price. The best restaurant we visited during our festival weekend stay.  Amazing service too!

We tried haggis for the first time (have to try the local foods) and it was very good.  We'll be interested to see if others are as nicely textured & seasoned as Howies. The service was very good & the atmosphere friendly.  We visited with two other tables of guests.

The hubby and I popped into Howie's around noon on new years day after unsuccessfully attempting to eat at Oink (again, for the six time).   The space is awesome - the owner told me it was a stable in it's old life. It's nicely decorated and since we were there over the holidays, they had a tree and some other Christmassy decorations arranged throughout the restaurant. Upon entering, you will be greeted by one of the many smiling staff and with the smell of delicious coffee and food.   Their two-course lunch offering was something we simply could not refuse. At 9.95, it was a steal. Included was either a starter and main or main and dessert. The husband and I opted for the starter/main option.   They offer daily specials which are detailed on a big black chalkboard hung high in the dining room. You know, pie of the day, casserole of the day, fish of the day, drink of the day. You get the drift.  The drink of the day - obviously since it was new years day - was a bloody mary. "Two of those, please" we said. The sad truth was that they were terribly disappointing - something you'd get in a chain pub.  I ordered the carrot and coriander soup as my starter which came with a slice of bread. It was delicious. Absolutely delicious. I have no idea what my husband ordered because I was so enamored with my soup.  For the mains, the husband ordered the beef casserole with root veg and mash and I ordered the steak pie with greens and mash. The long and short of our two orders were that they were basically teh same dish. The minor differences being that mine was served in a baking dish and his in a bowl, mine had carrots and his had parsnips, and mine had a pasty "lid." Everything else was the same - a good way to go about things from a kitchen perspective.  We both really liked the beef in our dishes. It was cooked well and neither of us found fatburgs floating around in our dishes. I could have done without the pasty crust but that's a personal thing. I'm just not a pasty kind of girl. I thought the mashed potatoes paired well with my kale and steak pie but my husband commented, "Your mash is better than this mash." Thanks, I muttered.  Overall, top notch for the food (one note though is that I think there are two microwaves in the kitchen which were being used A LOT which is kind of concerning).  Service was really good but we did have one issue. I ordered a glass of wine which never arrived. When the manager stopped by our table (randomly to see how we were getting on), she asked if we needed anything and I mentioned my MIA wine and she said that she would take care of it and she did, like immediately and then told us that they had comped the wine due to the mishap. Now, this is what I expect at restaurants and, unfortunately, this level of service is just so hard to find outside of the US. Job well done, Howie's!

Howies is a bit of an edinburgh institution, it's been around for years and offers quailty bistro food from fresh ingredients.  having never actually been, when it was decided that this was where we would be having our work christmas lunch i was looking forward to finally trying it.  we arrived at half two on a friday afternoon and were shown to a long table along the back wall.  the restaurant space is a bit odd... on entering there is a tiny waiting area which also serves as the bar so not ideal when you're a massive party squashed in waiting to be seated.  also the space lacks atmosphere and is sort of soulless with clean walls and a mix of blues for colouring.  the restaurant is two rooms, one slightly larger than the next and these may have more atmosphere on a normal night instead of when its packed with office christmas parties.  we had barely sat down when we were offered an aperetif and had our starters placed in front of us.  i had the spicy parsnip soup, which was quite nice and a good sized portion.  starters were shortly followed by mains of which i found my venison stew tasty but not overly impressive.  the stew compromised of venison, carrots, and a serving of mashed potatoes.  i thought it could have used a few more veg to round it out but found it to be nice just not that exciting.  finally dessert arrived in speedy time and i was quite pleased with my cheese board.  three different types of cheeses, quince, and a good number of oatcakes.  i would have appreciated being told what the cheeses were though...  so overall i thought Howie's was ok, it was nice enough that i would go back to try it on a non-christmas dinner basis but not so nice that i would go rushing back.  the part that really bothered me was that the whole meal felt like we were on a conveyor belt in some factory instead of there to enjoy a nice meal.  we were in and out in just over 2 hours which isn't really enough time to enjoy a three course meal.  hopefully if i make a repeat visit i'll be able to update my review with a further star.

Also a place I'd passed by, peeked in, and made a mental note to visit.   It's upscale without being pushy. I mean the decor. It's warm, but elegant; sparse but comfortable. My friend and I both remarked on how nice it was. There are a lot of staff, which is luxurious. Someone took my coat, someone sat me, another brought water, maybe one of the earlier ones took our order, a different one delivered it. It was funny, because usually you'd strike up little conversations with your waiter, but here it was always someone new, and if you were boring/naughty you could just keep saying the same things.  Anyway, the food was good. Not great, not WOW! It was tasty. I'd be fine if someone suggested this place again. A note on their Gluten Free options: some menu items have the little GF symbol, but it means they CAN be GF, like if something listed which sounds like it has gluten is taken out. For instance, one of the desserts was a pannacotta with a ginger biscuit and whatever. But to be GF there would be no biscuit. Not that there was also a GF ginger biscuit. So kinda disappointing in the level of accommodation.

This a proper Restaurant, not pub, on the dopest street in Old Town.  Classy interior, refined servers and hostess.  Tasty options for the prix fixe lunch menu.  Swanky and deelish.  This place is definitely for moi.

We stumbled upon this casual restaurant for dinner on a recent visit to Edinburgh, and had such a lovely dinner, that we came back for lunch the next day for our last meal in the city, only to be sadly disappointed. Our dinner was a 4-star, and our lunch a 2-star, so I split the two with a 3-star rating.    For dinner, we had perfectly cooked steak filets (mine medium-well, my friend's medium), tasty cocktails and wine.  And THE DESSERT. Just come for the dessert: This restaurant serves the BEST Banoffee dessert that I have ever had.  If I hadn't been so full, I would have ordered another on the spot.  So we did the next best thing and returned for lunch, with a plan to start and end the lunch with Banoffee.  This dessert was consistent and didn't disappoint.  It was SO GOOD (as a starter and as a finish!).  My friend ordered a lunch special with tomato soup (it was fresh, she added butter, but I like mine without), and a ravioli (which was bland and strange and in a watery broth that fell flat and severely disappointed).  I ordered the filet special again, but instead was brought a different (and less tasty) cut of steak.  When I pointed this out, the server politely offered to request me a new entree, but as we were already running late to catch our flight, I didn't have time to wait for them to cook a new one.  I ate it, but it certainly lacked the flavor and texture of the steak that I had had the night before.    We ended our meal with the Banoffee.  Delicious.  And for our trouble, they didn't charge us for this second dessert, which exhibits good overall sense and customer service.  While I would be willing to give Howie's another chance at a good meal, hoping the inconsistency was a rare event, my friend was so put off that she likely would not visit again.    Go for the dessert, and see what you think.  Meanwhile, I am wondering if I would perhaps be able to lure my friend back for the Banoffee alone. It was really that delightful.

We luckily stumbled upon this little gem while walking around Old Town in desperate need of some lunch. I'm quite fussy when it comes to food largely due to food intolerances but also because I refuse to eat meat that isn't at least free range. When I saw Howies sources their produce locally and that their chicken was free range I was sold. Even better the chicken dish was gluten and onion free!  Despite the restaurant being busy, we were quickly shown to a table and the service was very prompt and friendly. Our food took around 10 -15 minutes to come out.  It was delicious! The chicken was cooked the perfection, the chicken jus was tasty and the potatoes and beans rounded off the dish beautifully. I would have loved to have stayed and tried the dessert however as we were in a rush we had to go! I wouldn't hesitate to return.
Yummy authentic food at a fair price. Haggis was delicious followed by a lamb cassaerole better than my Mum made. No small accolade !

I really enjoyed the dining experience here. I had the 2 course dinner combo which was a great deal and the staff were all very friendly. I had haggis, neeps, and tatties for appetizer and the Scottish chicken breast for the main. I loved the haggis which was superb and the chicken was delicious as well, although it was a bit dry. I would definitely recommend Howies but it is a much better deal to come for lunch since they have the same menu but at a much cheaper price.

The hotel we are staying at recommended Howie's as a great restaurant to go to. When I initially saw the place, I thought it would be too upscale (I'm a big fan of comfortable pubs and restaurants with amazing food).  The staff was great, the food was amazing, and the interior was beautiful (high ceilings and a clean Victorian look).  The only reason why I'm giving them 4 stars instead of 5 is that i had ordered soup and they forgot. We ended up having our soup after the main meal. The staff was very apologetic and didn't charge us for the soup (which was really good btw).

A solid three-star location if you're searching for Scottish food. First course was Cullen skink which was warm, but distinctly fishy. Second course was risotto. Perfect texture and flavor. Dessert was a fruit trifle (maybe rhubarb?) which I didn't like - tasted like watery yogurt and stale granola. Complimentary bread was fresh and delicious. The waiters did a great job of handling a large group; they seemed a bit frazzled, but I suppose that's to be expected.   Would've been four stars except for the noise. This place is LOUD. I wound up screaming just to be heard by someone right next to me. I think it's because of the acoustics in the room, but it really made our experience difficult to e
Amazing! Best Cullen Skink in the city. I also ordered the Haggis, Neeps, and Tatties and they were fantastic. I will be visiting again next time I am in Edinburgh.

Howie's has an elegant interior and very friendly service, and was a lovely place for a big group of us to have dinner.  I'd make a reservation as we arrived at 5:30 on a Saturday, and by 6:30 it was really filling up. They were very accommodating with my friend's 4 year old son, as well!  They had Nanny State low-alcohol beer, my very favorite, so I applaud them for having something so tasty for preggos and non-drinkers.  I ended up getting their half lobster special - 14.95 for a half lobster in garlic butter, fries, and salad.  First, my husband and I shared the pigeon breast with black pudding, which was very good, all the other ingredients like golden raisins and pickled carrots played off each other beautifully.  The fresh-baked bread with olive oil and balsamic was a lovely thing to start with as well. You do have to pay for it, but it's cheap, so you aren't being ripped off by the bread basket.  Some of our friend started with the mussels and were really unhappy with them, and said they tasted fishy and weren't fresh.  They ended up exchanging for the haggis which everyone thought was delicious and loved. Staff were very accommodating and quick about this.  My lobster wasn't particularly hot, just warm, or particularly big, but the meat was tender and lovely, and I got big flavor from the garlic butter.  I just wanted more of it, and wanted it to feel a bit more piping hot.  The salad alongside was just some lightly dressed rocket, but the fries were golden and crisp and came in a big pile - as the lobster portion was small, I inhaled them all!  I tasted my husband's catch of the day (hake with chorizo and kale) which was good, but not as good as I hoped it would be, although beautifully presented.  Our sticky toffee pudding with ice cream was a classic example of the dish - a small portion, but extremely good and just the right temperature.  They were also very accommodating when 2 of us had to leave in a flash to make a train, letting us pay our part of the bill first and even bringing some shortbread cookies for everyone along with the bill.  We had a wonderful evening here with friends, but the food didn't stand out as exceptional.  It all looked beautiful, and some dishes were certainly better than others, but overall the presentation was superior to the preparation.

My wife and I chose to go to Howies for our 'fancy' dinner during our trip to Edinburgh and we had a lovely time.   Part of the reason we chose Howies was because it had a reputation for making really good haggis, which neither of us had tried before. So, as you can imagine, we started off the meal with the haggis, neeps, and tatties appetizer! Overall, it was quite good, though I should mention that it is a bit spicy. It's not much spice in an individual bite, but it does build as you eat.  For dinner, I got a fish course from their specials menu which was fantastic! And for dessert, my wife and I shared a chocolate and beetroot tart which was also quite good.  Overall, I recommend Howies. They've got a great selection of high quality Scottish food!

We loved our experience at Howies! We arrived at 6pm and benefitted from their Early Dinner special - 2 courses for 14.99 between 5:30-6:30pm.    We loved every dish we ordered! The seared pigeon breast was served medium with pink center, delicate flavor on a bed of herbs & sprouts. The Haggis was moist, delicious and served with mashed potato & rutabaga!  For our mains, we tried the daily catch (hake) and venison haunch- the venison was slightly tough, but gamey and flavorful with brown gravy!    Definitely try the Whisky Flight if you are a whisky fan! Our waitresses were amazing - highly attentive and checked in with us for every course. We hope to be back again soon :)

I was looking for a light lunch on our last day in Scotland, and wasn't disappointed with Howies. The placards they have outside look a bit too official and corporate, which gave me pause, but it was close to where we were staying and they had a lunch special on offer. Luckily the style of adverts outside don't define the dining experience inside.  I had the cullen skink and split the super salad with salmon, which was just the right amount of food so that I would be able to handle a big dinner later in the night.  The service was really friendly and quick, no complaints whatsoever in that department. The food was also very good as well. Cullen skink, as I'm given to understand it, is a very heavy, hearty soup, but it was delicious without weighing me down too much. It had a really nice combination of flavors. The salad was also delicious, with the salmon being perfectly cooked. The dressing was interesting - it could have used a bit of salt - but overall I was very satisfied.  Would definitely come back if I'm back in Edinburgh!

Our plane landed about 7:15p into Edinburgh and we knew we might start running out of dining options.  Fortunately, Howies was open until "late".   Even better the food was great!  We decided to the "Haggus, snippies & tatties" and Pigeon breast for appetizers.  Both were delicious.   I had the beef casserole - it was perfectly a spiced and cooked stew. Two folks had chicken and one of our party had the lamb.  We ended sharing bites because everyone loved there meals.   Incredibly tasty and fresh.   We shared a couple of the poached rhubarb deserts with apple sorbet.  It was a great end to a great meal.   We are only here for a short time, so I doubt we will make it back, but would all definitely recommend it.

What a great find on a small road. The food is solid, and it made for a perfect first meal in Edinburgh for me. I got the casserole of the day (beef), and husband got the venison. We also had cullen skink, which I'd never heard of, but is apparently a classic. I asked what vegetarian haggis was, and it was described as vegetables made to taste like real haggis. I wish I tried their haggis (vegetarian or classic). The casserole was solid, and the venison was quite good. I LOVED the cullen skink. Service is wonderful, vibe is casual (great after a day of travels and adventures), and prices very reasonable.

Great place at a great location. The prices are phenomenal considering the quality of the food. The atmosphere is nice with plenty of room and no pretentiousness. Only negative is that they staff is pretty aloof. They do get to you eventually, but don't come here if you are in a rush or if you are an impatient American. The staff is fun, but that may be the issue. They have so much fun interacting with each other, that I think they can forget about the customers. Just come here relaxed and chill, without other plans, and have a great meal at a great price.

Scottish food is not for me.  I wanted to experience real Scottish food so I ordered a whisky sampler and gnocchi. But, I actually really dislike whisky and gnocchi. I still wanted to give these items a chance and hoped that Howies, a highly ranked Scottish restaurant, would change my opinion of the country's food. Unfortunately, I was disappointed. I regret ordering the items I had chosen because I'm sure the restaurant offers food that I would've enjoyed.  --  taste / 1 aesthetics / 5 vibe / 5 service / 3 price for quality / 2 OVERALL / 3

We chose this place for Lunch time, as we have Scottish specialties for a good price. The restaurant atmosphere itself is simple and warm.  The waitress was friendly and nice. The service was good and fast. I had the Salmon and even if the quantity is not big, the quality was perfect. It was served with vegetables and perfectly cooked. I really enjoyed it. My friends ate the Haggis and the gnocchi and same, good food with a lot of flavours. I totally recommend this place for nice and cheap Scottish specialities!

Located on the gorgeous Victoria Street, this is one of the best places in town to get Cullen Skink (a classic Scottish dish of creamy fish soup). The food is consistently good and their lunch specials are really affordable too.

We found this restaurant on Yelp on our way to the castle.   Our waitress was super friendly and made some awesome recommendations. I can't remember her name but she was French. We started off with a few orders of bread and some drinks. The bread, which comes with oil and balsamic vinegar to dip in, was highly addicting! It was hot and fresh.  Our drinks were amazing! I ordered the gin spritz which was refreshing.   For my main meal I ordered the pan roasted chicken breast, served with potatoes and green beans. The portion was tiny and the chicken was a little bland. I wouldn't recommend the chicken dish. My boyfriend ordered the salmon and loved it.   For dessert, we ordered the toffee cake. Must get! Authentic and delicious!

Good food! We came for the 3 course lunch.   Starter = Cullen skink. So good. Full of flavor, perfect portion. Bread was also very fresh. Definitely the highlight of my meal. Entree = Chicken. Chicken was cooked perfectly and so we the veggies. I thought the entree was just okay, though. The sauce was a bit bland. I felt like it was missing something, but not sure what. Dessert = banana/biscuit pie. Good, but way too much whipped cream! We wound up scraping 90% of the cream off. It was just overwhelming and too thick.  Service was pretty awful, unfortunately. The restaurant itself is beautiful and it is in a great location.  Overall, I would come back.
An excellent meal with great service. Really good traditional but modern Scottish menu with focused on seafood with other options. Cullen Skink and Haggis FTW. Fish main plates were all delicious.

High yield: A scottish restaurant that offers truly scottish fare such as cullen skink, venison casserole, Atlantic Hake, catch of the day, salads, and soups but with aloof service despite a cheerful and nice environment. Prices are very decent, less than 10 pounds and large portions   Food: Great food and truly a must for those who want to experience Scottish food experience. We ordered the Atlantic Hake, Venison Casserole, Cullen Skink. I give them a 5/5 for food  Cullen Skink- it's a fish chowder with potatoes and is super hearty and delicious. I highly recommend this to anyone visiting Scotland- flavor is warm and comfortable and great for a cold day. You can get it as a bowl or as a main entree.  Venison Casserole- Tasted like a beef stew with carrots and on top a dollop of Mashed Potatoes. highly recommend too, cuz where else you gonna eat Venison?? And the price was less than 9 pounds.  Atlantic Hake: There is catch of the day, which usually is Salmon but to me if you're gonna try out a Scottish dish, go for their local fish which is this hake. it is a white fleshed fish that is a very soft version of tilapia or even Halibut. It's not chickeny or fishy tasting, and doesn't have that flaky feeling that some ocean fish have. No bones inn this fillet and comes with veggies underneath.   Service: i won't lie but this what prevented me from giving them the 5/5. I have never seen such rude/aloof service in all of Edinburgh. Staff was like robots doing their job for sake of doing rather than actually caring about the customers. We asked for hot water refill and that took forver, and saw our waitress busying herself with setting up tables etc that were items I felt could have waited. We asked her to take a photograph and she kept saying 2 mins while she finishes with another customer... and another customer.... and another. When she did serve us, very cold and kind of insincere. so I have to give her a 2/5 for service. The other waiters also seemed like that too except the drinks guy in the front.   Price: Everything less than 10 pounds. No reason why anyone would not give this place a shot if they are wanting scottish fare.

Attracted by the many favorable YELP reviews ( and a friendly tip from a fellow traveler at our hotel),  we felt we had to give Howies a try.  Both the digital and human assessments were on the money! Howies is a must stop for the weary traveler in search of authentic Scottish fare. Our meal was delightful and delicious. Don't be afraid of the haggis, It tastes like meatloaf, bu a bit grainier! If you want a more thorough review, check out Sandy J's 12/28/2106 review.  She said it all!

Couldn't leave Edinburgh without one last haggis.  We came to Howies for the super affordable lunch specials (10.95 for 2 courses, 13.95 for 3).  I did the two courses. I had the haggis as my starter, and the poached salmon as my main. If I had to do it all over again, I'd do the haggis as my main, because it was damn good. Portions were a bit tiny, but that's to be expected. The salmon was good, but nothing to write home about.  Would definitely recommend stopping in for lunch!

Lovely little local producing consistently good food at reasonable prices for the city centre. Staff are friendly & helpful. Chef does a good range of specials.   We had the sea bass with crushed potatoes and the lamb casserole for mains. Both decent sized portions and full of flavour.   If you want a decent meal  you won't go wrong here. Solid 3.5 stars

Probably the best meal and dining experience we had in Edinburgh. Could have been 4 stars, but considering the other restaurants we visited this one deserves 5. You'll have to book ahead. We walked in on a Friday night and were politely told there were no tables available for any time that night, so we went ahead and booked for Saturday.   We started with focaccia and the trio of olives, hummus, and olive tapenade. The tapenade was a little dry, but the bread was delicious, as were the olives. We then tried the haggis and Cullen skink appetizers. The haggis was delicious, and by far the best we had on the trip. If in doubt, try it! I didn't care as much for the Cullen skink, but maybe it just wasn't to my taste - a little too salty for me.   For mains we had the salmon (wonderful), lamb (although the accompanying lentils were undercooked), soup of the day (sweet potato and coconut - good), and ribeye with frites. My steak was well cooked, but it lacked flavor a bit. It was good, but I would choose something else if visiting again.   For dessert we had the poached rhubarb, banoffee pie, brownie, and sticky toffee pudding. All were good. The pudding was decadent, and I was glad there was accompanying ice cream, which cut the sweetness.   Make a booking - you'll enjoy!

Scott the bartender provided great customer service. He recommended the pigeon & haggis for starter, main lamb and the fish of the day which was hake in a brown butter hollandaise sauce. The starters and mains were perfectly sized and we did not feel overly stuffed at the end of our meal.  Bottle of wine recommended by Scott was also very good - Pinot noir By Domaine de Valent Liam was our server and did a great job.

We had a wonderful welcome---we started with haggis, neeps and tatties. My love got a steak and he said it was one of the best steaks of his life. I had the rump of borders lamb and particularly enjoyed the mint and pine nut pesto. Great wine selection and a very memorable meal. This is not your average food and staff was helpful and efficient throughout which made it a lovely dining experience, would highly recommend to foodies.

Such a lovely experience here to end our time in Scotland. The mabience of this place is spacious with the tall ceilings, elegant and bright with natural light. We were sat at a nice table near the window. We ordered the lobster and the lamb. Both were cooked perfectly and paired well with our Happy Hour champagne. Our server was sweet and took good care of us. The bread was fresh and we left happily after some tea. Thank you for a lovely time.

Howies was my very first meal in Scotland, which set a nice precedent for the rest of our trip. My husband and I ate here for lunch and were very impressed by the the simple, yet elegant, atmosphere. The staff was professional, and the food was fresh and thoughtfully prepared and plated. We had Scottish highlights such as cullen skink, mushroom soup, leek risotto, and pan fried hake (catch of the day). I thought everything was spot on, including the complimentary bread.   How would I describe Howies in two words? "Scottish bistro," if that makes any sense. They feature fresh, locally sourced ingredients. The chefs give a damn about presentation and attention to details. It's a good compromise between having to go to a pub or a high-end restaurant for a meal. I thought prices were very reasonable.

Such a great experience! Friendly service, quick food preparation, and some of the best flavors in all of the UK! The chicken was absolutely delicious. It was packed, but our server was so attentive and kind. Also, their bread is...otherworldly. And their olive oil. I don't know how it's so goddamn special, but it really, really is.

We ordered two venison dishes and they were great but what really blew me away was the TOFFEE PUDDING. Best I've ever had! Also, make sure to order the fresh bread. It was soft and warm and so perfect for a chilly, rainy night.

Love love love! Everything about this place was so perfect. The dim lighting and cool colors make this romantic, modern vibe. The Christmas lights added a really cozy aspect. And then the food was a standout on its own. Mmmmmmm! The Cullen Skink was creamy and warm the soul worthy. I loved my salmon entree too. Super fresh and cooked so great. Tender and moist. The staff was friendly and made us feel right at home.

Despite being a chain of restaurants, Howies of Victoria Street seems to keep some of its individuality - possibly from the finest of all four of the restaurants manu's.  It's most certainly Scottish, but not as we know it Jim. Using local produce, Howies have managed to create a simply mouth watering modern and yet somehow traditional menu using Scottish classics such as Salmon and Haggis without becoming some kind of Scottish Medevil Theme Restaurant.  The restaurant itself is cozy and clean, with a brilliant atmosphere that is both buzzing and vibrant, but also intimate and close all at the same tiem.  I havent always been happy with the Howies Chain (sorry! set of four individual restaurants under the same name) but this is the nicest by a long way.

I ate here after losing a 'where will we have dinner' argument. Even so, after reading about Howies and hearing good things from friends I was looking forward to it.  Both myself and The OH had the same starter, Scottish smoked salmon with salad and a thai dressing.  The OH likes his meat and so his face dropped, quite noticeably, when the starters arrived and we were greeted by a mound of green with flecks of salmon scattered throughout.   For my main I had a pork chop with winter vegetables. It was tasty, but dry. Dry pork gets on my nerves so between it and the starter I wasn't too happy with Howies so far.  However, the desserts are amazing in Howies. The cream concoctions are so delicious. I'm not big on desserts but I tried some off every plate on the table! I can see why the banoffi is much loved.  I found the waitress quite casual and friendly but The OH was annoyed by her slight forgetfulness and over familiarity.  From my one experience here, Howies seems a mixed bag. I'll definitely go back as the menu is interesting and the price is right, but my rating is based on this visit.

Went here for the first time a couple of weeks ago. Nice interior and a good varied menu. The special of the day was a lovely venison steak. The staff were  friendly and helpful. Nice central location if you plan on going out afterwards in the Grassmarket/Royal Mile area.

Of Edinburgh's four 'branches' of Howie's,  (they dislike being referred to as a chain, as each restaurant attempts to have its own identity and creates its own menu ) this is my favourite to come to for dinner. It has a sense of intimacy and romantic atmosphere that the other 'branches' haven't quite managed to cultivate. The menu is based around Scottish produce (Shetland salmon, Stornoway black pudding) and changes seasonally. They use organic bread from local baker Breadwinner, which is always fresh and delicious, and your first bowl is complimentary which I think is a nice touch. It would be fair to say that I've never had a bad meal here.   The restaurant is located in one of the city's prettiest streets and is perfectly situated for heading out into town after your meal, although I'd recommend that you nip across the road to the Bow Bar for a digestif first.

Lost count of the times I've been here over the last few years, with parties large or small. In my opinion the best of the Edinburgh Howies.   My visit this week was no exception to the standard of service and quality of the menu that I've come to expect. The haggis starter was tasty and the main course of parsnip, pepper & something tart was delicious and filling. Finished off with the renowned banoffi pie and efficiently served throughout this was yet another enjoyable meal in a deservedly popular Edinburgh institution.

Two of us went to have a nice dinner at Howie's. Everyone was courteous and the food was delicious. Though the service was very friendly, there were some moments we could not get anyone's attention. For the price, I thought the atmosphere/decor was a little underwhelming. The cooking on the night we went was excellent. Overall, I'd say it is worth booking and going.

I like Howie's, it's always got a really strong and vibrant atmosphere and even if it's not really busy, the music and the staff make it seem like it is.  I had a lovely and light duck salad to start, it was really tasty. My brothers both had haggis which they  said was brilliant. Haggis tends to get a bad press, most people would see it on a menu and avoid like the plague, but this version would make me order it. For main I had the special of the day, which was GORGEOUS  - venison with cabbage and potatoes in a red currant jus has never tasted so delicious. My brothers wern't too happy with their seabream (the healthy option, what did they expect) but said the banoffee pie was  delicious. The interior is lovely too, the stone walls work well. The waitress was lovely too - she was interested in the food and very helpful!

This is my favourite of all the Howies Restaurants. It's more intimate, friendly and comfortable, and the location couldn't be any more central.   It's reasonably well priced - especially for lunch, and the Scottish themed food is always very well presented and of good quality. Howies, while licensed, also allow you to 'bring your own bottle' if you so wish. Perfect if you're looking for a nice meal out but are looking to cut costs. Or, if you're particularly fussy about your wine and like to know what you're buying. The Howies website occasionally has vouchers available to print off for meals at reduced prices (buy two courses, get a third free etc), so it's worth checking this out before booking.   I've organised a Christmas meal for a larger group of people at Howies Victoria Street in previous years, however unfortunately I was rather disappointed. The booking time was mixed up (the restaurant wasn't ready for us when we arrived - their clock had stopped so they'd lost track of time), and as a result we had to wait for the best part of half an hour, then were rushed through our meal and hurried off the table when we weren't entirely finished, just to fit the next booking in. Whilst this wasn't a great experience - and I'd be reluctant to book Howies for a large Christmas party again, I won't let this tarnish my perception of the restaurant otherwise. Christmas is always a little hectic anyway.   Oh the whole, great food, nice settingI recommend this restaurant.

Howie's is indeed an Edinburgh institution, deservedly so, and you're almost sure to get a very decent meal here for a very decent price.   They seem to have abandoned the fixed price menu - or had last night at any rate. It always made group bookings so much easier to manage when it came to splitting the bill. But the prices are still fairly reasonable - 4ish for a starter, 10 to 16 for a main course and 4 to 6 for desserts.   Importantly, they let you bring your own bottles which can help to alleviate the cost of eating out somewhat - particularly if you drink as much as I.   I haven't been to the Victoria Street place before. I'm a Bruntsfield girl by preference. But the food was pretty good. I had a very tasty haggis as a starter and then a half disappointing vegetable strudel which looked a little less appealing that it turned to be. And then I had some very nice cheese though oh my, the oatcakes were hard as hard cardboard.   I can't comment on the wine as we guzzled our own.   And the general decor and ambience of the place was very nice. Bustley enough to be good for groups - or pairs where conversation might be flagging.   The waitress was a bit of a sourpuss was my only criticism. But maybe she was having a bad day.

Howies Restaurant was the food highlight of a short break in Edinburgh, it was highly recommended by our hotel (Tigerlillys) and rightly so, the food was outstanding. It wasnt busy at the time but the atmosphere was still good, friendly staff, good table by the window and a nice bottle of wine. Cant remember what we ate but my boyfriend had a chicken dish and i had food envy!!
Good dinner, very tender lamb. The only problem is that the service was very slow. It took ages from the first dish to the second.

Had the beef casserole. Was alright, but nothing to write home about. Also they "discretely" add a service charge and awkwardly ask if you would like to add the tip at the time of check out. Other than that, food was good.

Well established, well tasty, well central and well wouldn't you believe it a bit of an Edinburgh institution. I don't eat at Howie's regularly, but knowing that it's there and ready to tick all the necessary boxes to offer you a memorable dining experience is comfort enough. It helps that Howie's is tucked in at the top of Victoria Street, one of the most attractive areas in the city and within striking distance of several appealing watering holes for a post-prandial pint.  On my most recent visit I dined on partridge, Stornaway black pudding, salmon and other bits and pieces - I forget the details. [This may be seen as a contradiction to my earlier statement about the memorableness of the experience. Ahem.]  The service was fine, the range of menu choices suitable for everyone in my group and the atmosphere one of contented chat from all diners in this welcoming establishment.

The atmosphere was great and highly suggest for dating dinner or having lunch with friends. I think this restaurant is casual style but if you want to dress up it wont be strange either. We ordered the 2 courses special menu, all of them are exceed our expectation which are so great. The light salad is perfect as starter even if you have no appetite for a big lunch. My friend ordered the creamy fish soup which is so creamy and taste good, but if you are not that found of creamy food,i suggest that you can just go for some lighter choice. The main courses we ordered the chef of the day fish, the fish was perfectly cooked and fresh fish. The price is exceed our expectation again, which was so valuable. We are definitely will go back gain!

Greetings from NYC! Loved it here. Walked in for a late lunch after visiting St. James Court Factory Outlet. I had bread w olive oil, 175 Chile's sav. Blanc (great bargain for NYers), calamari and salmon. Salmon was moist and good. The breadcrumbs on top of it were good too. The calamari was crunchy and good too. 2 courses for L9.95... Great meal! I'll return the next time I am in EDI....

What a great little resturant.  I've done dinner and lunch there now and both were excellent.  The wait staff is attentive, and their 2/3 course specials are a good deal.  On the dinner side I had haggis/nips/tattis and a pork steak over mash.  The starter was excellent, with a bacon shave over it.  The pork steak was tender, juicy and perfectly seasoned.  It went well with the green beans in bacon/butter sauce.  On the lunch side I took an all daily special set for 7.95 - spicy tomato soup was fantastic and the beef and venison casserole was delicious.  I'd highly recommend you give it a try...

Just like Alex, I've harboured a love of potatoes ever since they were used to unintentionally comic effect during the nine hours of relentless boredom and homoerotica that was the Lord of the Rings trilogy. Our soil-dwelling friends are regular lunchtime choice for me, and Edinburgh seems to have it's fair share of Baked Potato takeaways to pick from.  The Tattie shop's location a bit out of the way sadly means I rarely get to visit, but I wish I had more opportunities. While I'll stick my neck out and suggests that the taters themselves aren't quite as good as Tempting Tattie in town, the fillings are some way ahead, especially the chilli con carne which is oddly absent from the menu at their city centre rival.  All round it's pretty excellent, and another jewel in the crown of the quite splendid Bruntsfield locality.

A nicely baked tattie let down by filling. - I felt, for the price, that this business scrimped on the amount of filling. It was really measly in comparison to similar businesses.  Other than that, I've no complaints. But when my favourite baked potato shop does the humble baked tattie so well, I wouldn't return to anywhere that does a poor job. Part of an amazing baked potato is the comforting mix of filling with the hot buttery centre. The amount of filling here made this tattie fall flat.  Tattie shops tend to do much better with baked potatoes over cafes, which is why I was excited to try The Tattie Shop one lunchtime. Sadly, I was disappointed.

I've been a fan of The Tattie Shop for a few years now and have seen it go through 2 different owners, a face lift and a menu shake up, which does suggest to me that I eat far too many complex carbohydrates than is normal for the average human being.  This is a lovely little shop down the lane that is parallel to the Bruntsfield Public Toilets (it smells a HELL of a lot better, don't worry) that serves up decent grub at a just above average price.  After being taken over fairly recently (maybe the last year or so), the tatties have shrunk in size which is actually a good thing, the last owners tatties sometimes being too much for me. The menu selection is a pretty standard affair as well with the option to customise your tattie the way you want it. My personal favourite being the chilli and cheese with the cheese on first.  The price does go a bit further than it should and I would maybe put that down to the cost of rates in the area, but for when it's freezing outside and you need somewhere to sit down and get something warm in your belly, the price is justified. Just don't make a habit of it, with a chilli and cheese tattie & can of juice coming to around the 5 mark.  Another tip I would give would be not to go here during school lunch hours, it's an absolute nightmare and I actually ended up wedged in to the back corner of the shop for about 10 minutes until the horde dispersed.

'Po-ta-toes...boil 'em, mash 'em, stick 'em in a stew' quoth the wise Hobbit Samwise Gamgee, but he forgot probably the best potato of all, the baked. It is a monster spud; when cooked to perfection with crisp skin and stuffed with an amalgam of different fillings, it is a God among veg. The Tattie Shop has perfected the art of baked potatoes; they are without doubt the best in Edinburgh.  Tucked into a side street just in Bruntsfield, The Tattie Shop is easily missed but do this at your peril. They have a huge amount of fillings, with the haggis being excellent, as well as the chilli con carne. You can create a tattie with as many fillings in as you like, just don't overdo it or you'll struggle to eat it all, they are remarkably filling. With prices being very reasonable and the owner a good laugh, it is one potato purveyor not to be missed

I've walked by the sign for the Tattie Shop again and again, and every time I am tempted to try it.  On a particularly blustery day I thought it would be the perfect time.  I scanned the menu looking for something which sounded nice or otherwise interesting, but it was all pretty standard fare.  I opted for chili and added cheese.  The helpings were generous but the filling was not as flavoursome as I expect from chili and cheese, and at 4.10, the tattie hurt my purse strings far more than it should have.   The helpings were generous, but it was far too much food for me and I would have been much happer to have smaller portions to go along with a cheaper tattie.    All in all, the meal was fine but I don't expect to be returning.  It just wasn't tasty or cheap enough to warrant a trip out for lunch.

Just off Commercial Street on Sandport Street, Domenico's does quite simply the best takeaway sandwich in Edinburgh. This tiny deli-cum-cafe is massively popular with office workers in the Shore area and the queue at lunchtimes is usually onto the street but it is well worth the wait every time. You choose your roll then select from a mouth-watering range of sandwich options or invent your own from the staggering array of ingredients in front of you. The black olive pesto is particularly good but it's pretty hard to go wrong. There are also a few tables if you want to eat in and when you do the food is equally amazing. Book a table or you've little chance of even getting in the door.
lovely resturant  great food big helpings and very friendly staff  I had scallops cooked to perfection

Leith is no stranger to good eats of all varieties, and Cafe Domenico is another in a long list of restaurants that has solidified my opinion of the district being a culinary headquarters for the city.  Cafe Domenico is set up in a tiny building off Commercial Street that is easy to miss unless you are looking for it. Don't let the outside fool you though. The interior is intimate without being cramped. Italian decor fills the walls without feeling cheesy. They've really managed to capture the spirit of a Roman trattoria with a low key setting and simple menu.  Brittany A. and I stopped by about an hour and a half before closing on a Wednesday night. The cafe was fairly packed at the time, but we were seated instantly. The staff are very cordial and will go out of their way to make you comfortable, including checking your coat. The menu is composed of several pasta dishes, some mains, sides, and desserts. Some of the dishes are classic Italian, while others infuse a Scottish twist. Ever tried veal and haggis pasta? They also run a few daily specials. From Monday through Wednesday night the cafe offers a pasta dish and a glass of wine for only 8.50. I couldn't resist such a deal, while Brittany opted for the lasagna on special for 10. We both split a starter of their mozzarella garlic bread, which uses panini pressed Italian bread covered in garlic, butter, and melted mozzarella atop a bed of rocket.   When our mains arrived I could not believe how huge the portion was, since the menu stated that the pasta special included a 'small' portion. My dish was composed of a large bowl of penne pasta, covered in a pesto creme sauce with a head of broccoli and spinach thrown in. I asked for a heap of freshly grated cheese and pepper thrown in for good measure. The pasta was perfectly cooked, and the creme sauce delicate and flavourful. I was so stuffed that I did not get a chance to sample their tasty looking desserts.  Cafe Domenico is what the UK needs more of - a humble, family run eatery that knows its customers like family and creatively adapts a cuisine to its locale.

I went here for the first time with a friend last week , was pleasantly surprised . Lovely cosy and well decorated place , candles , mirrors , etc. The waitress was lovely and made you feel welcome , as did the owner who came out to say hello. Great for lunch or dinner . Food was great and a drinks menu if you want. Will definitely return !!

This place is a family favourite of ours! Can't fault the gorgeous Italian food and the service is always top notch. They're super accommodating and very friendly.  Organised a birthday lunch here for my brother with kids and adults and when one of the toddlers got a bit restless they suggested taking him out to the nearby playpark. Such a good idea! It was quite a disorganised affair but they handled our booking fabulously, always worth a trip down Leith for a meal here!

As I have mentioned before, I am an insufferable boring snob when it comes to Italian food outside of Italy. I'm so horrible that I don't even want to listen to myself go on about it, which is why I rarely bother to try Italian restaurants in the UK at all. But when other people suggest a friendly meet-up at one, I try not to be a jerk about it, so I just show up with a smile. Which explains how I ended up at Domenico one evening. Lucky for me, because it was an utterly charming experience. The service was personable, welcoming, and accommodating. The food was, well, pretty good. Pasta cooked correctly. Good house wine at a reasonable price. Decent grappa.   I would go again. This is high praise, I assure you.

Well as #Cocktailquest strives to find the best in mixology the city has to offer Robyn wisely suggested we get some dinner first to ensure we were all 100% ready for the challenge that lay ahead.  Having lived and worked in Leith in the past Domenicos is close to my heart, from their daily lunchtime specialis to the focaccia sandwiches they have always been at hand with a taste of Italy.   So as to last night, 8 hungry Yelpers deceneded looking for a comforting meal on a cold night. From the minute you walk in the door Tony greets you like a long lost friend. His hospitality is second to none. I was running erm rather late for dinner so instructed Caz to order on my behalf. Having been given 3 options I went for the seafood stew....it was a good choice.  As a starter we were given a selection of anti-pasti - cheese...meats....ccheeeeese, roasted veg.....lovely.  To my fish stew - mussels, salmon, squid, haddock...smoked haddock all in a lovely broth. With bread on the side for mopping this was a very enjoyable dish. The mussels and the smoked fish were particularly tasty.   For desert I initially ordered the tiramisu - as it seemed I was getting the last one I agreed to share with Scott so we both got half tiramisu/ half banoffee pie. Nice enough and washed down with a lemoncello even better :)

Good service and even better food!  I went in late on a weekday lunchtime for a sandwich so they were pretty much shutting up. The staff were friendly though and happy to have a look about to see what they had left.   I went for a 'mexican' sandwich off the specials board. Freshly cooked (I assume) breadcrumbed chicken, salsa, guacamole, rocket, jalapenos, and no doubt some other things I can't remember. All the ingredients were great, from the bread to the rocket and especially the chicken. The combination worked really well too, it's good to get something that has had a bit of thought put into the flavours rather than just chucked together.  All in all a great visit, and cheap too for what I got. I'll certainly be returning a bit earlier next time and maybe sometime to try the restaurant/cafe for a sit in meal.

From the when you enter the door, to the moment you sit back and sigh after a happy, hearty meal, Cafe Domenico makes you feel like you've been embraced in the welcoming hug of a True Italian family.  Cafe Domenico is one of the most charming, delicious spots in Edinburgh and Leith, with fresh, exquisite ingredients, real Italian cooking, and genuine, kindly and fun service. If I could, I would visit Cafe Domenico for breakfast, lunch and dinner every single week.   Particular favourites are their lunchtime sandwiches, wraps and pastas - these cause a queue around the corner they are so scrumptious! For dinner, the intimate surroundings are perfect for a romantic date, or a family get together. Their antipasti platters are some of the most impressive I've seen in Edinburgh, and they are always happy to adapt meals off their menu or specials to suit your every whim!
Good menu choice for a small restaurant. Nice quaint atmosphere and good pasta. Had the daily special of rigatoni, very nice.

wednesday night found me merrily skipping my way from the bus stop to the warm lights of this restaurant that i have been desperate to try for ages!!  i was so excited, as the only reviews i'd ever heard about cafe domenicos could be summed up with the word AMAZING.  opening the door i was first greeted by one of my lovely night out companions sitting down followed by the handsome waiter asking if i would like my coat hung up.  so with a good looking man providing the service, the evening was already off to a great start!  our third companion for the night came along shortly after and we deliberated over the menus.  the first thing i noticed about the menu was how concise it was.  about 6 starters, 6 pasta dishes, and 4-5 main courses and a handful of specials.  even with limited options though i still found it rather difficult to make my choice!  after a bit of debate and discussion with the waiter we ordered the fig and blue cheese bruschetta, a tomato, mozarella, and pesto bruschetta, spicy sausage and red pepper pasta (extra chilli and garlic), auberigne and tomato pasta, and pesto, spinach, and broccoli pasta.  just a note, they offer a deal monday thru wednesday for a pasta dish and a glass of wine for 7.50.  they kindly subsituted my glass of wine for a diet coke as i wasn't drinking that night.   The bruschettas took a bit of time to arrive as the waiter made them all fresh, but they were definitely worth the wait.  each toasted piece of fresh bread was topped high with tasty ingredients accompanied by a sizeable portion of rocket and tomato salad dressed with olive oil.  both bruschettas were very good but i have to say the figs with blue cheese was just delicious!  the combination of the sweet fig with the salty slightly pungent blue cheese and the crispy bread was like bruschetta heaven in my mouth....  pastas arrived in an appropriate time after our starters had been cleared and for 7.50 (including the drink) these were very good portions!!  my plate held a very pleasing meal of spinach and broccoli with penne pasta mixed through with fresh pesto and just a hint of cream to bring it all together.  topped with parmesan, i very happily ate the lot because it was so tasty and comforting.  my fellow companions also found their dishes very tasty and we were even paid a visit by the chef to see how our dinners were.  as we had a movie to go to and decided to get some cinema treats, we didn't get dessert although there were a few tasty options on the menu.  the waiter kindly brought the cheque and was happy to accept three forms of payment as well.    i was very impressed with cafe domenico and felt that it completely lived up to expectations and i'm looking forward to going back already!  the excellent customer service and their willingness to tailor dishes or make them up specific to a diner's need was a really nice touch.  not too mention how delicious and fresh the food is and the excellent value for money, seriously can this place do anything wrong?  perhaps as i'm desperate to get lunch there as both my friends raved about the quality of the sandwiches, but working many miles away from leith will not allow such luxuries.  maybe they could set up a delivery service???
Great little haven.  Family business run on lots of heart. Lovely food. Exceptionally reasonable prices. A must-try !
Amazing sandwiches for take away lunch; lovely lunchtime pasta dishes; create rustic evening dishes. An absolute winner and Lunch Quest favourite.

If you want great not just good but really great Italian Food this is the place to go. It is on the outskirts of town but it is well worth a trip. Accessible by the #22 bus from town. For starters we ordered Bruschetta (Basil pesto, mozzarella cheese and fresh tomatoes) 4.50 and Mussels Marinera 4.50 The Bruschetta was deliciously full of flavour. For the main dish I had the Ravioli with Wild Mushroom in a cream sauce. Oh man! It was heaven! James had the pasta with chorizo and sea food. We both ordered off the "specials for the day" menu and loved our choices. The house wine was smooth and easy.

Domenicos is simply the best place to get a sandwich at lunchtime in Leith. Fresh ingredients, generous portions, and great service not to mention the incredible prices. The pasta is also great if you're not in a sandwich mood.

I've had 2 takeaway meals from here on separate occasions and have enjoyed both. I've ordered online for collection and both times the service I received was excellent - friendly staff and timely receipt of food. I've had one chicken dish and one vegetarian dish, accompanied by a naan. The mains were packed with flavour (not hot spice, which I'm too wussy for) and were good-sized portions. The naans however are another story altogether - ginormous! I had the Peshwari Naan both times and was possibly the highlight of the meal, especially as I had leftovers to accompany 2 more meals.  Guru Balti also have a nice-looking sit-in restaurant, although both times I have visited to collect my takeaways, it has been empty (mid-week evenings).

I have been to the Guru Balti a few times, over several years. It can be summed up as offering good quality meat and above average curry, though the hotter dishes tend to lack that real zing of back end heat. They have some of the best and biggest naan bread though their rice doesn't particularly stand out.  The restaurant tends to be fairly quiet through the week, making it a good choice for post cinema eating if you happen to be at the nearby Cineworld. Guru is a good choice for an Indian meal and if you live in the area it should probably be your Indian restaurant of choice.

Gur Balti is an amazing Indian restaurant on Dundee Terrace which consistently offers delicious food and great service at reasonable prices.  I've been here twice with some friends and both times we've gone away more than satisfied with the whole experience.   They pride themselves on serving some of the best Indian food in the city and each dish is presented immaculately.  The menu has loads to choose from and the last time I was in I went for the Balti Chicken Passanda.  It seemed to take no time to arrive and tasted creamy with a great range of flavours.  All the meat which they use is of the highest quality and you can definitely taste the difference in all their meat dishes. We all spent no more than 15 each, including drinks, rice and tips, and we'll hopefully be back sometime soon.

My flatmates and I have tried various Indian takeaways but we always seem to back to the Guru because their food is simply amazing.  Balti as good as it gets.  And the naan breads are giant. It may not be the cheapest place for a takeaway but totally worth every penny! I have not eaten in the restaurant so cannot comment on the service.

The Guru is a traditional Balti restaurant on Dundee Street in Edinburgh. It is run traditionally and there is always a struggle to get a tabel if you dont boook in advance as it is quite a small place.  The menu is extensive with all the favourites korma, Jalfrezi, Rogan Josh and a good few speacialities. The food is fresh and very tasty. A main course tends to be about 8-9 and then rice on top of that. The sides are great and the nan bread is huge - DO NOT get more than one!  The staff are excellent and do their best to make sure you have a great time, they are very humerous.  Also it is bring your own bottle with a cheap corkage charge which helps cut the cost of eating out.  On the whole this is a great place to go either with a group of friends or for a nice romantiv meal it really is excellent!

Guru Balti changed my life; before my first visit in 2007 I thought I hated Indian food. It is at Guru that I learned curry doesn't have to be burn your gob off spicy; their lamb passanda is absolutely gorgeous. Their nan breads (my favourite part of any Indian meal) are absolutely humungous. It's a very very small restaurant, with only a few tables, but the illusion is that it is bigger by having a full size mirror across one wall. I would definitely suggest booking a table if you're in the Fountainpark area and give this place a whirl. Mmmmm!

The Guru is an excellent Indian restaurant, the best in Edinburgh if you ask me! The menu is extensive, the food is beautiful and really good value. The staff are great and you really feel like you are getting a specialist service just for you.  It is really quite busy though so try and book a table or you might have to wait a while!

Pizza Posto is great. I ordered the special pizza, which contained a couple slices with artichokes, a couple with pepperoni, a couple with prosciutto, and a couple with mushrooms. I also had their beer that was on tap. That pizza had great flavor. The servers were pleasant and accommodating.   The service was great. Bonus: the table next to us couldn't finish their Prosecco and gave it to us! Thank you to the two ladies.   There is also a ramp, so the restaurant is accessible.

A pleasant surprise in the overloaded pizza restaurant market of Edinburgh.  Pizza Posto is located opposite to the Festival Theatre, on Nicolson Street, where a decade ago used to be the infamous Ti Amo restaurant.  First things first, front of house (which ever waiter is free-ish) accommodated me in no time in one of its front tables, which was a bit drafty as single window panels have no sealant between them, but it wasn't a big deal.  I ordered the pizza number 5 with spicy Italian salami, mozzarella, tomato base and olive oil plus mushrooms as an extra topping.  The order took a bit long to arrive as the pizza chefs were dealing with a couple of over-populated tables. The service was efficient but a bit detached.   The number 5 looks really good and healthy (AKA no dripping grease) and tasted like the genuine article as you can identify and degust the main flavours, from the properly made pizza dough, to the good quality mozzarella, aromatic tomato sauce and the tasty but not that fiery spicy salami. The added mushrooms came from an oil marinated mushrooms flask rather than their fresh counterpart, nevertheless it was a great flavour addition to the number 5.   The quality/price ratio was really good as the number 5 was  8 +  1 for the extra topping, a price that cannot be beaten in the Edinburgh catering scene.  I'll certainly go back to try some other flavour combinations.  Recommended.

Too few people know about Pizza Posto. It looks fairly new, and is kind of in a busy area near the uni and the Festival Theatre, so I wonder why it wasn't so busy when I popped in.  I was seeing a musical called SIX at the Underbelly in George Square. I'd just picked up my ticket from their box office and had just over an hour and 15 minutes to kill before the show. I remembered seeing a nice looking pizza place around the corner so headed back up there.  I walked in, got seated immediately, and promptly ordered myself a margarita pizza and a can of Coke. Now in a place like this - authentic clay ovens, exposed bricks and lightbulbs, you would expect it to be nearly 16 but my bill only came to 7.50 at the end of it all.  The service is good too. The waitresses I encountered were friendly and efficient at bringing out the food. The barman seemed pretty funny too.  For a pre-theatre meal in the Southside, it just has to be here. It's cheap, quick and much better supporting a local business than overpriced chains such as Pizza Hut and Dominos.

Huge restaurant with ample seating, which, to me would generally mean you're going to get perhaps decent food, but nothing that transcends... but no! This was our top choice for pizza in town, and had all the flavor and blistered-crust glory of the kind of pie you'd get in some little intimate gourmand or mom-and-pop Italian spot, yet in a cavernous space that could house a Times Square crowd. It was for sure a surprise, but a very happy one, and we came back a few times because we liked it that much.  The prices are quite reasonable and the pizza, oh it's so good. While you're plenty fine with anything on the menu (I'm a big fan of anything with garlic, mozz, tomato and pepperoni-- or spicy salami, I guess they say here?) number ten's "award-winning Grande Italia" was SO good-- it came with a WHOLE BURRATA on top! That's like an appetizer with your pizza. Loved cutting it up and spreading it on some crust. They ship in their ingredients from Italy, which often is a gimmick when restaurants make claims like that, but having traveled to Italy literally a week after eating here, I can say it's legit. (San Marzano tomatoes are everything!) Ironically, the pizza we had in Italy wasn't even as good as here, but that's another sad story. So... go here while you can! (Also, give their pizza specials a try, since those change and always sound interesting!)

We had the most delightful waiter (at least until about midway through our visit, when he took off - guess his shift was over!). He made everything so pleasant for us when we came in for brunch. He had some tourist tips for us, and he also let my son and youngest daughter help make the fresh squeezed orange juice (with the help of special juicing machine). Great juice they said! I had French toast with bacon. It was good, especially with both syrup and jam. My wife and oldest shared a ham and cheese panini, which they said was just ok. It was accompanied by fries and slaw, which they said were not good. Still, I give this little spot four stars for a friendly and fun brunch experience.

Honestly, this was such a fantastic find for breakfast. There was always one table available for us. The staff were all so friendly. Even with the Fringe Festival going on around us it was nice to just sit and have a bit of food here. If you can grab a seat outside, you spend all meal people watching. Inside is tight but cozy.   I grabbed the mini breakfast both visits. It was such a great size and not at all mini. One fried egg with two sausages, two slices of bacon, beans, toast. The works. The pies were really delicious and the gravy was perfect for dipping fries in. The pot of tea was perfect to warm you up for the Scottish morning.

***FAST, FILLING, AND REASONABLY PRICED***  I had just gotten into Edinburgh the night before and slept in so late that missed free breakfast at my hostel.  My breakfast dedication undeterred, I set out to get some authentic Scottish breakfast without breaking the bank.  I then stumbled upon Angus Fling Cafe, knowing the breakfast gods had answered my prayers.  For breakfast options, you can choose between an authentic Scottish, English, and American breakfasts. Naturally I went with the first one.  For about 8 and a have Euro, you get a fresh egg, tomato, potato patty, toast, beans, and a (surprisingly flavorful) black cake thing (pardon my touristy ignorance).  It was the perfect remedy to cure what ailed me! I didn't get a look at the lunch items but from what I could gaze on the tables around me the meals looked tip top.  Bottom line: If you're looking for a star quality meal at off Broadway prices, come to the Angus Fling Cafe!

Great little place! Little is the key word, this place is tiny and it looks like a hole in the wall kind of place. If you can find a place here, it'll be one of you best dining experiences in Edinburgh. The service is top notch. The waiter was incredibly attentive and engaging. The waiter made our meal very fun. My only complaint is that he got my son hooked on Irn-Bru (and we came here for breakfast). We had the English breakfast, the Scottish Breakfast, and the salmon and scrambled eggs and all three were perfect. This was the best Scottish breakfast that I had in Scotland and I had one of these almost every day while here. The prices were amazing considering the service and quality. The service is what makes this place special. I was also incredibly impressed with the respect that the cook and waiter showed toward each other. These guys are True professionals and gentlemen.
Great Breakfast. Would definitely recommend the Scottish Breakfast and the French Toast. Very good latte. Fast service, friendly staff. Nice tables out front if the weather permits.
Very nice food, also very nice location. The oysters and also other seafood is very fresh and there's a broad choice in the menu.

Very nice place indeed!  Food was good, like a fish tapas place.  Only concern was the price, if you are hungry avoid this place. If you want have a good time and order a few dishes to for a feel good lunch or dinner go for it

Very good food. Enjoyed it very much. Service was friendly and very attentive. Prices are a bit high. If you come hungry definitely order the full house and some small plates. Salt and Pepe fries were awesome.

We stopped by to see if we could have dinner here due to the high yelp rating. We walked in and were half ignored for a few minutes. Finally, someone spoke with us and asked if we had a reservation, the answer was no and they went on their way. A few minutes later after we asked how long would it be again they went away and then came back and said if we wanted to wait over 2hrs they might be able to get us in before they close. There were seats at the front bar open and a seperate table at the front bar open, we asked if we could sit there and were told the empty table was reserved and we could not sit at the bar as that's for waiting customers to have a drink until their table was ready. We explained we were waiting customers and they would not allow us to sit. Two other people were seated their eating dinner and drinking. After that they just didn't acknowledge we were there so we left. All three of us independently thought that they acted very rudely, apparently don't want our money and a 1 star was in order. We walked past about an hour later to find the table at the front still open and chairs at the bar still open. I guess they have a right to refuse service and we have a right to write a review. I would suggest not wasting your time here unless you have a reservation.

I didn't know that artisan marshmallows were even a thing, let alone something that could sustain an entire shop before The Marshmallow Lady.  I've bumped into this business at a few markets here and there over the past year but never thought too much of it, because i'm not a huge marshmallow fan (I know, i'm a monster). I didn't really understand why you might NEED an entire bag of marshmallows - do you just eat them like crisps at home? Or would I need to start harbouring a strong s'more addiction?   And then winter rolled around...  With hot chocolates and the occasional Baileys & coffee making a frequent appearance, artisan marshmallows suddenly made a lot more sense and The Marshmallow Lady's unique selection of flavours allow me to play the hot chocolate mad scientist on particular dreary days. I still can't eat them on their own - it's too much of a pure sugar hit for me - but an eggnog marshmallow in white hot chocolate? Pretty much crack. Christmas crack.  I delight in this so much, that today I bought over 50 marshmallows for an upcoming event to serve as a little extra something to plain old hot chocolate. What solidified my fandom of this store? Those 50 marshmallows cost me about 20 and the folks who helped me out were delightful.  I might not become a regular here, but for any and every occasion that MAY require marshmallows, it will forever be my go-to.

Listen up y'all, imma tell you about my homie the Marshmallow Lady. She will change your life and she will improve your Christmas, and here's how.  Do you know what Secret Santa is? Do you have to do it with family members that you hardly know? Did you scramble to think of anything you know about them and come up with, "Well, they eat food, and I've seen them pick up a cup of tea every now and again..."   Bazinga! Get them some dang fancy-ass hot cocoa. And then scoot yer butt on down to the Marshmallow Lady and goggle all her wares, everything from mulled wine flavor to classic vanilla to chocolate to PEANUT BUTTER. Some of them you can get in cute little perfect-gift-size packages at a steal for 2 for 6, because let's face it, where else can you get ballin', homemade, artisan marshmallows in Edinburgh?!  Now that I've changed your life let me tell you how I know that the Marshmallow Lady is on point: it was thanks to ONE of her marshmallows, one gifted to me in what should've been an obvious coupling with a packet of hot cocoa. This silly marshmallow novice thought instead that it was a Turkish Delight. When I bit into like the godless heathen that I am my mind and tastebuds blew into a million tiny delighted pieces. It was seriously so good that I left that same day to purchase more as gifts, ready to spread the love. So, you make of that what you will, folks!  If you do manage to make the trek to the Good Lady's abode, then you should definitely treat yourself to a snack or a cuppa while there. Despite the small size of the place that simultaneously functions as a cafe and marshmallow laboratory there are a few seats available for a quick respite, and what better way to test the marshmallowy waters? You certainly can't trust my word alone, so go forth, for science!  My only word of caution would be to vegans and vegetarians, as the marshmallows do contain gelatin as all good marshmallows do. It would be stellar if the Marshmallow Lady came up with a non-gelatinous version, but until then I'm not-so-secretly bending my own rules a wee bit because... THEY'RE DAMN GOOD!

Point the first: the shop is a working shop devoted to marshmallows and also stocking the finest in local artisan confectionery (Pinnies & Poppyseeds shortcake, Edward & Irwyn chocolate) - no longer any cafe element to it. Kitchen visible. Packaging stacked neatly on the shelves. Icing sugar tramped charmingly from till to window over the otherwise pristine shop floor. Point the second: it's vintage and cutesy without being kitsch or saccharine. The colours are very slightly brighter and more vibrant than the oh-so-trendy macaron/candyfloss shades you're seeing everywhere at the moment. Point the third: They have a framed picture of Mr StayPuft. Point the fourth: Sean, aka Mr Toontrait, the chirpy fun chappy who served me, seemed to be 100% in love with the shop and I could have stuck around chatting about marshmallows and his illustrations (he did the logo) for hours. Point the fifth: those marshmallows though. UNFFFFF. Uh. May. ZING.

I confess; I haven't visited the Marshmallow Lady. But I just had to write a review because I have tried her wonderful, dreamy sugar-puffs of heaven. All those other marshmallows you've had...Those aren't marshmallows! THESE are marshmallows. Believe me, you're going to want to buy packs for all your sweet-toothed friends just to see their faces when they taste these perfect light and fluffy squares and take a one-way ticket to sweet, sweet mallow heaven.   Thank you to Brown & Co delicatessen in Bridge of Allan for stocking such a delicious  product. Of course, I want to share the joy of these sweet heaven-sent bouncy mallow-pillows with everyone. But I also want to keep them all to myself. Such is the yum of the Marshmallow Lady's produce, and what a predicament to be in!  I want to try all the flavours and I want to visit the fine Lady herself.   Marshmallow Lady, I commend you. Keep working your mallow-magic and I'll forever be a fan!

Read the recommendation and decided to come find this place. It's a little bit far away from the centre, but it is well worth the walking. Rose marshmallow is too sweet for me but the raspberry and lemon ones are really good! Roasted marshmallow milkshake is good to try as well. Bought the Jack & Daniel's flavour (yep, they have this wonderful flavour here) as well, looking forwards to trying it :D
Great little shop and cafe. They do scrumptious toasted marshmallow milkshakes, just choose the  flavour youd like!. They  have beer marshmallows too! Nice for gifts too & not expensive.

Have passed by this unassuming cafe so many times and finally got around to popping in. Great selection of organic teas and some groceries too.  Friend had their organic earl grey and we both have freshly made fruit smoothies.  I'd definitely go back for another. Didn't have food but whatever they were cooking smelled great. Sadly though the open kitchen meant I came away smelling of food too though for the rest of the day.

I have to knock one star of this wonderful cafe simply because it isn't as cheap as I'd first thought. The guy who served me on my first visit must have been feeling particularly generous or he was new. - He gave me more salad for a much cheaper price.   I've now learnt that the salad prices are similar to anywhere else in the area. - I'll still visit just not as often as I'd like!

I am on a quest in Edinburgh to find the best scones around. The sheer size of the scones at Papii is exactly what drew me in.  Overall, this was a decent scone. Decent price, came with a huge serving of clotted cream and jam.  On a side note, highly recommend the iced tea for those rare Scottish summer days.

Waffles as big as your head (bigger than some), pretty cakes, warm and cosy setting. This is a central cafe of which the clientele are both tourists and locals.   The seating is a little awkward. My friend and I awkwardly have a "I am more polite than you battle" waiting to sit down, who takes the comfortable seat with a back rest or who puts up with the stool?  We both opted for soya cappuccino... and counteracted the dairy free goodness with those massive waffles. I can't remember the exact price, between 5-6. It seemed steep but the portion size was more than decent. We could have easily shared one! I got a maple syrup and strawberry waffle whilst my friend took one with cream, banana and honey.
