Upstairs, the food is probably the best you can get in an Edinburgh pub. With their recently updated menu you can now add a duck and orange salad to the traditional steak pies, fidget pie and excellent burgers and fish and chips. The starters are much better than you would expect from normal pub food, with the best being the fish cakes and the salmon wrapped around cucumber. A starter and a main with a beer or two will cost you less than 20 a head which is pretty reasonable when you bear in mind the quality of the food.  And that's still not all; their beer garden is surrounded by the rest of the pub so you aren't distracted by outside noise when supping. On Wednesdays there is a pub quiz which is always good fun, and you can win about 30 to 50 depending on how many groups are taking part. As well as this they have the only remaining Victorian skittle alley, which can be rented out for parties and is a great way for a group to spend an evening. An extra incentive to come to what is already one of the best pubs in Edinburgh.  And that's all.

It claims to be the oldest pub in Scotland.   It has a wooden skittle alley.   These are the two reasons I went searching for this pub. And as I walked past Arthur's Seat, admiring the view I was quite sceptical about this place, I heard it was great, I heard it had one of the best selections of ales in the city and even offered brilliant tasting food!   Imagine a pub offering great food!   And did these expectations all live up to the hype? Well, yes they did. The bar is quite traditional inside, with a warm, cosy atmosphere. The ales on offer were all very tempting, and were very reasonably priced. The food as well was not expensive, and the Sheep's Heid menu had an extensive menu for a traditional bar. The beer garden outside looked very nice, slightly too cold for me to use that day, but during the summer it must be great! It also has pub quizzes and live music most weeks!   The aura of being in Scotland's oldest pub adds to your own experience of visiting this place. Go on, step back in time and visit Scotland's oldest pub!

Without question the best place in all of Scotland to get Haggis.  Period.  I liked to take a long walk over Arthur's Seat and then stroll in and have a nice filling lunch before making my way back home.  Being Edinburgh's oldest pub, this place is a must visit.

How have I not reviewed this yet?!?!  This is a strong contender for our favorite fish & chips in Edinburgh.  We park on the east side of Holyrood Park, follow Queen's Drive to the south, then walk down the hill path to Duddingston and you're right there at Sheep's Heid.  If you make that stroll, then you feel you've earned at least part of your supper.  ("Heed, pants, now!"  Does anyone else like "So I Married an Axe Murderer?  That's how you pronounce "heid.")    The haggis stack of mash, neeps and haggis was just perfect -- great seasonings & textures.  Fish & chips were crisp, hot and tasty.     Great atmosphere as well:  perfect place to bring those picky out of town guests looking for authentic.  Don't forget to bowl.

This is quintessential Scottish pub at it's best. It's amazing, there's no other way of putting it.  Edinburgh is a funny place, because although it is a huge city, you never actually feel like you're in a city. Probably because there's a great big bloody hill in the middle of it, but still. But if the city ever gets too much, I always go to the Sheep's Heid. It is about 25minutes from the city centre but you could be on a remote island in the middle of the North Sea.  It has such a great atmosphere, and has brilliant live music every week.

A great place to spend a whole afternoon!!   As Edinburgh's oldest pub it has atmosphere in spades and aa ghostly legend to boot!   Fantastic for food, great pub quiz nights to test you!!   All in a fantastic local!   Ess

Love place vegetarian haggis is yummi well worth the visit.   Book at the weekend tho cause it is very busy.   Was going to write about the history but the other qypers beat me to it.   I enjoy myself a lot the only reason its not 5/5 is because of slow service, I think they need more staff but the ones there are nice and pleasant.

It is said to be the oldest surviving public house in Edinburgh possibly dating as far back as 1360. An Olde Worlde Pub decorated throughout with old photographs, pictures, maps and other things. Located on the South East corner of Holyrood park, great wee place to visit for a pint after a walk around the park or on arthurs seat. Serves traditional pub grub and has a wee beer garden which serves a Barbeque at weekends throughout the summer months. (weather permitting of course.)

This is one of the most atmospheric and charming places that you could drink a beer or two in Edinburgh.   Tucked away on the furthest from town side of Arthur's Seat, it's nestled in the heart of Duddingston Village which is worth a look just for its quaint cobbled streets and rose-lined (in summer) stone houses.   The pub is old. I'm not exactly sure how old. But old. Even by Edinburgh's (old) standards. And inside, it's twisty turny enough, cosy enough, low ceilinged enough to win over the most cynical of olde worlde pub goers. And they have satisfyingly crackling log fires to keep you snug in the dead of frosty winter.   In the summer, they fling the doors wide and turn the back yard into a barbeque venue, chock full of Findlay's finest sausages and burgers a succulent plenty.   They have a great selection of beers, wines, spirits, ciders, sure to keep the fussiest drinker happy. And their food is good honest reliable pub grub at its best.   For those with a short attention span who are less enamoured with their co-drinkers chat, they have a real old-fashioned wooden ten pin bowling alley tucked away at the back of the pub. The only shock horror moment comes when you realise the pins dammit won't reset themselves   This is British pubdom at its best. So earn the reward by taking a turn through Holyrood Park on a brisk autumn / winter / summer day with the Sheep's Heid as your destination. I would be surprised if you regretted it.

If its a sunny weekend with no plans or cares in the world, this is always a favourite way to spend the afternoon. Head down to The Sheep Heid on foot along the road at Duddingston Loch to the village and get some barbecue in you (take some bread for the ducks and swans)!   The barbecue foods your basic pub-grub, their burgers can be a little on the small side and their fancy sausages can come out dry but who cares when you've got a whimsical olde covered beer garden to sun out in, behind a truly British ale pub. Get some local draught for your troubles and make sure its on the cold side!   Never been to the restaurant there but next time we're there for barbecue we may just end up staying for the evening. This is a real day-out pub.

This is a well known and visited little pub.  The decor is kitschy, yet adds to the flavour.  The food is truly worth the price, and one can visit after hiking Arthur's Seat.  It is hard to get to for people who don't know the area via public transport, without a car, or the invalid.  That is a drawback.  But, recommended.  They have a great selection of whiskies.

neat old pub! great place to bring a visitor to scotland, full of history and authenticity. Also fun to take a bike there (on a nice day) or a bus, which gives you a little tour of the south part of the city. It's a pub that gets you out of the hustle bustle for you to enjoy your pint.

A favourite location and bar/restaurant of mine. Went along for lunch today as its been a while and just loved it. The food is great and so fresh. Great setting and a really nice experience. There wasn't one thing on the menu that didn't sound delicious. Keep up the great work.

It's the oldest pub in Edinburgh! Definitely worth checking out!  It's kind of out of the way but it's definitely a nice way to treat oneself after a few hours on Arthur's Seat.  Honestly, we just went because we heard it was the oldest pub in Edinburgh/Scotland (?). We didn't try any food so I can't comment on that. The bartenders were friendly though!

Somehow I've lived in Edinburgh for 8 years without ever venturing to The Sheep Heid Inn before, mostly because I don't have a car. However, this week, with the two siblings with whom I share a car back in Glasgow both being on holiday, I had unrestricted use of the Clio so it was brought through to Edinburgh and I've basically been driving everywhere to get some practice.  Yesterday we went for a lovely drive round Arthur's Seat and ended up in Duddingston. Finally making it here, after so many years, it seemed silly not to pop by The Sheep Heid for a drink.  Obviously, being the driver, I wasn't able to sample anything more exciting than a diet Pepsi, but my sister and boyfriend both opted for the more unusually named offers on draught - Mad Goose and Shark Bite (or something Shark anyway). The former was delicious - not too hoppy but with enough of a flavour to give it some body - but the latter was a little disappointing (or at least the small sip of it I had was). I love a cool, light and refreshing lager, but this Pilsner was a bit meh. Maybe the rest of the pint was better, as I didn't hear any complaints.  The inside was busy, as we'd arrived bang on teatime, but the outside courtyard is pleasant with wrought-iron tables and chairs and a covered area with comfier seats (useful when it started to rain!).  The interior looked very nice though, in keeping with its oldest pub in Scotland tag. On that, by the way, it's worth noting that whilst there has apparently been a pub of sorts on the premise since 1360, the present building is much newer (though still about 200 years old).  We didn't eat, but the food looked and smelled okay. I was a bit perplexed by the prices though - the starters and desserts were on the cheaper end (3/4) but the mains were distinctly averagely priced (9/11).  Maybe it deserves 4 stars, but it's hard to tell at the moment. They didn't have a great selection on draught (or at least, not a great selection of anything interesting) and whilst the inside is nice, it's nothing massively special when you consider other Scottish pubs in Edinburgh.  It is nice though, and would be treat to reward yourself with at the end of a walk or drive through the park. I'll be back I imagine (mostly cos I want to try the 19th century skittles alley!), but I won't be hurrying here.

Set in the very historial location of Duddingston Village, The Sheep Heid's Inn  has had a revamp of late and looks like it has a boost of much needed TLC.  We were only stopping by for a wee tipple for Mr C's birthday but the menu looked nice and i would like to give it a try soon.  I love the cosiness of the place and could quite happily curl in a corner for hours here.

I'd heard quite a bit about the Sheeps Heid Inn, mostly very positive, so it seemed like the natural place to stop after a day wandering the Lothian countryside.   The pub has a decent bar, but we were in to eat so grabbed a table in one if the dining areas.  We were served with a smile and chose the fish and chips and a goats cheese salad which arrived about 10 minutes later.  I have to say I thought the food was fairly average.  The fish seemed heavy with fat, and the goats cheese salad lacked imagination - a handful of green leaves with a lump of goat's cheese dumped on top.    Just a small improvement wih the food would see this place elevated to 'real gem' status and make it worth the trek out of town to visit.  On this evidence they've got a bit to go though so I'd pop in for a passing pint but there are better eateries closer to home.

I have come here several times now, and must say I really like it.  Having lived most of my life in the countryside, going to a cosy pub or cafe was the reward at the end of a long walk. Edinburgh is great at providing instant satisfaction, but sometimes it's nice to go through the ordeal of facing the elements, in exchange for a nice reward.   Most times I have been to the Sheep Heid Inn, I have really come face to face with the Scottish weather. To get to Duddington, one must walk around the foot of arthur's seat, a passage, a path that is often blasted with gail force winds which feel like continuous slaps across the face, made even more severe by the hail, drizzle, or whatever else Scotland feels like throwing at you. Aside from this, it's a pleasant walk. Arthur's seat is beautiful, and you will see the loch at Duddingston before actually reaching the village.  I advise you to walk a little around the cobblestone streets before entering the pub. There's a cute little church overlooking the loch, which is itself quite a stage to the spectacle of elegant swans. You may think you just stepped into Hogsmeade? Not so far off. Apparently this little village influenced even J.K.Rowling.  The pub prides itself in being the oldest in Scotland. Inside, it does feel a little more modern than one might expect, but it still retains a certain charm. Arriving after a wee walk in the cold is a massive relief. Though the quality of the drinks is great, they are a bit pricier here than elsewhere. I have had some good cider and gin and tonics here over the years, and came here for New Years eve for two years running. There's a skittles alley, a VERY difficult pub quiz, and a area reserved to dining upstairs.  I am yet to try the food, but it looks very good went put out on the plate!

This. Place. Is. Amazing. It claims to be Scotland's oldest pub, and it's easy to see why it's still in business since 1360.  This place is just far enough out of the city centre that you can justify spending a whole afternoon or evening there, but close enough that almost everyone you ask will know about it or have been at least once.  From the outside, it looks just like any given old man's pub, serving real ales and home-cooked food. Nothing surprising so far. But when you get inside the place has a surprisingly young and laid back crowd, with an atmosphere to match.  The food is way better than you'd expect in most pubs, although it is slightly pricer. For your money though, you get decent-sized portions and according to the menu certain ingredients like the sausages are sourced locally, so you can feel proud of yourself for helping out local farmers/butchers in the process of stuffing your face with bangers and mash.  I'm not a real ale drinker, in fact I'm about as far in the opposite direction as you can go, and there's definitely a good range of spirits and wines to cater for the likes of me. They stock ginger beer to go with my gin for a start, instead of watery ginger ale that a lot of places have.   But saving the best 'til last... they still have the original Victorian skittles alley out the back which you can hire out. Most pubs are doing well with a pool table or an it-box, but this definitely trumps a dartboard and I'd highly recommend it.

This review is for the pub only. I haven't eaten at the restaurant.  I'd like to give 3.5 but if forced to round up or down, 3 stars it is. I went here with high expectations after having it built up for me by guidebooks and reviews, but it was just a pub to me. Lovely decor, and we managed to snag a couple of comfy chairs (although it was tight on a Sunday afternoon!), but the ale selection was not out of the ordinary, and the whole experience wasn't anything special. They do make lovely chips though.  I would like to go back to eat, and I'll probably stop in again the next time I'm walking to or from Craigmillar Castle. This is a perfectly nice pub -- just not amazing.

Have you wanted to get out of the City but you don't have a car and can't be bothered with buses? Head towards the famous "hill" of Edinburgh, Arthurs Seat. You can climb it if you want- it does have spectacular views from the top and provides the feeling of self accomplishment. However you can also walk around it and head towards the village of Duddingston. There are a variety of routes to reach the village, either following the road , from which you will get to see Duddingston Loch, or under via the Innocent Cycle Path or even over Arthur's Seat. Once you arrive at the village head towards the famous Sheep's Heid Inn- the "oldest public House of Scotland" (from 1360!). It was thought to be the stopping place for travellers and royalty going between Holyrood and Craigmillar Castle. Here you will find a good selection of beers and ales and other drinks (much needed after the walk) as well as food. The pub is like a treasure trove, with various memorabilia left from previous visitors-so take your time to have a look around(I surely did), as well as board games you are welcome to use. There is also a cute beer garden in the back if you are lucky with the weather, and do not miss out on taking a look at the old skittle alley- ask a member of staff to let you in if you can't find it. Skittles is like an early form of bowling and the Inn is quite popular for it, so it is usually hard to book a slot. There is a large variety of food to choose from, from tourist favourites of haggis and other Scottish delicacies to lighter options. On Sunday's there is also a roast which tends to get quite popular (call to book in advance!) and around spring and the summer there are various barbeques and beer festivals (check their website for more details: sheepheid.co.uk/history....). Prices are on the verge of affordable, but one is really visiting this place for its ambience. I always take visiting friends here as a sort of "outing". Although the food can be quite stodgy and heavy I would highly recommend this place to any visitor or resident of Edinburgh who wants to let go of the city and get a feel of an "authentic" pub-a cosy place whatever the weather may be!

After debating whether this pub was called the sheeps head OR the sheeps heed, a friend and I trekked past Arthur's seat to go find out! It's a beautiful walk up there in good weather, but definitely out of the way if one's situated in Edinburgh city centre.  It has the cosy feeling that many Edinburgh pubs have, but seemed much lighter, probably due to the sunny day and after ordering our drinks, we made our way to the back where there's a really pleasant outdoor seating area. There was a little drama over our orders, as not that many  bartenders are accustomed to mixing Guinness with coke!   The most surprising aspect of the trip was how large and modern the bathrooms our; they would do any hotel proud! If the Sheepsheid was a little bit closer, I'd probably visit more often!

Sheep Heid has location, location, location. Duddingston is a lovely wee part of Edinburgh, and for those on the tourist trail (and locals, who are not), The Sheep Heid Inn offers more than most. However, Sundays are mental crazy busy - too much for me. We took the parents here, and were crammed into a corner for Sunday lunch. The various meals we had... none of us really got that excited about them - lacking in flavour and generally just... meh. I wouldn't rush back to be honest, it's definitely for me, style over substance but perhaps on a quieter night I would have a different impression.

It's good. Not world-beating but reliably good. It's a bit pricey and it can get very busy. It amounts to glitzed up gastro pub but the atmosphere is rather homey and lovely and its location makes it almost the only game in town. I really love the fish and chips and they do cater for vegetarians with more than just the usual suspects. My husband had the veg haggis with neeps and tatties and loved it. The draught beer is always excellent and the beer garden is nice in warmer weather. I love the skittles hall and generally the walk there after a trot around Dr Neill's Gardens or Holyrood Park is the perfect Sunday but you should book. It's super busy on a Sunday because everyone had the same idea.

Stopped by on a Sunday afternoon after a gorgeous walk up and over Arthur's Seat.  The place was packed, even as it was well past lunch time. Nevertheless their staff were polite and accommodating. It seems rare these days to find a pub that can serve so many people professionally without being flustered.   The fish and chips was quite good, the Sunday roast was significantly better than we would have expected, and the beer selection was ample.  The food isn't 5 star, but it is very good for a pub and considering the location, the atmosphere, the staff, and the lovely afternoon we had there I can't give it less than 5 stars.  So make a day of it: climb Arthur's Seat, enjoy the views, dine at the Sheep Heid, and walk off the Sticky Toffee Pudding as you wind your way back to Edinburgh.  Oh, and while I'm not sure this would be True every day, last Sunday the background music selection was perfect for fans of pop music between 1994 and 1996.

I've always really enjoyed a trip to the Sheep Heid, especially after a walk up Arthur's Seat.  What is it about walking that makes you really want a beer? Is it a UK thing, or a Scottish thing?  Is it because you've just done something healthy, you must counteract it?   And man does that beer taste good after a long walk.  It makes me want to go walking this weekend so I can tuck into a few well deserved pints.    Anyway .... I have always really enjoyed coming here for pints.  The best bit, in my opinion, is in the summer when they have the BBQ on.  They even have amazing beer festivals here and when you combine beer festival with BBQ and sun, you have my perfect weekend.    My guy and I are house hunting at the moment and last weekend I looked at a house about 8 minutes walk from here.  My guy wasn't too keen on the house itself and I was like "but then we would live withing really really close walking distance to the Sheep Heid and the beer and the barbeque and the beer and the beer!!!"  He was not convinced that my argument was strong enough to buy a house there.  Pff.    The only downside is the tourist trade.  Dastardly tourists take up lots of space in this place, but at least they have good taste.

I love this place. Officially the oldest pub in Scotland!  After a long post Christmas walk up and around Arthur's seat we needed some grub. We had visited the Sheep's Heid before so we knew we would get something good.   Nestled down a cobbled street in Duddingston, The Sheep's Heid is the cutest Inn you ever did see. Inside is super cosy and welcoming. We walk into the bar and the friendly staff show us to a table in the back. This pub looks small but it can hold quite a few tables!  The lighting is dim and the chairs are super comfy, after a couple of pints you could easily drift off into a slumber. We look at the menu and David does his usual and goes for the burger. I decide upon the seabass. The food doesn't take long and we are soon tucking in.   My seabass is beautifully cooked and came with delicious vegetables and dressing. David's burger must have been good as he seemed to inhale it! We are both too full for a dessert even though they do sound amazing.  Lunch cost about 30 but that was with a drink each as well, not bad at all. A great place to bring the family to or just hanging out on a Sunday. I am desperate to try their Sunday roast!  If you have the energy afterwards you can play a game of proper old fashioned skittles, they have an alley in the back. Just ask the guys at the bar.  A definite winner for me!  Cheers, Amy

A good pub, part of the same chain as the Salisbury Arms, Greyfriars Bobby, and various other Edinburgh staples, with lovely atmosphere, but more mixed food and service.  I've been going to the Sheep Heid on and off for 10-12 years now.  It's a lovely, charming venue and it's a fun place to show off when I've got guests visiting Edinburgh.  There's good beer on tap as well.  Over time, I do feel that there's been a gradual but increasingly noticeable decline in the quality of the food and service.  It's basically 20-25 a head for a main and a drink, and other places in the same bracket (e.g. Spoon, the Outsider) have much more interesting, better quality options.  The food isn't bad per se, just kind of standard meals at a high price, kind of like an airport pub.  There's lots of choice from various international options to traditional pub fare.  In fact, I wonder if having too much choice is part of the problem - it's a really big menu, and perhaps a narrower set of options would allow a focus on either a) some really impressive high quality options or b) the current stuff at a more reasonable price.  Service is fair to middling.
Glad we tried the oldest pub in Scotland (I think?). Drink choices were good and I like that it's hidden away a bit and doesn't feel touristy.
Great atmosphere but small. They have an awesome burger that if your American, like me, you will love it! All the drink are awesome also!

Following the steps of Her Majesty the Queen we paid a visit to the renowned Sheep Heid Inn. We booked for 4 people at 1:30pm, the table was waiting for us upon arrival and we're welcomed by friendly front of house Kelsie. The place was rather busy as all tables were pre-booked. We ordered some drinks (alcohol free beers, Caesar Augustus ale and some orange juice) As per starters we had two soups of the day, Stilton & Mushroom with artisan rustic bread & butter, Salt & Szechuan Pepper Squid followed by Cod & chips, Wagyu Burger with extra bacon, child portion Fish Goujon and a Duck Salad as mains.  And here's when all kicked off... we were served by a tall dude who looked spaced out/in the zone and by waitress Kelsie & a bearded waiter as a back-up... Tall Dude took the drink orders, but they never arrived...until we re-asked to Bearded Waiter and ...voila drinks arrived in 1 minute... After a 25 minutes wait our starters arrived; the Stilton & Mushroom soups were a terrible disappointment as they did not taste of Stilton or mushrooms either, they were certainly not creamy and they looked more like some green over diluted salty stock...or dirty warm water... To top it up, Tall Dude got catering lesson 1.0.1 wrong as he did not do the mise-en-place...AKA forgot to bring spoons....we asked him for them to no avail so I started to drink it from the bowl, camping style... when we got the attention of Bearded Waiter we got the spoons in a second... After finishing our almost edible starters, we ordered a second round of drinks to Tall Dude; who of course did not deliver...after 5 minutes we got Kelsie and she brought our drinks in a good timely fashion, thank goodness. After a long wait for our mains, Tall Dude appeared with all our mains; but guess what ... catering lesson 1.0.2 was missed too as he forgot to clear the empty bowls & plates from the starters to make room...anyhow... My mate's Cod & Chips was a 5/10 experience while my Wagyu Burger was good enough; so it was the Duck Salad (7/10). Pros: Kelsie & Bearded Waiter, the atmosphere, the pub interiors. Cons: the food & the Tall Dude appalling non-existent service. Plenty room for improvement as you may guess...but it won't be me testing if that happen (or not)... any time soon....

Worth the journey!  We read about Sheeps Heid in our lonely planet guidebook: the oldest existing inn/pub in Edinburgh.  Tucked away behind Arthur's seat, on a house lined street that looks like it's an ancient little town of its own, is a precious gem serving contemporary gastropub fare along with some simple but interesting cocktails I've never heard of.  If you love atmosphere, you'll forgive the slant in the floor of the dining room and the slender pickings at the bar and just enjoy soaking up the vibes of what's been a travellers waystation for several centuries.

Pretty mediocre Sunday roast. No lamb option. The chicken was immediately forgettable. The beef was over cooked. The potatoes were under cooked. The cabbage was starting to turn.   Maybe they hated me because I tried to order custard and was told there was no custard. Then someone in my group ordered custard. Dude, I'm going to find out because we are literally sitting next to each other. Totally not cool.

This is such a cool place! Not only is it Edinburgh's oldest pub which makes it great in itself, but it is set in a lovely location, being in Duddingston Village and close to Arthurs Seat. It's good to go to on sunny or rainy days. I love the atmosphere in this pub. When I went I was able to grab a seat in the beer garden, before it became really busy, and was able enjoy the sun (yes sun in Edinburgh). Then myself and a friend went inside to have some good food. I don't think you're allowed to have food out in the beer garden, though there is a small balcony area upstairs where it looked like you can have food. There's a good mix of clientele from families to groups of friends out for a few drinks. They had a guy singing in the beer garden yesterday which was a nice touch. He did covers of what I consider to be chilled out songs which suited the atmosphere of the place.   There is also the skittles alley which I've yet to try, but I've heard great things about it so it's definitely on my list of things to do. Great pub!

The Sheep Heid is our local so we've been in quite a few times & it's a lovely little gastro pub, with a good atmosphere & above average food.  During the week it's great for an after-work drink & after a couple of glasses of wine I'll inevitably crack & order the scallops which are delicious. There's also a great mix of people with local mingling with tourists who've just finished climbing Arthur's Seat.  However, over the weekend it becomes a bit of a nightmare. It ends up being packed & even when we've booked ahead for dinner or lunch, we've been sat in a cramped corner surrounded by people, which doesn't exactly make for a great dining experience. We also found the Sunday lunch to be pretty disappointing considering the overall good quality of the food.  Overall, I'd definitely recommend a trip to the Sheep Heid whether you're a visitor or an Edinburgh local, but avoid the weekend!

This place is the perfect country pub - but you don't have to drive out to the country. Very cosy with great staff (though maybe a bit mental). Always got a couple great Real Ales. Good bar menu, we had the steak frites and the burger, both were great value for money. freshly ground coffees also, and we shared a chocolate brownie, BOOM! This is what pub lunches are all about, don't look anywhere else.  Also, don't forget, beer garden, beer festival, separate restaurant, child and dog friendly, skittle alley.... I HEART The Sheep Heid!!

I know that no Greggs is different from any other but this one is pretty posh! It is Edinburgh's newest Greggs so it still looks shiny and new and the staff were very fast considering how busy the shop was.  There are about 30 seats in the main cafe area and then a few benches in the counter area. There were plenty of clean tables and we didn't have to clear anything away from our booth.  I had 2 sausage rolls, a packet of Walkers ready salted crisps and a Capri Sun. It may be very unhealthy but it is tasty and cheap and that is all that matters.  I went to the toilets before I left which were clean enough but could have been better.  There is a huge stained glass ceiling in the ordering area which really adds character to the building. The high ceilings also help make it bright and airy.

The Devil's Advocate was recommended to us as a great place to grab a drink after dinner.  We stopped in for a few pints and the bartenders were very friendly.   There isn't much seating, so we just hung out by the bar which worked out perfectly. They also serve food here however we did not indulge.    The atmosphere was a bit chic, low lighting etc which was enjoyable.  After a few pints we were on our way back home.   I would like to come back and try some of the food as it seems like it would be quite enjoyable.

Love this place! It's got a great feel - lots of wood and stone. The cocktail list is superb and they have a good selection of beers as well.   I ordered Jerusalem Artichoke soup and it was to die for. Pure deliciousness. Also had a side of roasted seasonal vegetables and they were divine.   This place seems to be pretty popular, so I recommend booking a reservation in advance.

There is a reason Devil's Advocate has such good Yelp reviews. This place is cute, cool, kind of hidden and has a really nice ambiance and menu. The booths in little hidden alcoves makes having intimate conversation with friends much easier and the darker mood lighting is a nice touch.   I came here with some friends for a girls night with food and drinks. The drink menu is pretty eclectic and has some really interesting options. The server had some good off-menu suggestions and everything we had was very good. One thing we did notice though is that the drink/price ratio is pretty bad. All our drinks came in tiny, fancy cocktail glasses of various forms. While adorable, this makes for about three sips before your drink is gone and you are looking around for another. The food was similarly good and eclectic, but small portions that were hard to share and didnt go far.   Aside from the cost ratio, the only other real downside I see to DA is that service wasnt always the fastest. We waited for drinks a lot via table service, which seemed silly when we were three steps from the bar. The food came out pretty quickly, but it you wanted to get your server's attention for anything they were difficult to track down. Same deal with getting and paying the bill.   Overall a nice place, great drinks, food and ambiance. Will definitely return, just dont be in a rush and be prepared to lay down some cash.

Unfortunately, we were not able to get in for dinner as they book up days in advance, but stopped in for a couple drinks. The atmosphere and decor is simply amazing. It feels like you've stepped back in time a couple hundred years. Also, the cocktails are divine. Try the Rose on St. James. We will definitely be back for dinner next time we are in Edinburgh.

This place is annoyingly hipster, and the waitstaff are all too cool to smile or be friendly, but the food and atmosphere are so so good. I had the duck leg confit and my husband had the ox cheek and both were cooked perfectly and delicious to the last bite. It was one of the best meals we had the entire time we were in Edinburgh.

They hosted an amazing yelp party, and the place is gorgeous. I will have to say because of the amazing yelp people, the yelp cake, and endless prosecco my review is a bit out of the ordinary. But the bartenders were cute and quick, the ambience was candlelight,  perfect for a romantic night out. And it was romantic!

Cool new bar down Advocates Close!! I love the look and feel of the place. It looks like it has lots of potential so I'll look forward to going back again on a weekend night, or day. An exciting new bar to go to in the Old Town. From the sounds of it they're going to be opening up mega early for breakfast so I'll have to try it sometime.

Incredible, absolutely my favorite restaraunt we visited while in Edinburgh. Great service, awesome drinks and even BETTER food!! Located off of Advocate's Close down the Royal Mile, we stumbled upon this place while walking to new town. They bar area is large with plenty of room to stand either at the bar while waiting or at a smaller high top. Very cool selection of house cocktails and the bartenders seemed to be able to whip different things up off the top of their heads as well!!   We were seated on the ground floor in a somewhat private booth. 3 of us split a charcuterie board of excellent selections of meats and cheeses and oil. I got the pan roasted pork chop with chorizo and sweet potato puree and it was by far one of the best meals I've had in months. Everything on their menu looked and smelled incredible from what we saw. I will 100% be returning to this place when we return!!
Great place to have drinks or a dinner. Reservation highly recommended (or go early). Very popular restaurant. Great food and great service. High recommended

Most expensive restaurant I went to when I visited Edinburgh, but also the most delicious!   The restaurant has a lively ambiance, almost noisy. It's also really dim inside, but I suppose that enhances the vibe. They are well known for their drinks, so definitely order one (or two) at the bar.   I ordered the chicken pasta and it was just divine. The truffle oil was the best part of it.   For dessert, I got a whiskey sour sorbet with poached pear. Hands down the best sorbet I've ever had. I also love how it was artfully garnished with white chocolate pieces and raspberries.   Despite my meal costing me a pretty penny, I would absolutely return. The flavorful dishes make it well worth it!

Hmmm....   It's a very well done room, very upmarket hipster. Staff is friendly - with lots of handsome beardy bartenders.  Food is quite good, but doesn't quite manage to transcend to greatness.  Service is generally good if somewhat unfocused - five different servers over the course of our meal - so no bond of hospitality with your server happening here, and they're very busy, so despite what you'll charitably credit as their best efforts, don't expect a lot of love.    Overall a positive experience, but it seems like the kind of place where your table assignment is partly based on simple availability, but you can't help but feel like tables are awarded based on how beautiful you are. Apparently we should be happy that we got a table and accept that we're just not as beautiful as those people who didn't have a reservation but got seated on the patio regardless - if this kind of thing makes you crazy, this is not your place.  If you're looking to be seen in a happening restaurant then you'll love it.

Had the smoked fish platter. Smoked salmon was good but the rest was just ok. Would take something else.  Had the fried haggis; was good but nothing amazing. It had peppers on the side; nothing special.  Had the orzo with goat cheese and peas. By far the best thing we ate! Cocktails were good. Ambiance is nice.

Excellent restaurant food was superb! Had the cod and side of truffle fries and they were unbelievable. Great scotch selection and tasty deserts. This is probably one of the few best meals we had in Edinburgh.

Nice place to get cocktails! Romantic, dimly lit and mysterious. Really loved this vibe. Tucked away in Edinburgh's hills and it has a great bar scene. Nice cocktail list! The only disappointment was that after the waiter gave us the bar menu and when we were ready to order, he came over only to tell us that the kitchen was closed. Wee bit annoying. Wish they didn't give us menu at all if they weren't going to serve us. Still, a great place to come for a drink.

I will remember this restaurant forever! Tucked down a steep alleyway off the Royal Mile, Devil's Advocate has that hole in the wall mystery feel immediately. They have the widest selection of alcohol I have ever seen, and they have some great mixed drinks.  Definitely a good place to go if you want to experiment. The food is solid, but it is now where near as amazing as their drink selection! One of my favorite restaurants I've been to in the UK!

Devil's Advocate "should" be a great little spot for dinner to to dine in with a date. It has great 'tucked away to be found only by the locals' ambience and great beer (I recommend the Dia des los murtes IPA), but the food isn't 5-star and staff are quite capable of making mistakes. The upstairs eating area, although nice, means that staff spend a lot of time not seeing that you need them - particularly given that we gave me the wrong beer originally and I spent several minutes waiting to get it replaced (which they did with no fuss).  Probably the main thing that dragged my experience down though, was the hard sell I got from the guy giving me the bill, given both the less-than-fantastic service I'd received and the fact he'd not himself served me at any point before that exchange! Left with a 2-star taste in my mouth instead of a 3-star.  I'd probably grab a beer here with a couple of friends, and might edit this back up to a 3-star based on that experience, but I don't see myself eating here again when there's at least four better restaurants up the top of Advocate's Close and straight down George IV Bridge a couple minutes, let alone every other direction.
The staff are polite, warm and welcoming. The food is on the pricier side, but mouth watering. Music is a little louder than expected, but perfect for a dinner with a friend

I love The Devil's Advocate - it's tucked in the Advocate's  close in Old Town, and unless you accidentally stumble upon it or know about it, it may remain a hidden gem..  I was there recently for a pre-dinner drink with my husband. The place is not very big - it has a few seats downstairs and a mezzanine area reserved for diners. But it has a cosy atmosphere, great for candle lit chats.   If you want whisky, this is a great place for it as they have over 200 whiskies to choose from. However, we ordered a glass of pinot noir and a gin & tonic (table service). The drinks arrived and I requested a new glass as it looked dirty. They were very apologetic about it and actually deducted the wine from the bill, which was unnecessary but I accepted that.  I would love to try out the food as well so maybe next time it will dinner and drinks!

After a long morning of site seeing, we chose to visit the Devil's Advocate for a late lunch based on its proximity to our hotel, and its reviews.  Wow!  This was maybe the best meal that we had in Scotland with an interesting menu.    The drinks are creative and tasty.  My friend wanted to mix up the fun brand in one of her cocktails for our second round, and they kindly obliged her request, and then returned to check that it was still okay.   I LOVED my sweet potato chili (though my friend found it slightly too spicy) and my specialty salad.  All the ingredients were fresh and created in the perfect flavor combinations.  So delicious!  And our service was fantastic.    I would happily return for another meal!

A tiny haunt tucked into a nondescript alleyway that serves a mean old fashioned? Hell, they had me at the entire shelf of Japanese whisky, the rest was just icing on the cake.  After a colourful (read: boozy) start to our evening, myself and visiting Edmonton CM turned to the ol' Yelp mobile to continue our shenanigans with a few cocktails. Even with a map in front of us, it took three walk bys before we spotted the wee little alley that leads to this wee little cocktail bar. The stairs down (or up, depending on your vantage point) are perhaps the city's best sobriety test. I'm sure the door gents just watch and only allow those who can make it down without looking like they'll pitch to their certain death at any moment. Because of this, I very vocally pointed out the difficulty level of high heels on uneven steps as we teetered down in the rain.  With a quick shake of the umbrella, we stepped into a beautiful gem of a bar. I can't speak for the food, or the seating in general. To be honest - we saw the bar, and happily stayed put for a few rounds, but for that, I can happily speak to the quality of the libations.  It's a long standing tradition that I judge a bar by the oomph of their old fashioned. The Devils Advocate did not disappoint - they served up a beautifully balanced drink, made with care but without the 15 minute show you can get at other "we do good cocktail" joints. It was well made, without the pomp and much appreciated by our little party. But where this spot truly won my heart, was with a brief glance up to an entire shelf dedicated to Japanese spirits. A nice Yamazaki or Nikka is my newest whisky obsession and hailing from Vancouver, where you're lucky to see one or two bottles on the go, the sheer promise of a 5+ range? This lady is a happy camper.  Service was lovely, quick and no bs. The folks milling about the bar are a fun mix of eclectic professionals and the vibe is one that makes you want to pull up a chair and put back a few. I didn't get a chance to ask about their wifi, but seeing as though they open at 9am, I daresay with a good signal, this will fast become a regular "office" soon enough.  Either way, come cocktail hour, I will definitely be back. Afterall, I only tried two whiskies while I was there - more research is definitely needed. Worth getting lost for, and as always, mind the stairs.

I love this place. The staff are so friendly and they let us stand (or sit) at the bar all night on busy Friday evenings. The cocktails are super tasty and it has an overall really friendly atmosphere.  I really have nothing negative to say - maybe the ladies toilets were a bit on the freezing side! haha  The night we were in they had some bartenders visiting from Poland or Norway (sorry I am predictably fuzzy on the details of the night) who allowed us to sample (for free!) some of their cocktail creations.  All in all, excellent tucked away venue, great friendly and knowledgeable service and a delightful atmosphere. Can't wait until I visit again!

Just simply fantastic.  I had the lamb at the suggestion of the host.  It was superb, balanced with a refined mixed salad that complimented the lamb at so many levels!  I ordered an outstanding IPA, also at the recommendation of the bar staff....it was great!  Service was a pleasing balance of relaxed but very professional with no pressure ....   What can I say, this was an evening to remember!!!!

I'll be keeping four stars for now but had a pretty off putting experience here recently.  A few weeks ago, The Man and I popped in for a last drink before home (about 10:30 or 11). We went up to the bar to order, but were quickly whisked to a table instead. This was fine, except that no one told the wait staff that there was a new table waiting to be served and we sat there for about 10 minutes until we were able to flag someone down.  Drinks order placed, drinks received, all in order.    Until our drinks were finished.  We sat with empty glasses for long enough that "let's have one more" turned into "let's just go"  When we were finally able to get the bill, we quickly handed over our money, the bill whisked away, and no change given.   I get that tipping for table service is becoming more of a done thing, especially when getting special drinks like cocktails.  But certainly not for beers, and not when I tried to order at the bar anyway.    With the waitress well and truly disappeared, we had to go to the bar where we were faced with confusion about where the waitress had gone and hadn't we paid "AGES ago" anyway?  Yes we had, we've been waiting for change.   It all left us with a bad taste in our mouths.   I would go back, but for goodness sake just relax and let people order at the bar and we'll be alright.

I called here on a recommendation and it was awesome. We all had starters and a main and they were just perfect. The menu was quite limited (dinner menu) but we each found something that we liked and then loved once it arrived. The cocktail / drinks selection is also superior. Great service, food and it has a gorgeous rustic design inside. Love it. My starter was 4 and main was 13 which was spot on.

Great spot, loved the decor! We sampled a Carver (Bread, Meat, Cheese, Olives & Olive Oil) (Good) and I had the Ribeye (Great and tender) with Shoestring Chips, and my wife had the Chicken (Good). Tasty food in a great, just off the beaten trail, spot!

A real hidden gem - who knew it was possible to get so lost only a stone's throw from the Castle?!   This bar is tucked away on Advocate's Close up some winding steps that made me start thinking my colleagues had given me the wrong address. It has atmosphere by the bucketload, that builds from when you're wandering up the historic old Close, to when you're standing at the beautiful high-ceilinged bar with its rough stone walls that makes you feel like it's been carved into the hillside.  The clipboardful of drinks menus is a treat - several pages of whiskies that I must go back for, and cocktails that intrigue. Our bearded barman took real care over making these, and was a joy to watch and chat to.  My first cocktail was gin-based and enjoyable but it was the second that blew me away - if you're a whisky fan (and don't mind a girly glass) get The Convent. I always try to pick something with a new ingredient for me, and this had creme d'violet, malic acid solution, peat and heather, which all sounded suitably exotic! Oh and Highland Park 12. It was deliciously strong, and felt extra special after they told me it was the last one of the night because they'd run out of the violet stuff. Win!  Front of house staff are also on the ball - most of the tables were busy when we arrived but the lady who first welcomed us kept us in mind when one of these cleared, and explained we could sit until the reservation arrived. So we took a seat up on the mezzanine, at which point the guys promptly got food envy and ordered a couple of ham and cheese platters with bread and oil. Yum.  You probably need to book ahead for food, but it's a new fave to pop in for post-work drinks. Make sure you're not in a rush though, as you'll need time to pull yourself together and choose a drink after admiring the candlelit bar itself... :)

THE GOOD: Neat atmosphere and attentive staff.  Abundant whisky options and several different whisky flights poured high.  Pork chops and Beef Tails were cooked perfectly and presented elegantly. Moist meat and appropriate volume of sauce for flavoring. Many restaurants drown their meal is sauce to cover underlying flaws, no need here as the meat is well selected and prepared.  Decent selection and variety of deserts. The lemon desert provided a light zest on the palate with a creamy texture.  THE BAD: Nothing of mention.  THE UGLY: Nothing of mention.  OVERALL IMPRESSION: If you are in search of a centrally located, appropriately priced restaurant with perfectly prepared dishes and good atmosphere then look no further. I would highly recommend attending. They have a sister restaurant in the "new town" of Edinburgh called El Cartel which is also fantastic (see review).

Restaurant is located in a neat location in the old town of Edinburgh. The building has great character.  The menu is very short but also has the feel of being very fresh.  We had an out of town guest with us, so the Scottish influence on the menu was a great option for him to try lots of local flavours.    Unfortunately we went on a night the owner was hosting a very large dinner adjacent to our table and things got very loud.  Perhaps reasonably so, the staff were more focused on the other dinner than ours.  It led us to feel both ignored then rushed at the same time.   Overall the food was nice, but the atmosphere left us unimpressed.

The brilliant alley to get away from the noise of the city center!! Especially the small balcony makes you feel like you are on vacation somewhere different. However, the place inside is also amazing.  Unfortunately, it is quite expensive..   Furthermore, we had the desserts, which were mousses (one lemon and the other caramelized chocolate) .. aaaand I am not a fan! I would like to have more options...  The four stars go to the environment which was very beautiful and comfortable!
Great ambiance and food. The menu is small but there are interesting options. The best part was the cozy atmosphere. Make sure to make reservations !! Very busy on a Saturday night. Would go again.

I've been to devil's advocate twice now. The first time was part of an impromptu pub crawl, and I thought it was a pretty cool spot. Since then I've been keen to head back here and try out the food.   I had the pea and leek arancini, and my date had the butternut squash salad. I though the salad was pretty tasty, even if I'm not the hugest fan of cold salads when I'm super hungry. The arancini was absolutely scrumptious! A lovely crispy outside, with soft gooey risotto in the middle. Heaven. And definitely what I needed for my second (!!) dinner after yoga with a certain former CM.  My only down point for this place is the very limited desert menu. In fairness, DA is a Gastrobar thing and not an actual restaurant. The kitchen space is probably pretty limited for making a load of deserts.  All in all I really like this bar. I definitely want to try out more of their food, and more of what's behind the bar.

The walk down the crooked narrow street to this wee hideaway bar just as the sun was leaving us for the day was really special and part of the dazzlement of devil's advocate.  This bar is amazing, quirky and has a really chilled vibe. The bar staff are knowledgeable about their alcohol and happy to whip up your favourite cocktail or invent one for you on the spot. Table service is available or you can stand in the bar area admiring the many bottles of whiskey on show or the bartenders ever growing beards and moustache art! It's such a cool bar and a great place to come with friends or visitors of the city. Reasonable prices for the quality of drinks, service and ambience, easily my favourite bar in Edinburgh and tonight you were looking beautiful.

A great vibe here - I love it. I'm annoying when it comes to cocktails but I do it on purpose ;) I love to ask for something that's not on the menu and like to be vague to see how good the guys are behind the bar...these guys are good and not at all prescriptive. Owned by the same chaps as Bon Vivant on Thistle Street. I didn't have the food here nor did we get the chance to sit at a table (you'll have to book) so we stood at the bar which is what my review is based on. The lighting is low and this place is excellent for a date night. Prices are Edinburgh average - not cheap but not ridiculously expensive either (cocktail ~8). A place I will be taking newbies to the city to.  When you turn off the Royal mile onto Advocate close just keep going and it's on your left hand side (there was a point when I thought we weren't on the right close!).

"We should check out that new place down Advocate's Close!" we said. Little did we know that it was a new regular haunt in the making. Great food and a massive list of whisky (and whiskey) coupled with no-BS serving! Shame about the beer selection, though.  Aside from the odd G&T and White Russian, I'm no big fan of cocktails. When I'm at home, I tend to prefer a straight up single malt if I'm not having beer or wine. When I'm out, I find spirits are almost always way too expensive. So! When I'm out, it tends to be wine with the food or beer at the bar. And the beer selection is a bit on the sad side when compared to the massive list of whisky and the general quality of everything else at Devil's Advocate.  So, that's the "bad" stuff out of the way (not so bad, really, just a matter of choice.) Let's move on to the good stuff!  I fairly regularly get visitors from out of the country, and when I do, I have a small selection of places I tend to recommend for food. Devil's Advocate has now joined First Coast (great and diverse food, decent prices), World's End (reasonable, proto-scottish pub-grub), Grain Store and Blackfriar's (Both high end, for when my parents visit and insist on paying).  I almost always order at least the black haggis bonbons to start with as they are a great and easily shareable haggis/ black pudding treat for people who are curious about haggis but not quite comfortable getting the full haggis, neeps and tatties experience. I really should start considering other options for myself, as the other starters look delicious!  Their burgers, though not the BEST I've ever had, are fabulous! Chunky and full of flavour and come with similarly chunky chips. You might need a fork, not necessarily for eating the burger (though it is one of those "take the top off to eat it" jobs) but for protecting your chips from the thieving fingers of your cohorts. You have been warned.  They change up their menu every now and then, and usually have a Fish of the Day, which is always worth considering. Their vegetarian options are limited but just as worthy of consideration as all the other meals. Last time I went, both my partners in crime opted for the butternut squash risotto after considering that and the oxtail, and it was great! For the record, I've tried their oxtail, and it's QUITE good.  It's been a while since I've had their desserts, I'll make a note to try them next time I go.  The service isn't full of unnecessary pleasantries, nor are they overly polite, but they're (usually) friendly and always effective and have always treated me and mine well. They know what they're doing and they do it well. That isn't to say they're terse or in any way unhelpful, just that I never felt like they were imposing a manufactured "friendly" atmosphere on us, as can happen in a lot of places.  All in all, a great place to go for food and cocktails, just not one I would stay in afterward to drink. And that's fine. They can't be everything to everyone.

Great meal - walked a mile in the rain so we were hoping this place would live up to the great reviews - and it did.  Had the fish and chips and a steak - both were very good.  Had wine, whisky and beer - it was medicinal. Service was good.
Mad expensive, but a very very delicious burger that comes with fries. You'll be full, but your wallet will hurt.

The bar is really cool. They have a massive selection of liquor and can mix just about anything. The bar itself looks awesome and unique. They have several nice beers on tap. When we came in it was already packed with people but the door man let us in for a beverage not the restaurant. The bar area was full with people waiting for the restaurant. Only a short walk from the Royal Mile. If you're debating which bar to visit, I would add this to your list!

Awesome venue, novel and concise gastropub menu including interesting cocktails and craft beer, stellar service, sizeable food portions. It's upscale enough to make for a romantic date night.  The Devil's Advocate is a modern looking buildout in a historic part of Edinburgh. Inside the venue, they've done an excellent job incorporating the original, now exposed, stonework with modern decors like Edison lights and exposed ceilings. There is an upper loft of table seating along with an open floor space near the bar. We sat up in the loft for dinner service. Interior lighting was very dim, which gives it an old tavern-like ambiance.  The menu here is rotating and concise with limited options, which is a good thing. I went for some local beer on draft that tasted fresh and was served in a large mug to keep the tavern feel going. Wife went with a signature cocktail, which tasted great and was served in a chilled, stainless shaker. Wife ordered the whole grilled sea bream, which I tried and it was phenomenal. Bone-in, rock salted, crispy skin. Wow! I ordered the braised lamb shank, which needed some salt but was otherwise braised to perfection served with a unique carb base of al dente chickpeas. Service was phenomenal throughout the evening.    Overall, this was one of our favorite dining experiences in the UK.

Ambiance was outstanding. Seating was very close. Tried to go one night without a reservation, and couldn't get in, so we made a reservation the next night (Hint: Make reservations at night) I heard about the burgers being great, but they must be a daytime item, as there were no burgers on the menu when we went. All of our food was great however, even if i didn't get a burger. Whiskey lovers will enjoy the place, as many many selections. We had grown fond of Ciders here in the UK, and their only cider options were in a can. That's the only down side. Give it a try, and you'll enjoy the meal!
Good cocktail spot, wasn't busy early in the evening. Got the Doha date which was pretty good and def recommend. Didn't get food.

Off the beaten path by the Royal Mile. Great spot to have everything Scotland. We had a flight of scotch as well as the haggis to start. It was excellent! The restaurant is extremely small so make sure you make a reservation. There is seating outside,however, very cold due to it being in a close.

One of the coolest bars ever. Built into the steep side of one of Edinburgh "closes" - narrow slip roads that wend their way through the streets, carrying you from one gothic level to another - the mood here is trendy medieval, if there is such a thing. The bar space is massive and the main dining area is upstairs. When we popped in, we didn't have a reservation, but they told us that we could eat if they could have the table back in an hour. We had a ghost tour in 90 minutes, so this was more than ideal! Despite the time constraints, we didn't feel rushed. The menu is solidly British. Highly recommend any of the fish dishes. The beer selection is lovely as well. Overall, an awesome experience in a very cool setting. Don't miss this place when you're in Edinburgh!

Quite possibly the most hipster place I visited while abroad. We arrived for a late lunch around 2:30 on a Saturday. There was no one to greet us and it seemed pretty chaotic. Bartenders trying to make drinks, food runners racing up and down the stairs, and no host stand in sight. We finally waved down a worker, told him our party size, and he said it would be a 20 minute wait... didn't take our names or anything so we just stood at the bar and ordered drinks. The drink menu is vast and there are a number of creative cocktails available. Our wait ended up being closer to 45 minutes, but whatever.   The upstairs area is pretty small, so I wasn't surprised why we waited to so long to be seated. The service was pretty nonchalant-- no sense of urgency, greeting, or description of the menu. Luckily, we still had our drinks that we ordered from the bar and were able to place our food order right away. Our food took awhile to come out. However, the falafel/lentil appetizer was very unique and tasty. The fish and chips were okay, not the best I had while traveling. My husband's burger was very dry and definitely needed some sauce or cheese to moisten it up. It did have a "tomato salsa" on it that resembled neither tomato nor salsa, but more of a tomato paste. It was weird in a bad way. He was pretty disappointed with how terrible the burger was, considering so many other reviewers raved about the burgers here.   Overall, we had an A-OK time. Would I come back? Maybe for a cocktail. Was it the best hipster place I experience while abroad? No.

Cute little bar and restaurant that was near our hotel. The food was absolutely fantastic! I took off one star because, for the price, we left a tad hungry. I ordered the baked cod in a leek and artichoke sauce. It was so yummy, but definitely needed a side or bread. My husband ordered the lamb, which was a bit more substantial. For dessert we ordered the chocolate mousse. It had orange and almonds in the ingredients, and was something to write home about! And our service was really excellent. It was a Monday so we got in and a table was emptying, but I would suggest reservations.

Delicious food in a great space down one of Edinburghs charming closes. We had both vegeterian and gluten free options and all items were delicious! I would highly recommend making a reservation before you go.

This place is great to have dinner and drink. We had Corn fed chicken and Roaster Heritage beetroot. They were amazing and very delicious. They have great cocktails. The place is a bit crowded and noisy, however great atmosphere. Definitely recommend this place.

No food this time.  I was waiting at the bar and I saw the 'cocktail master' preparing some delicate cocktails. I asked him to provide me with a signature spicy Bloody Mary. He was happy to oblige. I found that he was using a 'celery bitter' and this has now become a real hit with me. I could easily identify the bitter and found it very pleasing.  Service overall has been efficient and welcoming.  I may return for a meal at some point.

Classy place, I recommend it for the atmosphere. The cocktails, however, don't quite work. Either you have to really enjoy whiskey, or something about how they choose to pair it (trying to be inventive but seems to not quite work)- just not my cup of tea. The bar itself has the feel of a NYC loft and nestled in old town on a street most tourists wouldn't think to walk down, I love taking people there to be surprised at what is in there.
Great place, cosy bar with lovely restaurant upstairs.

I'd heard about this place, both on here and on the TWITTAH grapevine. Given I was wandering aimlessly from place to place the other night, I figured this would be a test of my navigational skills.  I never realise where the stairs at the bottom of Advocate's close came on until I walked down them after I left here, but I'm getting ahead of myself now, I suppose. Back to the beginning!  So from the outside, it looks nice and new and stylish and clean, and a big glass door entrance. When you go in, it's very modern and funky, all exposed brick and chrome and black steel... indeed, the first thought I had was that I'd walked into the nightclub from the original Terminator movie, which would have been weird and required time travel too.  There was a huge range of spirits behind the bar, and the staff seemed to be spot on with their recommendations to people; I settled for a bourbon, lemonade, and lime - and it came in at a reasonable 4. For a modern-ish new bar, that's not bad, especially in city centre Edinburgh prices.  It was exceedingly busy when I was in, about 10pm on a Friday evening, and a lot of people did seem to want to be there to be seen to be there, if you know what I mean. Wandering in off the street on my own, I did feel a little out of place, and the lack of hidey holes or wall based drinking places stuck out like a sore thumb to me.  All of those problems wouldn't have mattered if I wasn't Johnny No Friends and was with a huge group, so that's on my head, not the bar's :)  With all that in mind, I would definitely come back here, although I think it would have to be early in the night to try and get a seat!
Great lunch. My friend won't stop talking about the pork belly and beef burger.  Excellent cocktails and service.

Nice place, came in for a beer but they do not have cider on tap, only bottles. The prices are jacked up for tourist. Really good location but be careful with the stairs and drinking, can be deadly. Besides that, luv the decor and the name , will return next time for more food and beer!!

This place is a heavy 4 stars! Never ate the food here, always came for drinks, and the drinks are amazing! Definitely come here! Amazing wooden atmosphere, not too bright and super comfy feel. They make amazing whiskey cocktails!

Fun upscale pub-style restaurant.  The tapas were great, and the ambiance was fun and upbeat.  I am not a scotch drinker, but for those that are, [others in my group are] they have a selection of scotch that cannot be beat.  Go for the fun, food and laughs!   You will be happy you did!

Largest selection of scotches I've seen, but this is the first spot I've stopped. I don't drink scotch but the atmosphere here is great, warm and cozy. I had s lovely glass of wine and cheese platter. The plate was amazing and completed as my dinner. Dinner didn't start until 5 so there was a small menu available and as I understand the items on that menu are not available once the dinner menu starts. I would suggest maybe ordering off the small menu at 445 as appetizer then at 5 dinner... if that could work.

We had attempted to go somewhere else, but it was unfortunately closed. So we wandered aimlessly until we saw tourists photographing one of the many closes in Edinburgh.  The advocate close led us to a restaurant. At first we were slightly confused how to get in, but clearly you just keep going down the stairs and don't attempt the left turn.   They advertised a dinner menu at the door and we decided to lunch here. We were kind of expecting the prices for lunch to be a bit cheaper than the dinner menu. But perhaps that is the norm when dining in Edinburgh and with the proximity of the Royal Mile..  I ordered the Swordfish main that was 14, which I thought was reasonable. The waitress returned to say that there was a problem with the communication with the kitchen. They were all out of Swordfish! This only left about 4 mains options, apart from the grill options (steak etc). Nothing really appealed, but finally I opted for the Crispy Polenta main with poached egg, long stem broccoli and hollandaise sauce 14. My OH had the fish and chips 15.  I just want to say that we were both pleasantly surprised. The Crispy Polenta was a delicious dish. A bit like some sort of brunch dish, but I love brunch so this was ideal. The fish and chips were pretty awesome. The fish tasted really fresh and not that horrible oily-fatty way!  So glad we discovered this little wonder.

The food is really, really delicious. It's best to make a reservation because the tables are extremely limited. The menu is limited but the the selections are diverse and interesting. Vegetables are extremely fresh. Joe had grilled polenta with vegetables and poached egg. I had an extremely well prepared steak that was medium rare. Not medium and not rare. The place was very busy with lots of people coming to gather at the bar and at the bar tables around the outside of the restaurant. Seems very popular in the area. Cocktails are excellent, very inventive and tasty. Really fun place to hangout

I've been twice, intending dinner both times, but foolishly the first time failing to book in advance.   Apple maps actually functioned here for once, and led us straight to the little alley that I'm not surprised people miss, though I was slightly alarmed navigating the steep steps in early december, which unfortunately, are unavoidable. The tucked away alley is apparently always quiet, but the devil's advocate is always packed, dimly lit, cosy, small, and i'd even push to say ambience over atmosphere (micky flanagan jokes, and all that) you can mostly drink standing, there are a few tables you can sit at for bevies, but they're mostly for eating.   As a whisky drinker, she slurs, you've got a pretty damn good choice here, and not just scotch either. These guys now how to present a pretty bar but there are lists too so you don;t have to annoy every human tutting behind you who knows exactly what cocktail they want. The bar staff know their shizzle, they obviously know how to help tourists with no whisky experience under their belts at all. Again, be wary of the peaty ingredients if you aren't fan of smoke, expect florals and botanicals too, nice gin list as well, which if you ask me, is always worth noting. The platters are great sharers and assembled nicely, I was a big fan of the haggis bon bons, and my meat was cooked to perfection.  I do plan to visit again at some point, mostly because I flipping love edinburgh.

We couldn't walk past the Devil's Advocate simply because of the name. This place is a must if you are visiting Scotland as it feels like a traditional pub.  We went in for drinks - mainly to enjoy different types of Scottish Whiskey. We were not disappointed. The bartender was well informed and provided us each with several drinks we enjoyed thoroughly.  When we visited it was on the quieter side which made it a nice place to sit and have a drink and visit with friends. It's location is also very walkable from different public transportation sites and the downtown area.  We really enjoyed speaking with the staff. This is one of the best parts of the Devil's Advocate. The knowledgeable and friendly staff. We will definitely be back.

I ordered the crispy polenta with mushrooms, spinach, figs, and hazelnuts and it was so good. My husband ordered the ribeye with chips and he enjoyed his too. The star may have been the salted caramel chocolate mousse, we shared it and it was delicious. Great place.

If a hipster bar and a speakeasy had a baby, this place might be it   I just had to come here for the number one rated spot in Edinburgh. I wasn't super hungry so I stopped in for an appetizer and some wine after a day tour. The place is hidden down an alley, which gives it unique character already.   I love the atmosphere and decor. I sat in a small booth off from the bar. The lighting is dark, the waiters are as hipster as they come and super friendly!  I ordered the soup, which was a courgette and fennel soup - it was divine!   I would definitely come back here next time I'm in town. Such a cool spot!

A fun walk down to a very stylish space for upscale clientele. Very friendly, kind staff made us feel very welcome. Had the Cullen Skink, Smoked Fish Board, and the  Grilled Ribeye with chips (fabulous chips). All very good. I took the recommended whiskey (excellent) and nursed it through out the meal (I'm a lightweight). We made our reservation on Thursday before noon for 5pm Friday evening. No waiting!

We had gotten a recco for this place from a bartender in London and happened to stumble upon it one day.  Thought we'd pop in for a dram and ended up staying a few hours.  The whisky list is impressive as expected but the service was fantastic.  We chatted with one of the bartenders who I would guess is also the manager and he was incredibly enthusiastic about whisky.  Very generous with advise and tasting.  We ended up ordering the scallops and serrano and were very pleased with the quality of the scallop dish.  It was delicious.  Can't really mess up serrano but the bread they served with it was fresh and the olive oil very good.  Can't wait to go back.

Eh wow. How friggin gorgeo is this place.  First of all, if you're going from the high road, you have to step through one of those little laneways that seems like it's going nowhere but turns out to be like a portal into a whole other old Edinburgh world. Also the laneway is called Advocate's Close which I thought was kinda cool. (Laneways and passageways and doors into streets - jeez Edinburgh you're mad covert)  Anyway. Back to the Devil's Advocate. The name is quite apt as it's a tempting dark spot with lots of naked flames around (gorgeous candles. If hell is like this, sign me up tbh). It's got that perfect mix of old and new - contemporary finishes over old, old stone. It envelopes you as soon as you go in and makes it rather difficult to leave.   They have an incredible selection of whiskeys. And knowledgeable and sound bar staff who can explain and recommend each and every one to you.  I didn't get to try the food but I bet it's great.   It's all bloody great. Go. You just might not ever leave...
Nice ambience with candle light ,stone and wood . Friendly service and the best pork chop I've ever eaten in my life!

It's a 3 start restaurant.   Very hipster posh, upmarket & slightly on the snobby side. Like what is this pretend wanna be an LA bistro?   The food was average at best. However The ambience is nice and location is close to city center.   The waiting staff had a bit of an attitude if I'm honest. But I was hoping the food would wow me. But it was fairly bland.   But good for drunk people I guess ;)

Colour me impressed! I'd heard nothing but good things about the Devil's Advocate but hadn't had the chance to try it out yet (I was gutted to miss Yelp Edinburgh's 3rd Birthday Bash here!), but then my mum was through and I met her for a drink before she got the train home. And where better located for a pre-Waverley-pick-me-up than DA?  You'd never know it was here if you started wandering up Advocate's Close from Cockburn Street, but then you turn the corner and voila! The space inside is lovely, I can only assume that it's been used as storage space for years, as a lot of the lower buildings of the closes have, and it still retains a bare feeling inside, with exposed walls complimented by warm woods and metals.  Alas as it was Burn's Night they were not serving food (other than the special Burn's menu for those who'd already booked), so no light bites for us, just drinks. The cocktail menu caught our eyes straight away - there are none of your traditional drinks on it (though I assume they'd make you a margarita if you asked for one), but everything sounds delicious and is helpfully sorted into sections like 'Sippers' with subsections of 'Short', 'Long' and 'Up'. We both plumped for the Whiskey Swizzle, which was delicious. I cannot remember what was in it (other than a rye whiskey), but it was fragrant, refreshing and had a good amount of kick to it.  We did only stay for one drink, but I'll definitely be back and my mum is already talking of bringing my dad here next time they're through. If this is where the Devil's legal representative drinks, then this law grad has gone to the dark side.

I went here with friends for drinks and the atmosphere is lovely. It's really intimate feeling and cozy. It really plays off the history of old town with the stone walls and candles.  The beers there are great. Not the type you have at every bar. The cocktails are great. It's a bit pricey so a good place to go for a classy catch up or a relaxed yet snazzy date.

Just popped in for a drink & got a wee table upstairs on the mezzanine level. Service was prompt. Nice vibe but does get very noisy when full due to the low ceiling.  Great selection of cocktails. I had the "pick a pear" one & it was lovely.  Looking forward to working my way through the rest of the menu :-)

Is it the scotch here in Edinburgh or am I just lucky? I keep writing 5 star reviews and I promise I am sober. Devils advocate is no exception! Great cocktails and really tasty food! They do know they are good, but are not too cocky... just wish I made reservations cause they are always full!
This place was amazing..... The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was the time it took to get our cocktails. Amazing place for tourists to visit****

The Devil's on my shoulder, and I've got his back!  It gets great reviews because it is consistently great. Some people might think it is a bit hipster, but I don't agree with that. Yeah they have beards tattoos and wear braces, but wait and just look at the clientele, it's popular with everyone - even that American tourist with the NY giants jacket on.  This place is cool, not effortlessly as a lot of thought has gone into it, but they certainly aren't trying too hard either. Listen if you like traditional, then this probably isn't your spot, and if you like uber modern, the same goes - try the royal mile or George Street respectively.   Great drinks selection, from cracking wines to an on trend beer range. The best part of the drinks list are their cocktails, it's a well thought out list perfectly executed every time. I like a bit of the speakeasy vibe, old school cocktails focused more on the base spirit and minus the gimmicks. Great structure to the food menu also makes this a very hard bar to move on from.

Delicious food, amazing drinks, and beautiful atmosphere. The venison was to die for but the lamb dish was a little lacking. Overall though, really enjoyed the food and the mixed cocktails. OUr waitress seemed a little annoyed to be waiting on us and the place is pretty busy.

We came in forty minutes before close one night. I found us a table while my husband went to the bar to get us drinks. We didn't see a waitress at the time and didn't want to keep them open any later than they had to be, although they were pretty full.
